### 4.3.11 Internal Comment Thread (Workspace-Scoped, Buyer-Only)

Container for Internal Comment Post entities. Anchored to a Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Scenario, or Selection Report draft. Buyer-side only — invisible to seller-console users, invisible to vendors via any API or export. Modeled on §18.3.1 Q&A Thread schema, with three differences: (a) no `vendor_id` or author-masking primitives because vendors never see threads; (b) `attached_to` polymorphism broadens beyond Requirement; (c) `status` adds `resolved` with resolver audit fields.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | For residency and tenant isolation |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | FK → Workspace | All threads hang off a Workspace (even when attached_to=`use_case` or deeper) |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | Buyer console only; seller console has no equivalent |
| `attached_to_type` | Enum | `workspace` \| `use_case` \| `requirement` \| `response` \| `scenario` \| `selection_report_draft` | Polymorphic anchor; see Appendix J |
| `attached_to_id` | UUID | Matches `attached_to_type` FK target | Validated on write |
| `title` | String | 0–100 chars | Auto-derived from first 80 chars of first post if blank |
| `status` | Enum | `open` \| `resolved` \| `archived` | See Appendix J; state machine in Appendix L |
| `visibility_scope` | Enum | `buyer_workspace_members` \| `buyer_team_leads` \| `private_to_author_plus_mentioned` | See Appendix J |
| `subscribed_user_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | FKs → User, ≤ 200 entries | Auto-subscribe: author + @-mentioned users; opt-out available |
| `post_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized for listing performance; updated transactionally with Post writes |
| `last_post_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Used by Unread Marker math; null on empty draft thread |
| `resolved_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on transition to `resolved` |
| `resolved_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | Who marked resolved |
| `resolution_note` | String | 0–500 chars | Optional closing comment from resolver |
| `plan_quota_counted` | Boolean | Default: true | False only for system-generated threads exempt from §5.11 caps |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Thread author |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last mutator |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; when set, child Posts and Mentions inherit soft-delete |

**Indexes:**

- `(workspace_id, status, last_post_at DESC)` — workspace-level thread listing, sorted by activity.
- `(attached_to_type, attached_to_id, status)` — per-anchor thread lookup (open threads on a Requirement).
- `(workspace_id, created_at DESC)` — chronological listing.
- `(org_id, created_at DESC)` — org-scoped volume analytics and plan-quota counting.

**Scope Isolation:** Workspace-scoped, buyer console only. Never exposed via seller console APIs. The seller console's API authorization layer (§32) must return 404 — not 403 — if a seller-console token attempts to read any Internal Comment Thread, Post, or Mention; 403 would leak thread existence. Add to Appendix I error catalog: `internal_comment_cross_console_access` maps to HTTP 404.

**Relationships:** One-to-many with Internal Comment Post (via `thread_id`). One-to-many with Internal Comment Mention (via `thread_id`). Parent anchors validated: `attached_to_type=workspace` ⇒ `attached_to_id = workspace_id`; `attached_to_type=use_case` ⇒ `attached_to_id` FK → Use Case in same Workspace; etc.

**Authoring Intent:** Internal Comments are the buyer's private collaboration surface for discussion that must never reach vendors. Placing the entity in the data model with strict console enforcement (not merely a UI boundary) closes the leakage risk flagged in §7.2 Cross-Console Firewall. The polymorphic anchor supports the Summary C.119 requirement that threads attach to Workspaces, Use Cases, and Requirements; Response, Scenario, and Selection Report anchors are authored extensions covering realistic buyer workflows (discussing a specific vendor response during Phase 10, debating a scenario parameter, redlining a report narrative before export) and are flagged in RECONCILIATION.md under Authored Extensions.

### 4.3.12 Internal Comment Post (Workspace-Scoped, Buyer-Only)

Individual post within an Internal Comment Thread. Follows §18.3.1 post schema with normalized mentions (per Gap 3.6 pattern).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `thread_id` | UUID | FK → Internal Comment Thread | Parent thread |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Denormalized from thread for residency queries |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | FK → Workspace | Denormalized from thread for listing indexes |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | Seller console never reads |
| `author_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Post author |
| `author_role_snapshot` | Enum | `workspace_owner` \| `workspace_admin` \| `use_case_lead` \| `reviewer` \| `guest_full_participant` \| `guest_contributor` \| `guest_scorer` | Frozen at post time; survives later role changes for audit |
| `body` | String | 0–5000 chars (per §39) | Markdown; sanitized server-side against XSS before render |
| `attachment_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | FKs → Attachment, ≤ 10 files (per §39) | Virus-scanned per §18.5.2 |
| `parent_post_id` | UUID | FK → Internal Comment Post, nullable | Reply-to reference; null for top-level posts |
| `edited_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on first edit; multiple edits overwrite |
| `edit_locked_at` | Timestamp | Immutable, = `created_at + 15 min` | Server-enforced edit window per §18.5.1 |
| `deleted_placeholder` | Boolean | Default: false | True when author self-deletes within window; body replaced by "Deleted by author" on read |
| `moderated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | Workspace Owner admin-override per §18.5.1 |
| `moderated_reason` | String | 0–500 chars, nullable | Required when `moderated_by` is set |
| `mention_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized; matches COUNT of Mention entities for this post |
| `attachment_total_bytes` | BigInt | ≥ 0, ≤ 500 MB (per §39) | Sum across attachments; enforced on write |
| `client_submit_source` | Enum | `web` \| `mobile_web` \| `ios_app` \| `android_app` \| `api` | For analytics |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; frozen when `deleted_placeholder = true` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID, = `author_id` | Invariant enforced at API layer |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last mutator (author or moderator) |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Hard soft-delete (not placeholder); only admins can set beyond edit window |

**Indexes:**

- `(thread_id, created_at ASC)` — chronological post render within thread.
- `(author_id, created_at DESC)` — "my posts" and moderation review.
- `(workspace_id, created_at DESC)` — workspace-level audit and analytics.
- `(thread_id, parent_post_id, created_at ASC)` — threaded reply rendering.
- `(moderated_by, created_at DESC)` — moderator activity audit.

**Scope Isolation:** Inherits workspace + console scope from parent thread. Cross-console read returns HTTP 404 (see 4.3.11 scope rules).

**Relationships:** Belongs to Internal Comment Thread (`thread_id`). One-to-many with Internal Comment Mention (`post_id`). May self-reference via `parent_post_id` for reply semantics. Attachments referenced via `attachment_ids` (Attachment entity defined in §4.6, unchanged).

**Authoring Intent:** Extracting Post as a first-class entity (rather than nesting posts inside Thread JSON, as §18.3.1 does for Q&A Threads) follows the Gap 3.6 normalization pattern and is required to support the §18.6 full-text-search index, the §29.1 mention notification fan-out, and per-post audit (§22). Inline nesting would prevent index-level mention queries and make the 5000-char × unlimited-posts cap explode the parent row. Reconciliation log flags this as a divergence from §18.3.1 precedent and recommends that Q&A Thread posts be similarly normalized in a future integration phase.

### 4.3.13 Internal Comment Mention (Workspace-Scoped, Buyer-Only)

Normalized @-mention record. One row per mentioned user per post. Drives notification fan-out (§29) and the `has_unread_mention` flag on Unread Marker (§4.3.15).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `post_id` | UUID | FK → Internal Comment Post | Source post |
| `thread_id` | UUID | FK → Internal Comment Thread | Denormalized for fast per-user inbox queries |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | FK → Workspace | Denormalized for scope filtering |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Denormalized for residency |
| `author_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Who authored the mentioning post |
| `mentioned_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Mention target; must be a Workspace Member |
| `mention_kind` | Enum | `user` \| `team` \| `role` | See Appendix J; `team` expands to each member at write; `role` expands to all users holding that role in the Workspace at write |
| `expanded_from_team_id` | UUID | FK → Team, nullable | Set if `mention_kind=team` at expansion time |
| `expanded_from_role` | Enum | Workspace Role enum, nullable | Set if `mention_kind=role` at expansion time |
| `notified_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when notification successfully dispatched to Loops/in-app channels |
| `dismissed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when mentioned user dismisses in-app notification |
| `read_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when mentioned user opens the post |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; cascades from Post soft-delete |

**Indexes:**

- `(mentioned_user_id, read_at, created_at DESC)` — per-user unread mentions feed.
- `(post_id)` — enumerate mentions on a post for rendering.
- `(thread_id, mentioned_user_id)` — "am I mentioned in this thread?" O(1) lookup for Unread Marker computation.
- `(workspace_id, created_at DESC)` — workspace-level mention analytics.

**Scope Isolation:** Mentions expanded from team/role at write time are frozen — subsequent team-roster changes do not retroactively notify new members, per the principle of author-intent preservation.

**Relationships:** Belongs to Internal Comment Post (`post_id`). References User (`mentioned_user_id`), Team (`expanded_from_team_id`), and Workspace (`workspace_id`). Drives Unread Marker `has_unread_mention` flag updates (see §4.3.15 Indexes note).

**Authoring Intent:** Normalizing mentions out of the post body addresses three gaps: (a) @-mention parsing at read time (which §18.3.1 implies) fails on edited or moderated posts because the Markdown string may no longer contain the original mention; (b) team/role expansions must be frozen at mention time for audit; (c) per-user inbox queries would otherwise require a full-text scan. This entity is an authored extension beyond Summary C.119 and is flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

### 4.3.14 Presence Record (Session-Scoped, Ephemeral, Cross-Console)

Convex Presence-backed live-cursor and collaboration state. **Not persisted to the primary data store.** Lives in Convex's session-scoped memory with TTL-based eviction. Modeled here for schema completeness and for DSAR/retention clarity — Presence is explicitly outside DSAR export because it is transient (§40.4 confirms "Real-time presence indicators" are excluded from round-trip fidelity).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `session_id` | UUID | Primary key (Convex session) | Generated by Convex on client connect |
| `user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | The acting user |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | For cross-console firewall |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` \| `seller` | Which console the session is operating in; a single user may have simultaneous sessions in both consoles (distinct `session_id`s), but a single session is console-locked |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable; FK → Workspace (if console=buyer) | Current buyer workspace; null when user is outside workspace routes |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable; FK → Bid Workspace (if console=seller) | Current seller bid workspace; null outside bid routes; mutually exclusive with `workspace_id` enforced by `console` |
| `current_route` | String | Max 500 chars | Canonical route path, e.g. `/w/{workspace_id}/requirements/{requirement_id}` |
| `cursor_position` | JSON | Max 500 chars; `{x: int, y: int, element_ref: uuid \| null}`, nullable | Null when not in a shared doc |
| `viewport_element_ref` | UUID | Nullable | Entity currently in viewport, used for off-screen presence indicators (C.112) |
| `color_token` | Enum | `hue_1`…`hue_8` | Deterministically assigned per session per C.112; 8-color palette wraps after 8 concurrent sessions |
| `last_heartbeat_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated, UTC | Client heartbeat every 5 seconds |
| `status` | Enum | `active` \| `idle` \| `disconnected` | `idle` after 10s without heartbeat; `disconnected` after 30s; evicted after 60s |
| `typing_in_entity_ref` | UUID | Nullable | Which entity the user is currently typing into; clears 3s after last keystroke |
| `client_timezone` | String | IANA timezone, max 64 chars | For display of live-cursor tooltips in viewer's local time |
| `client_device_class` | Enum | `desktop_web` \| `mobile_web` \| `ios_app` \| `android_app` | For degraded-presence rendering on mobile |
| `connected_at` | Timestamp | Immutable, UTC | Session start |

**Indexes (Convex reactive queries):**

- `(org_id, workspace_id, status)` — renders "who is in this workspace now" (buyer).
- `(org_id, bid_workspace_id, status)` — same for seller side.
- `(org_id, viewport_element_ref, status)` — per-entity viewer indicator.
- `(user_id, console)` — enforce one-presence-record-per-console-per-user.
- `last_heartbeat_at` — TTL eviction sweep.

**Scope Isolation:** Session-scoped and Convex-managed; **never crosses the Dual-Console Firewall** (§7.2) — a buyer-console session is invisible to seller-console sessions for the same Org. For cross-tenant (different Org) sessions, Presence is likewise invisible — a Workspace Guest from Org B sees Org B teammates only; Org A internal users are not surfaced. Enforced by the `(org_id, workspace_id)` index scope.

**Cross-Org Guest Presence:** When a guest from Org B is a Workspace Member of an Org A workspace, the Presence Record carries `org_id = B` (the authenticating Org — auth anchor) with `workspace_id = <Org A workspace>`. Visibility is computed by the consuming query: users rendering presence for Workspace Owner/Admin of the hosting Org A see all Presence Records matching that `workspace_id`, regardless of `org_id`. Guest users see only Presence Records with matching `workspace_id` AND matching `org_id` (their own Org). This avoids leaking Org A teammate presence to Org B guests.

**Retention:** Ephemeral. Never written to cold storage. Evicted 60 seconds after last heartbeat, or immediately on explicit disconnect. **Excluded from JSON export** (§40), **excluded from DSAR exports** (§6.8, §45.1 — data is transient), **excluded from backup snapshots**. Listed as "lost in round-trip" in §40.4. No retention row needed in §40.2.

**Relationships:** References User, Organization, Workspace, Bid Workspace. Consumed by Unread Marker for determining "last seen" positions but never FK'd to — Unread uses `last_read_at` timestamps independently.

**Authoring Intent:** Formalizing Presence as a schema entity (even though Convex manages it) answers three specification gaps: (a) clarifies that Presence is **not** subject to DSAR export (avoids a QA / privacy review stalemate); (b) defines `color_token` collision behavior for >8 concurrent sessions (wrap); (c) enforces the buyer↔seller firewall at the Presence layer, which the Summary C.120 implies but does not specify. Authored beyond Summary C.120 baseline; flagged in RECONCILIATION.md under Authored Extensions.

### 4.3.15 Unread Marker (Per-User-Per-Thread, Cross-Console)

Per-user-per-thread unread-count tracker. Powers badge counts across Internal Comments, Q&A Threads, and Inbox (§29.1). One marker per (user, thread_type, thread_id) tuple.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | The viewer |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | For residency/tenant queries |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` \| `seller` | The console surface this marker belongs to |
| `thread_type` | Enum | `internal_comment_thread` \| `qa_thread` \| `inbox_item_group` | See Appendix J |
| `thread_id` | UUID | Matches `thread_type` FK target | Polymorphic; validated on write |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable; FK → Workspace or Bid Workspace per `console` | Denormalized for inbox/dashboard filters |
| `last_read_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | User's last visit to this thread; null if user has never opened it |
| `last_read_post_id` | UUID | Nullable | Last post marked read (authoritative over `last_read_at` if both present) |
| `unread_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Cached count of posts with `created_at > last_read_at`; recomputed on post-insert via Convex subscription |
| `has_unread_mention` | Boolean | Default: false | True if any unread post has a Mention targeting this user |
| `muted_until` | Timestamp | Nullable | User-set mute horizon; while set, `has_unread_mention` still tracks but does not generate notifications |
| `suppressed_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `muted`, `left_workspace`, `archived_thread` | Why unread_count is not incrementing |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; set on first time user accesses thread context |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete when user leaves workspace or thread is hard-deleted |

**Indexes:**

- `(user_id, thread_type, thread_id)` UNIQUE — idempotent upsert on post-create.
- `(user_id, console, has_unread_mention, updated_at DESC)` — global mention badge.
- `(user_id, console, thread_type, unread_count DESC)` — per-surface inbox.
- `(workspace_id, user_id)` — workspace-level dashboard unread summaries.
- `(thread_id, thread_type)` — fan-out on thread mutation (update all markers).

**Scope Isolation:** Per-user; `console` enum separates buyer- and seller-side marker sets. A user operating in both consoles has independent marker sets that do not leak across the Dual-Console Firewall.

**Retention:** Purged when (a) parent thread is hard-deleted + 30 days, (b) user loses Workspace Membership + 30 days (`suppressed_reason=left_workspace`), or (c) Organization deleted per §40.2 (90-day purge). Ties to §40.2; update retention row below.

**Relationships:** Polymorphic pointer to Internal Comment Thread, Q&A Thread (§18.3.1), or Inbox Item Group (§29). References User, Organization, Workspace.

**Authoring Intent:** Centralizing unread state in a single entity (rather than computing on-the-fly across three surfaces) is required by Convex's reactive-query performance envelope: recomputing unread counts across Comments + Q&A + Inbox per paint cycle exceeds the Convex function-execution budget for Orgs with >1,000 threads. The polymorphic `thread_type` field avoids three parallel marker tables.

**`has_unread_mention` Derivation Per Thread Type:**

- `internal_comment_thread` — set by Internal Comment Mention.post_id ∈ posts with `created_at > last_read_at` AND `mentioned_user_id = user_id`.
- `qa_thread` — §18.3.1 does not normalize Q&A mentions. The Unread Marker derives this flag at Q&A post-write time via Markdown @-mention parsing of the post body. The parse result is written to a denormalized `qa_post_mentions` index (authored extension; flagged in RECONCILIATION.md — a future phase should normalize Q&A Thread posts to match Internal Comment Post + Mention separation).
- `inbox_item_group` — set when any Inbox item in the group carries `direct_mention = true` per §29.1 Inbox Feed Schema.

Centralizing the flag regardless of source keeps the UI contract identical across surfaces, but the underlying derivation is surface-specific.

### 4.3.16 Buyer Referral (Org-Scoped, Buyer-Only)

M16 Buyer Referral Credit entity. Tracks referrer → referee relationship, credit issuance, fraud signals, and reconciliation state per Summary C.74.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `referrer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | The referring buyer Org |
| `referrer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Individual who initiated referral; must hold `org_owner`, `org_admin`, or `billing_admin` role at referral time |
| `referee_email` | String | Valid email, max 320 chars | Target email; lowercased before storage |
| `referee_email_domain` | String | Max 253 chars, lowercased | Denormalized for same-domain detection; indexed |
| `referee_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID, nullable | Set when referee signs up and Org is provisioned |
| `referral_code` | String | 10 chars, URL-safe Base32, unique | Used in invite URLs and magic-link redemption |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `referral_status` | State machine in Appendix L |
| `credit_value_usd` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0, ≤ 2000 | Referrer credit; plan-dependent; Scale=$100, Enterprise=$200 at time of first integration, configurable per C.97 |
| `credit_issued_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When credit posted to referrer's wallet |
| `credit_expires_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | = `credit_issued_at + 365 days` |
| `credit_redeemed_usd` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0, ≤ `credit_value_usd` | Running total applied to invoices |
| `credit_forfeited_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `referral_forfeit_reason`, nullable | Reason credit was withheld or reversed |
| `min_activity_reached_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when referee hits the activation threshold (default: referee Org has completed ≥1 workspace through Phase 9 and has ≥3 paid users; configurable in Ops Console) |
| `activity_threshold_policy_version` | String | Max 50 chars | Version stamp of activity threshold at referral creation; ensures retroactive policy changes don't retroactively disqualify |
| `fraud_signal_flags` | Array\[Enum\] | See Appendix J `referral_fraud_signal` | Set by Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100); multiple flags allowed |
| `same_domain_suppressed` | Boolean | Default: false | True when `referrer_email_domain` = `referee_email_domain` and Ops has not overridden |
| `payment_method_overlap_detected` | Boolean | Default: false | True when Stripe fingerprint of referee payment method matches referrer's |
| `ip_range_overlap_detected` | Boolean | Default: false | True when signup IP /24 matches referrer's recent login IPs within 30 days |
| `velocity_flag` | Boolean | Default: false | True when referrer has ≥10 referrals in a 7-day rolling window (threshold configurable) |
| `ops_override_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | Ops admin who overrode a fraud block |
| `ops_override_note` | String | 0–500 chars, nullable | Required when `ops_override_user_id` is set |
| `campaign_id` | String | Max 100 chars, nullable | A/B attribution tag |
| `invited_via_channel` | Enum | See Appendix J `referral_invite_channel` | Channel used to issue referral |
| `referee_opt_out_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Global Vendor Opt-Out Registry (C.123) or referee explicit decline |
| `stripe_credit_note_ids` | Array\[String\] | Stripe Credit Note IDs, ≤ 50 | For financial reconciliation; appended on each redemption |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID, = `referrer_user_id` | Invariant enforced at API layer |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last mutator (Ops override or system) |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; **never used** for active referrals pending reconciliation; Ops-only |

**Indexes:**

- `(referrer_org_id, status, created_at DESC)` — referrer dashboard.
- `(referee_email_domain, status)` — same-domain detection fan-out.
- `(referral_code)` UNIQUE — magic-link redemption.
- `(referee_org_id, status)` — enforce "one redeemable credit per referee Org" rule.
- `(referrer_org_id, created_at DESC)` — 7-day velocity-spike detection window.
- `(credit_expires_at, status)` — nightly expiry sweep.

**Scope Isolation:** Org-scoped on `referrer_org_id`. Buyer-only; sellers never initiate Buyer Referrals (sellers have a separate Ghost-Bid Importer M15 pathway). The `referee_email` and `referee_email_domain` are Org-readable by the referrer's Org Owner, Org Admin, Billing Admin, and Ops; not readable by anyone at the referee Org to preserve anonymity until signup (per §7.3 PII handling).

**Retention:** Retained indefinitely for financial audit and reconciliation with Stripe Credit Notes, per Sarbanes-Oxley–aligned financial record retention (§40.2 updated row below). DSAR right-to-erasure pathway: `referee_email` pseudonymized (irreversible hash), `referrer_user_id` pseudonymized, `fraud_signal_flags` retained in aggregate form. Core financial fields (`credit_value_usd`, `credit_redeemed_usd`, `stripe_credit_note_ids`) are retained unaltered per Stripe audit requirements and §45.1 financial-record exemption. Retention window: Org-life + 7 years.

**Relationships:** References Organization (`referrer_org_id`, `referee_org_id`), User (`referrer_user_id`, `ops_override_user_id`). Cross-referenced by Usage Event (`event_category=referral`). Drives Stripe Credit Note issuance per Appendix H.

**Authoring Intent:** Summary C.74 establishes the M16 mechanism but does not specify the entity shape. The field set supports the three fraud-control axes named in C.74 (same-domain, payment-method overlap, minimum-activity gating), extended to add IP-range overlap and velocity-spike flags per §3.5 anti-spam framework. `activity_threshold_policy_version` is an authored extension that prevents retroactive disqualification when Ops adjusts the activation threshold — a known failure mode on referral systems without version stamping. `stripe_credit_note_ids` is mandatory for the Appendix H billing model reconciliation. All authored extensions flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

**Referee Exclusivity Rule:** Only one Buyer Referral row per `referee_email` (case-insensitive) may be in status `credit_issued`, `credit_redeemed`, or `credit_expired` at a time. At the `activated → credit_issued` transition, the system MUST query for any other row with the same `referee_email` already in one of those states; if found, the new referral transitions to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = insufficient_activity` (semantic: another referrer already claimed this referee). First-to-activate wins. This rule is enforced at application layer because DB unique constraints on `referee_email` would prevent multiple `pending` rows from coexisting (which is legitimate — a referee can be referred by multiple orgs concurrently; only the first to complete activation gets credit).

**Failure Modes Addressed:**

- **Double-credit on duplicate referrals.** Resolved by Referee Exclusivity Rule above.
- **Payment-method fraud (referrer and referee share card).** Detected via Stripe PaymentMethod fingerprint comparison on referee's first invoice; sets `payment_method_overlap_detected` and transitions status to `flagged_fraud`.
- **Sybil attack (single actor creating referrer → referee chain).** Detected via `same_ip_range` + `bootstrapping_pattern` co-occurrence; SIM triggers.

### 4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant (Org-Scoped, Buyer-Originated, Seller-Redeemed)

M17 entity that tracks the lifecycle of a single Pro Trial Seat from issuance (buyer-side) through redemption (seller-side) to outcome (converted / auto-downgraded / declined). Complements §34.13 procedural text with the persistent record.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `grant_code` | String | 16 chars, URL-safe Base32, unique | Invite URL token |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | Granting buyer |
| `buyer_billing_cycle_month` | Date | First day of buyer's billing cycle (UTC) | Pool accounting bucket tied to the buyer's Stripe billing anniversary, **not** the calendar month. A buyer with anniversary on the 15th has cycles running 15th→14th; this field stores the cycle start date. |
| `buyer_plan_tier_at_grant` | Enum | `scale` \| `enterprise` | Frozen at grant time; Ops cannot retroactively re-tier |
| `buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of buyer's pool balance at issuance for audit |
| `issuer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Must hold Buyer Admin, Workspace Owner, or Billing Admin role per §5.3 |
| `issuing_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Workspace ID, nullable | If grant issued from workspace invite context |
| `issuing_target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | Target Account ID, nullable | If grant tied to a vendor invite |
| `vendor_email` | String | Valid email, max 320 chars, lowercased | Invitee email |
| `vendor_email_domain` | String | Max 253 chars, lowercased | Denormalized for fraud checks |
| `vendor_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID, nullable | Set when vendor signs up |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `trial_seat_status` | State machine in Appendix L |
| `provisioned_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When Seller Starter entitlements activated on vendor Org |
| `trial_starts_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | = `provisioned_at` |
| `trial_expires_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | = `trial_starts_at + 30 days` |
| `rejection_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `trial_seat_rejection_reason`, nullable | Populated on vendor decline or system block |
| `outcome` | Enum | See Appendix J `trial_seat_outcome`, nullable | Terminal outcome; set at day 31 or explicit action |
| `converted_to_plan` | Enum | `seller_starter` \| `seller_growth` \| `seller_scale` \| `seller_enterprise`, nullable | Plan vendor converted to |
| `converted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor converted |
| `ai_value_consumed_usd` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0 | Running total of AI value-dollars during trial (metered to vendor's AI budget per §34.13.1) |
| `same_buyer_365d_block_triggered` | Boolean | Default: false | True if system rejected the grant because vendor received a grant from this buyer in prior 365 days |
| `already_paid_block_triggered` | Boolean | Default: false | True if vendor Org was on a paid seller plan at grant time |
| `revoked_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | Set only if buyer revokes before provisioning |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Same |
| `audit_event_grant_id` | UUID (FK) | Audit Event ID | `pro_trial_seat_granted` audit row |
| `audit_event_outcome_id` | UUID (FK) | Audit Event ID, nullable | `pro_trial_seat_converted` / `_expired` / `_rejected` / `_revoked` row |
| `stripe_meter_event_ids` | Array\[String\] | ≤ 10 | `sourcera_pro_trial_grant`, `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion`, `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` per §34.13.6 |
| `anti_spam_hold_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `trial_seat_rejection_reason` | Populated by Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID, = `issuer_user_id` | Invariant |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last mutator |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete (Ops only) |

**Indexes:**

- `(buyer_org_id, buyer_billing_cycle_month, status)` — per-month pool accounting (§34.13.2).
- `(vendor_email_domain, status)` — abuse correlation.
- `(vendor_org_id, created_at DESC)` — enforce "one grant per buyer per 365 days" rule (`same_buyer_365d_block_triggered` lookup).
- `(trial_expires_at, status)` — nightly auto-downgrade sweep on day 31.
- `(grant_code)` UNIQUE — redemption lookup.
- `(issuer_user_id, created_at DESC)` — individual issuer activity for abuse review.

**Scope Isolation:** Org-scoped on both sides. Buyer's Org reads only the issuer-side columns (plus outcome); vendor's Org reads only the redemption-side columns (plus conversion outcome). The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is enforced at the API layer: a single `GET /v1/pro-trial-seats/{id}` endpoint returns different projections depending on the requesting console's org_id relative to `buyer_org_id` and `vendor_org_id`. A third-party Org MUST get HTTP 404.

**Retention:** Retained for Org-life + 7 years per financial audit (Stripe meter event reconciliation). DSAR pathway: `vendor_email`, `issuer_user_id`, and `vendor_email_domain` pseudonymized on request while preserving aggregate conversion metrics. New §40.2 row required (see below).

**Relationships:** References Organization (`buyer_org_id`, `vendor_org_id`), Workspace (`issuing_workspace_id`), Target Account (`issuing_target_account_id`), User (`issuer_user_id`, `revoked_by_user_id`), Audit Event (`audit_event_grant_id`, `audit_event_outcome_id`). Drives Stripe meter events (§34.13.6) and Usage Events (`event_category=trial_seat`).

**Authoring Intent:** §34.13 defines the mechanic but does not materialize the persistent entity needed to enforce the "one grant per buyer per 365 days" rule, to reconcile Stripe meter events, or to support the internal conversion-rate dashboard named in §34.13.6. This entity is the authoritative ledger. `buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant` is an authored extension that preserves audit integrity when Ops retroactively changes plan allocations. The dual-projection read rule is an authored extension that resolves the ambiguity in §34.13 about vendor-side visibility of grant metadata.

**Failure Modes Addressed:**

- **Buyer downgrades mid-trial (Scale → Growth).** Grants in status `in_trial`, `provisioned`, or `invite_sent` at downgrade time are **grandfathered** through their original outcome (the trial continues to day 31 with auto-downgrade as normal). Grants in status `issued` (not yet sent) are **auto-revoked** at downgrade with `status = buyer_revoked`; Audit Event logged. New grants cannot be issued while the buyer is on a sub-Scale tier. `buyer_plan_tier_at_grant` is frozen so downstream reports correctly attribute the mechanic to the plan level at issuance.
- **Pool accounting under mid-cycle upgrade (Scale → Enterprise).** The buyer's current-cycle `buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant` is **not retroactively increased** for the current cycle; the upgraded allocation takes effect on the next billing anniversary. Authored extension; documented here and in RECONCILIATION.md.
- **Vendor already on paid plan.** `already_paid_block_triggered = true`, `status = fraud_blocked` with `anti_spam_hold_reason = vendor_already_paid`; the grant is reversed to the buyer's pool (restores one seat) and the buyer notified in-app.
- **Same buyer/vendor within 365 days.** `same_buyer_365d_block_triggered = true`, `status = fraud_blocked`; pool seat restored; buyer notified.
- **Vendor Billing Admin declines during trial.** `status = vendor_declined`, `outcome = vendor_declined`; the pool seat is **not** restored (buyer has already used the slot meaningfully). Authored extension.
- **Vendor never signs up (30-day invite TTL).** `status = expired_unaccepted`, `outcome = never_provisioned`; pool seat **is** restored to the buyer's cycle balance (the grant never activated). Authored extension.

### 4.3.18 Usage Event (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console, PostHog-Mirrored)

C.88 / C.89 standardized event. Every buyer- and seller-side action surfaces one row here **and** a matching PostHog event. Dual writes use an outbox pattern (§34.12) for at-least-once delivery with deduplication by `id`.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key; used as PostHog event distinct ID | Ensures idempotent retry |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | Org that owns the event |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` \| `seller` | Source console |
| `event_name` | String | Max 100 chars, must match Appendix G registry | Enforced at write via enum registry lookup |
| `event_category` | Enum | See Appendix J `usage_event_category` | Rollup dimension |
| `user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | Null for system-generated events |
| `session_id` | UUID | Convex session, nullable | Null for server-initiated events |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable; FK → Workspace (buyer) or Bid Workspace (seller) per `console` | Validated against console |
| `phase` | Integer | 0–15, nullable | Workspace phase at event time; denormalized for joinability |
| `entity_ref_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `usage_event_entity_ref_type` | What entity this event concerns |
| `entity_ref_id` | UUID | Nullable | Specific entity; validated against `entity_ref_type` |
| `capability_id` | UUID (FK) | Capability Declaration ID, nullable | Populated for AI Operation events |
| `capability_window` | String | Max 100 chars, nullable | Outcome Resolver window (e.g., `pre_scoring.accept`) per §34.14 |
| `outcome` | Enum | See Appendix J `usage_event_outcome` | Aligns with Outcome Resolver |
| `properties_json` | JSON | Max 10000 chars | Event-specific properties; schema constrained to `event_name` per Appendix G |
| `latency_ms` | Integer | ≥ 0, nullable | For performance events |
| `ai_value_dollars` | Decimal(10,4) | ≥ 0, nullable | AI value-dollars consumed by this event; ties to §34 Wallet |
| `client_timezone` | String | IANA tz, max 64 chars | From client at capture |
| `ip_address_hash` | String | SHA-256 hex, 64 chars | Never raw IP per §45.1 |
| `user_agent_class` | Enum | See Appendix J `usage_event_user_agent_class` | Class, not raw UA |
| `correlation_id` | UUID | Nullable | Groups related events within a single user journey (e.g. multi-step AI operation) |
| `posthog_delivery_status` | Enum | `pending` \| `acked` \| `failed` \| `skipped_pii_blocked` | Outbox delivery state |
| `posthog_last_attempt_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | For monitoring ingestion lag |
| `ingested_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When PostHog acked |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |

**Indexes:**

- `(org_id, event_name, created_at DESC)` — dashboard queries.
- `(org_id, user_id, created_at DESC)` — User Usage Dashboard (C.90).
- `(org_id, capability_id, created_at DESC)` — per-capability AI spend (C.90).
- `(entity_ref_type, entity_ref_id, created_at DESC)` — per-entity traces.
- `(posthog_delivery_status, posthog_last_attempt_at)` — outbox retry sweep.
- `(correlation_id)` — multi-step journey reconstruction.
- `(org_id, event_category, created_at DESC)` — category rollups for Time-Saved.

**Scope Isolation:** Org-scoped on `org_id`. Cross-console by design — a single Org may operate both consoles. Row-level read rules enforce the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2): a requesting session operating in buyer console may only read events with `console = 'buyer'`; seller-console sessions may only read `console = 'seller'`; Ops Console roles may read across consoles under §6 audit scope. Role gating within a console: Org Owner, Org Admin, and Billing Admin read all events for that console; standard users read only their own (`user_id = requesting_user_id`). PostHog projection is org-scoped + console-filtered with the same role gating.

**Polymorphic `workspace_id` Validation:** Because `workspace_id` may reference Workspace (buyer console) or Bid Workspace (seller console), the FK is not enforced at the database layer. The API write layer validates the reference against `console` at ingestion; PostHog mirror writes carry `console` as a required super-property so downstream joins are unambiguous. Invalid cross-console references return Appendix I error code `usage_event_console_mismatch` (new; HTTP 422).

**PostHog Outbox Retry Policy:** `posthog_delivery_status = pending` rows are retried by the ingestion worker on an exponential backoff curve aligned with §31 webhook retries (1s → 5s → 30s → 2m → 10m → 1h). After 5 failures, status transitions to `failed` and the row is routed to the Usage Event DLQ (Appendix F retry policies extended to cover this). DLQ items are retained 30 days; Ops Console surfaces a DLQ queue depth alert at >1000 items. `failed` events remain in the Convex store (source-of-truth integrity preserved); only PostHog mirror is lost.

**Retention:** 24-month rolling raw retention per C.88. At 24 months, rows are anonymized: `user_id` pseudonymized, `ip_address_hash` purged, `properties_json` compacted to coarse counts, and rolled up into monthly aggregates. Aggregates retained for Org-life. DSAR right-to-erasure redacts `user_id` and `properties_json` values referencing the subject within 30 days per §6.8. New §40.2 row required.

**Relationships:** References Organization, User, Workspace / Bid Workspace, Capability Declaration, and arbitrary entity via `entity_ref_type`/`entity_ref_id`. Drives Time-Saved Credit generation (one-to-one via `source_event_id`).

**Authoring Intent:** Maintaining a canonical ledger in Convex **in addition to** PostHog (rather than writing only to PostHog) is required by three constraints: (a) billing-grade reconciliation for `ai_value_dollars` — PostHog is not a system of record; (b) DSAR compliance — PostHog's erasure semantics lag Sourcera's 30-day SLA; (c) Convex reactive queries power in-product dashboards (C.90) with sub-second latency that PostHog cannot provide. The outbox pattern guarantees at-least-once delivery with `id`-based dedup on PostHog's side. `posthog_delivery_status=skipped_pii_blocked` handles the edge case where a user's DSAR is mid-process when an event fires.

### 4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console, Computed)

C.91 Time-Saved Baseline Model output. One credit per Usage Event that crosses a capability's minutes-saved threshold.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Organization ID | Owning Org |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` \| `seller` | Source console |
| `user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID, nullable | User attributed; null for aggregate credits |
| `source_event_id` | UUID (FK) | Usage Event ID | One-to-one with triggering event |
| `capability_id` | UUID (FK) | Capability Declaration ID, nullable | Which capability produced the saving |
| `capability_window` | String | Max 100 chars | Mirrors Usage Event.capability_window |
| `conversion_factor_version` | String | Max 50 chars | Version stamp; ties to C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager |
| `conversion_factor_minutes` | Decimal(8,2) | ≥ 0 | Minutes-saved-per-event at credit time; frozen against version for audit |
| `minutes_saved` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0 | Actual minutes credited |
| `loaded_hourly_rate_usd` | Decimal(8,2) | ≥ 0, default: org setting | Labor rate for monetization; org default overridable per user for Enterprise |
| `loaded_hourly_rate_source` | Enum | `org_default` \| `user_override` \| `ops_calibration` | See Appendix J |
| `value_saved_usd` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0, = `minutes_saved / 60 × loaded_hourly_rate_usd`, rounded banker's | Monetized savings |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Workspace or Bid Workspace, nullable | When tied to a workspace |
| `recognized_at` | Timestamp | Immutable, UTC | ≈ source event time |
| `reversed_by_credit_id` | UUID (FK) | Time-Saved Credit ID, nullable | Set on this row if a reversal supersedes it |
| `reversal_of_credit_id` | UUID (FK) | Time-Saved Credit ID, nullable | Self-FK; populated on reversal rows only |
| `reversal_reason` | Enum | `ai_outcome_undone` \| `user_rejected_retroactively` \| `ops_correction` \| `fraud_removal`, nullable | See Appendix J |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC, = `recognized_at` + epsilon |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete discouraged; reversals preferred for audit integrity |

**Indexes:**

- `(org_id, recognized_at DESC)` — Org dashboard.
- `(org_id, user_id, recognized_at DESC)` — per-user totals.
- `(org_id, capability_id, recognized_at DESC)` — capability mix.
- `(source_event_id)` UNIQUE — one credit per Usage Event (reversal rows use `reversal_of_credit_id`, not a new `source_event_id`).
- `(reversal_of_credit_id)` — reversal lookup.

**Scope Isolation:** Org-scoped; cross-console. Role-gated read parity with Usage Event.

**Retention:** 36-month rolling raw retention; after 36 months, raw rows purged and only monthly aggregates retained. Aggregates retained for Org-life. DSAR pathway identical to Usage Event. New §40.2 row required.

**Relationships:** References Usage Event (`source_event_id`), Capability Declaration, User, Workspace / Bid Workspace. Reversals form a self-referential linked list via `reversal_of_credit_id` + `reversed_by_credit_id`.

**Authoring Intent:** Persisting Time-Saved Credits as entities (rather than computing on-demand) is required for three reasons: (a) C.97 allows conversion-factor changes; without frozen `conversion_factor_version` and `conversion_factor_minutes`, the Org Dashboard figure would retroactively change on every factor edit, which is unacceptable; (b) the reversal model supports retroactive AI-outcome undoes (e.g., a Pre-Scoring accept later reverted by a reviewer); (c) the Org Dashboard and the PLG inline surface must hit sub-100ms for the headline figure, which rules out on-demand computation. `loaded_hourly_rate_source` is an authored extension that resolves the ambiguity in C.91 about per-user rate overrides.

**Aggregation Semantics (Reversal-Aware):** Org Dashboard and PLG surfaces compute `total_minutes_saved` and `total_value_saved_usd` as a SUM across Time-Saved Credit rows where `reversed_by_credit_id IS NULL` — i.e., the original row is excluded once it is superseded by a reversal row, and the reversal row itself is **not** aggregated (it is a pointer-only record). Equivalently: a reversal row has `minutes_saved = 0` and exists solely to flip `reversed_by_credit_id` on the original row. This keeps aggregate queries as a single indexed SUM with a NULL filter and avoids SUM(credit - reversal) arithmetic. Reversal authors must maintain this invariant at the application layer.

### 4.4.7 Marketplace Category (Platform-Scoped, Ops-Managed Taxonomy) {#4.4.7-marketplace-category}

**Authoring Intent.** Marketplace Category is the canonical, Ops-maintained controlled-vocabulary taxonomy that all vendor-facing and platform-generated Marketplace entities reference by FK. Per Summary C.60 (Marketplace Tags & Controlled Vocabulary) this registry is maintained in the Ops Console CMS, not authored per-Org. Enumerates the `category` dimension used by SellerSoftware, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, HeatMapCell, and SellerSignal.

**Scope:** Platform-scoped (no `org_id`; single global taxonomy). Not console-scoped. Read access is public; write access restricted to the Ops Console role `ops_taxonomy_admin` (new; added to Appendix J).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `slug` | String | 3–60 chars, lowercase, `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, globally unique | URL segment for Category, Guide, Heat Map paths |
| `name` | String | 1–100 chars | Display name (e.g., "HRMS for Mid-Market") |
| `short_name` | String | 1–40 chars | Compact label for breadcrumbs and comparison headers |
| `description` | String | 0–2000 chars | Ops-authored category description (markdown) |
| `parent_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Marketplace Category | Supports two-level hierarchy (parent + child); deeper nesting rejected at write |
| `depth` | Integer | 0 or 1 | Computed; 0 = root, 1 = child. Enforced at write |
| `sort_order` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Display order within parent |
| `icon_token` | String | See Appendix J `marketplace_category_icon_token` | Design-system icon reference |
| `state` | Enum | See Appendix J `marketplace_category_state`: `draft`, `active`, `deprecated` | See state machine below |
| `deprecated_replaces_with_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Marketplace Category | Populated when `state=deprecated`; points to successor |
| `seo_metadata_json` | JSON | ≤ 4000 chars | Default `meta_title`, `meta_description`, and `hreflang` defaults for derived pages |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops User ID | Creator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops User ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; cascade per Scope Isolation below |

**Indexes.** `(slug)` unique, `(parent_id, sort_order)`, `(state)`, `(deleted_at)`.

**Scope Isolation.** Category rows are global. FKs pointing at Category (from SellerSoftware, SoftwarePage, etc.) do **not** confer any Org-level read access. Deleting (soft) a Category MUST NOT orphan SellerSoftware rows — the write layer rejects delete when ≥1 SellerSoftware references the Category; Ops must reassign via the `deprecated_replaces_with_id` migration worker (authored below) before soft-delete. Hard-delete is forbidden; deprecation is the terminal state.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Ops creates | — | New taxonomy node; not resolvable on public paths |
| `draft` | `active` | Ops publishes | Slug + name + parent valid; SEO metadata populated | Category becomes resolvable; search indexers pick up |
| `active` | `deprecated` | Ops deprecates | `deprecated_replaces_with_id` set; zero referencing SellerSoftware rows (after migration) | Public paths 301-redirect to successor; derived pages archived per each page type's state machine |
| `deprecated` | `active` | Ops reactivates | Within 30 days of deprecation | Reverses redirects and un-archives derived pages |
| `draft` | `deleted_at` (soft) | Ops deletes | Zero referencing rows | Only valid from `draft` |

**Retention.** Life of platform. Soft-deleted `draft` rows purged 30 days after soft-delete. `deprecated` nodes retained indefinitely to preserve historical FK integrity and redirect continuity. DSAR: not applicable (no PII). Residency: served from global edge cache; taxonomy does not carry customer data.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a Category with `depth=1` and a `parent_id` that is itself `depth=1` MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_max_depth_exceeded` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
2. Attempting to soft-delete a Category that has ≥1 active referencing SellerSoftware row MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_delete_blocked_by_references` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). The error payload MUST include the count of referencing rows and a link to the migration endpoint.
3. Transitioning a Category to `deprecated` without `deprecated_replaces_with_id` populated MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_deprecate_requires_successor` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
4. Category slug collisions MUST be rejected at write with error `taxonomy_slug_conflict` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Slug is case-insensitive-unique.
5. Resolving a deprecated Category on a public path MUST 301-redirect to the successor's public path; the redirect chain depth MUST NOT exceed 3 hops.
6. Cache-invalidation events for CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, HeatMapCell, and MarketIntelligenceReport rows referencing an updated Category MUST fire within 60s of the Category `updated_at` bump (observable via the `taxonomy.category.updated` webhook authored in a subsequent phase).

### 4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record (Org-Scoped, Seller-Origin, Platform-Honored) {#4.4.8-vendor-opt-out-record}

**Authoring Intent.** Vendor Opt-Out Record is the authoritative Opt-Out Registry per Summary C.123. A Seller Org uses it to suppress their name, pages, or product references from public-facing, Sourcera-owned Marketplace mechanics (Public Selection Reports, Category Pages, Comparison Pages, Heat Map, Market Intelligence Reports, Guide Pages, and any other downstream mechanic that references their identity). Opt-outs are retroactive (scan-and-redact existing rendered content), honored across all buyer Orgs, and append-only: new opt-outs create new rows rather than mutating prior ones, so the audit trail is immutable.

**Scope:** Org-scoped (`org_id` = Seller Org). Cross-Org read: Platform read access only (Ops Console + derived-page rendering paths); never exposed via the Buyer Console API.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Seller's organization |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | Identifies originating console |
| `scope_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind`: `global`, `category`, `software`, `page_type`, `specific_page` | Controls suppression breadth |
| `scope_ref_id` | UUID (FK, polymorphic) | Nullable for `global`; required otherwise | FK target depends on `scope_kind` (Marketplace Category, SellerSoftware, Page entity, etc.) |
| `scope_ref_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_scope_ref_type`: `marketplace_category`, `seller_software`, `category_page`, `comparison_page`, `guide_page`, `market_intelligence_report`, `heat_map_cell`, `public_selection_report`, `null` | `null` only when `scope_kind=global` or `page_type` |
| `page_type_filter` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_page_type_filter`: `comparison_page`, `category_page`, `guide_page`, `market_intelligence_report`, `heat_map_cell`, `public_selection_report`, `seller_org_page`, `software_page` | Required when `scope_kind=page_type`; forbidden otherwise |
| `effective_from` | Timestamp | Immutable | When the opt-out becomes active; may be backdated by Ops |
| `effective_until` | Timestamp | Nullable | Expiration; null = indefinite |
| `reason_code` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_reason_code`: `legal`, `competitive`, `accuracy_dispute`, `gdpr_request`, `ops_imposed`, `other` | Drives Ops review routing |
| `reason_note` | String | 0–1000 chars | Seller-provided rationale; required when `reason_code=other` |
| `ops_review_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_ops_review_status`: `auto_honored`, `pending_ops_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `revoked` | Opt-outs are auto-honored on write; Ops review runs post-hoc per C.123 |
| `ops_reviewed_by` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Ops User ID | Set on Ops action |
| `ops_reviewed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on Ops action |
| `ops_rejection_reason` | String | 0–500 chars; nullable | Populated when `ops_review_status=rejected` |
| `retro_backfill_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_retro_backfill_status`: `pending`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `failed`, `not_applicable` | Tracks sweep of already-published pages |
| `retro_backfill_completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when backfill sweep finishes |
| `retro_backfill_affected_page_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | Count of public-page rows updated |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Must hold seller-console role `seller_billing_admin` or `seller_org_admin` |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User or Ops ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; equivalent to `revoked` when `ops_review_status=revoked` |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, scope_kind, scope_ref_type, scope_ref_id)` composite for fast suppression lookup; `(ops_review_status, created_at)` for Ops review queue; `(retro_backfill_status)` partial index on non-terminal states; `(effective_from, effective_until)` for active-window queries.

**Scope Isolation.** Writes are restricted to seller-console sessions with role `seller_billing_admin` or `seller_org_admin`. Buyer-console API MUST return 404 (not 403) if a buyer token attempts any CRUD; error code `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404). Ops Console retains full read + state-machine transitions. The Registry is queried by every public-page render path as a precondition — rendering MUST abort with a "Vendor opted out" placeholder when a matching opt-out is active.

**Suppression Match Semantics.** At page render, the registry is evaluated against the candidate `(seller_org_id, referenced_entity_type, referenced_entity_id)` tuple. Match rules:

- `global` → suppresses all references to this seller_org across all public-page types.
- `category` → suppresses references to this seller_org on any page whose primary Category matches `scope_ref_id` OR on any SoftwarePage whose SellerSoftware's Category matches.
- `software` → suppresses references to a specific SellerSoftware `scope_ref_id`.
- `page_type` → suppresses references to this seller_org on all pages of `page_type_filter`.
- `specific_page` → suppresses references on a single named public-page row (`scope_ref_id` + `scope_ref_type`).

**State Machine (`ops_review_status`).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `auto_honored` | Seller creates | `effective_from ≤ now`, valid scope | Suppression active immediately; retro sweep scheduled |
| `auto_honored` | `pending_ops_review` | Flagged for review | Reason code in `{legal, gdpr_request, accuracy_dispute}` OR seller Org flagged by SIM (C.100) | Seller-visible status remains "Active"; Ops queue populated |
| `pending_ops_review` | `approved` | Ops approves | Ops user with `ops_opt_out_admin` role | Suppression remains active; `ops_reviewed_at` stamped |
| `pending_ops_review` | `rejected` | Ops rejects | Rejection reason required | Suppression reversed; `retro_backfill` re-fires in reverse |
| `approved` / `auto_honored` | `revoked` | Seller revokes OR Ops revokes | Any time | Suppression lifted; retro backfill re-populates the affected pages |

**Retention & DSAR.**

- Identity fields (`created_by`): pseudonymized on DSAR within 30 days per §6.8, leaving `retro_backfill_affected_page_count` and the opt-out record itself intact for audit.
- Reason notes: pseudonymized with the identity fields.
- Record retention: Org-life + 7 years to preserve Marketplace audit trail and legal defensibility of suppression decisions. Not subject to right-to-erasure under §45.1 platform-integrity exemption.
- Residency: record stored in originating Seller Org's data region; consumers (global page-render paths) query via a globally-replicated read index.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Race between seller write and page render.** Public-page render paths MUST evaluate the Opt-Out Registry against a snapshot taken within 60s of the render; snapshots older than 60s are rejected and re-computed. Pages rendered before an opt-out's `effective_from` are re-rendered within 15 minutes of opt-out write (triggers `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook + cache bust).
2. **Opt-out targeting a deleted entity.** If `scope_ref_id` points at a soft-deleted target, the opt-out remains valid for historical pages during the target's soft-delete window. After hard-purge of the target, `ops_review_status=auto_honored` rows with `scope_ref_type` pointing at the purged entity transition to `revoked` with reason `scope_target_purged` (authored here; add to `vendor_opt_out_rejection_reason`).
3. **Ops-imposed opt-outs vs. seller-originated opt-outs.** Ops may create opt-outs with `reason_code=ops_imposed`; these skip the seller-side write-gate (created_by is an Ops User ID) and cannot be revoked by the seller — only by Ops.
4. **Backfill sweep fails mid-flight.** If `retro_backfill_status=failed`, the opt-out remains active (fail-closed). The sweep worker re-attempts on an exponential-backoff curve (see §31 retry curve class `retroactive_sweep`, to be added in Phase 3) and pages the Ops on-call after 5 consecutive failures.
5. **Cross-Category deprecation with successor.** If a Category is deprecated and successors are reassigned, `category`-scoped opt-outs are cloned at write to the successor Category with `reason_code=ops_imposed` (authored extension; flagged).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Seller Billing Admin or Org Admin creating a `global` opt-out MUST see all referenced public pages redact the seller's name within 15 minutes (measured via `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook timestamps).
2. Any buyer-console session attempting to read/write the Opt-Out Registry API MUST receive HTTP 404 with `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`.
3. A reason_code of `other` with empty `reason_note` MUST be rejected at write with `vendor_opt_out_reason_note_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
4. Revoking an opt-out MUST re-publish the previously suppressed pages within 15 minutes and emit `vendor_opt_out.revoked`.
5. Retroactive backfill sweep MUST update `retro_backfill_affected_page_count` accurately (tolerance ±0); a QA suite (§13.10 style) compares pre-sweep vs. post-sweep page snapshots.

### 4.4.9 SellerSoftware (Console-Scoped, Seller) {#4.4.9-sellersoftware}

**Authoring Intent.** SellerSoftware represents a single software product owned by a Seller Org — distinct from the Seller Org itself — per Summary §6.15.5. One Seller Org → many SellerSoftware rows. Powers Software Pages, Comparison Pages, per-product Capability Declarations, per-product KB namespaces, and Marketplace search granularity. Introduced because a vendor with five products cannot be adequately represented by a single Seller Profile row.

**Scope:** Console-scoped (Seller). Not Marketplace-domain — this is the authoring entity; the public-facing render is SoftwarePage (§4.4.11).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Seller's organization |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | Identifies console scope |
| `seller_profile_id` | UUID | FK → Seller Profile | Parent profile |
| `name` | String | 1–200 chars | Product name as marketed |
| `slug` | String | 3–80 chars, `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, unique within `(org_id)` AND globally unique for published rows | URL segment; see Slug Collision Rule below |
| `tagline` | String | 0–200 chars | Short pitch |
| `description` | String | 0–5000 chars | Markdown; product description |
| `category_id` | UUID | FK → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7); `depth=1` preferred | Primary category |
| `secondary_category_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–3 entries; FKs → Marketplace Category | Additional categories (surfaced in Comparison Pages) |
| `logo_url` | String | Valid HTTPS URL; ≤ 2000 chars | Product logo |
| `hero_image_url` | String | Valid HTTPS URL; ≤ 2000 chars; nullable | Hero/banner |
| `pricing_model` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_software_pricing_model`: `subscription`, `consumption`, `perpetual`, `custom`, `freemium` | Pricing type |
| `pricing_summary` | String | 0–1000 chars | Human-readable pricing note |
| `maturity_stage` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_software_maturity_stage`: `alpha`, `beta`, `ga`, `sunset` | Product lifecycle |
| `capability_declaration_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–500 entries; FKs → Capability Declaration (§4.4.4) | Normalized association (see scope rule below) |
| `kb_namespace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → KB Namespace (per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4) | Software-level KB namespace; one-to-one |
| `former_kb_namespace_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–10 entries | Historical namespaces from prior renames/merges; used by retrieval for provenance (KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4) |
| `claim_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_software_claim_status`: `unclaimed`, `claim_pending`, `claim_verified`, `claim_disputed`, `claim_revoked` | See state machine below |
| `claim_verified_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when `claim_status=claim_verified` |
| `claim_verified_by_method` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `seller_software_claim_verification_method`: `dns_txt`, `email_verification`, `ops_manual_verification`, `sso_domain_match` | How claim was verified |
| `claim_disputed_by_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Organization | Disputing party (other Seller Org) |
| `page_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_software_page_status`: `no_page`, `page_drafting`, `page_pending_review`, `page_published`, `page_suppressed_by_opt_out`, `page_archived` | Tracks linked SoftwarePage lifecycle (denormalized for list views; SoftwarePage.publication_status is source of truth) |
| `seo_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_software_seo_status`: `not_indexed`, `indexing_pending`, `indexed`, `deindexed_by_opt_out`, `deindexed_manual` | SEO indexing state |
| `seo_last_crawled_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last observed crawl (via Search Console API; updated daily) |
| `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last time the Opt-Out Registry was evaluated for this row (see Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule below) |
| `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) | Active opt-out suppressing this Software's visibility, if any |
| `retention_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J `data_retention_tier`: `standard`, `extended_financial` | Drives retention; `standard` by default |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Creator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; triggers KB namespace migration per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, slug)` unique, `(slug) WHERE page_status='page_published'` unique (global slug contention only for published rows), `(category_id, claim_status)`, `(kb_namespace_id)` unique, `(vendor_opt_out_ref_id)` partial, `(deleted_at)`.

**Scope Isolation.** Console-scoped to the owning Seller Org. Capability Declarations referenced via `capability_declaration_ids` MUST resolve to declarations where `org_id` matches this SellerSoftware's `org_id`; cross-Org references rejected at write with `seller_software_cross_org_capability_ref` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Buyer-console API MUST NOT expose SellerSoftware rows in `draft`/`page_drafting` state; only `page_published` rows (via the SoftwarePage projection) are buyer-visible.

**Slug Collision Rule.** Slugs are unique within an Org (to support draft/staging workflows) and globally unique for rows with `page_status=page_published`. Transitioning a row to `page_published` when its slug collides with another published row MUST be rejected with `seller_software_slug_collision` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Slug may be changed while the row is in `no_page` or `page_drafting`; once published, slug becomes immutable (append-only — rename creates a 301 redirect slug-alias row authored in Phase 3).

**Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule.** `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` is stamped every time the render path (or the nightly sweep) evaluates the Opt-Out Registry for this Software. `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` is populated only when an active opt-out matches this row; it is nulled when the opt-out is revoked or expires. The Opt-Out Registry (§4.4.8) remains the canonical source; `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` is a denormalized pointer for read-path performance and MUST be reconciled nightly against the Registry. Reconciliation drift ≥1% fires an Ops alert.

**State Machine (`claim_status`).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `unclaimed` | Row created by Sourcera enrichment worker before any seller has claimed | Row auto-created from Summary §6.15.4 seller enrichment or ghost-bid imports | Public SoftwarePage may render in "unclaimed" state with a "Claim this listing" CTA |
| `unclaimed` | `claim_pending` | A seller Org initiates claim | Must provide one of: DNS TXT record, verified email at domain, SSO domain match | Claim expires after 14 days if not verified |
| `claim_pending` | `claim_verified` | Verification succeeds | `claim_verified_by_method` populated; domain cross-check passes | Seller Org granted edit rights; `seller_profile_id` set |
| `claim_pending` | `claim_disputed` | A second Org initiates concurrent claim | `claim_disputed_by_org_id` populated | Both claims frozen pending Ops resolution |
| `claim_disputed` | `claim_verified` | Ops resolves in favor of one party | `ops_resolution_note` logged in audit | Losing party notified and blocked from re-claim for 30 days |
| `claim_verified` | `claim_revoked` | Ops revokes (e.g., domain ownership lost, fraud) OR seller Org deleted | — | Row reverts to `unclaimed`; SoftwarePage suppressed |
| `claim_pending` | `unclaimed` | 14-day TTL expires without verification | — | Claim attempt cleared; logged in audit |

**KB Namespace Relationship.** Each SellerSoftware owns exactly one KB namespace (`kb_namespace_id`). Namespace is auto-created on SellerSoftware creation and auto-migrated to the Org namespace on SellerSoftware soft-delete per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 (which authored the migration procedure). `former_kb_namespace_ids` is append-only; entries never removed, so provenance audits across renames remain reconstructable.

**Retention & DSAR.**

- Row retention: Org-life. On Seller Org deletion (§7.2 cascade), SellerSoftware soft-deleted then hard-purged after 90 days, with KB namespace migrated to a platform-managed "orphan" namespace for retrieval continuity of historical bids.
- DSAR: `created_by` and `updated_by` pseudonymized on user deprovisioning; product content (description, capability refs) retained as Org-owned material.
- Residency: SellerSoftware rows stored in the Seller Org's data region; public-page projections (SoftwarePage) are globally cached at the edge.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Two Orgs claim the same product.** Resolved via `claim_disputed` state + Ops arbitration.
2. **Seller Org loses domain ownership.** Resolved via Ops revocation (`claim_revoked`) + 30-day re-claim block.
3. **Category deprecated while SellerSoftware references it.** Migration worker reassigns to successor Category (per §4.4.7); `secondary_category_ids` pruned of deprecated entries.
4. **KB namespace orphaned on deletion.** Handled by KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 migration procedure.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a SellerSoftware with a Category that is `state=deprecated` MUST be rejected with `seller_software_category_deprecated` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
2. Two concurrent claims for the same `slug`+`name` from different Orgs MUST both transition to `claim_disputed`; neither Org may edit the row until Ops resolves.
3. Soft-deleting a SellerSoftware MUST trigger KB namespace migration within 5 minutes (observable via `kb_namespace_migration` audit event per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4).
4. Publishing a SoftwarePage for a SellerSoftware with `claim_status != claim_verified` MUST be rejected with `seller_software_page_requires_verified_claim` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
5. Reading a SellerSoftware with `vendor_opt_out_ref_id != null` through any public endpoint MUST return the suppressed projection (name redacted to the seller's chosen placeholder, capability declarations hidden).
6. Capability Declaration references in `capability_declaration_ids` MUST be reverse-validated nightly; dangling references increment the `seller_software.capability_reference_drift` metric (Appendix G) and page the Ops on-call at drift ≥1%.

### 4.4.10 SellerOrgPage (Marketplace-Domain, Seller-Authored, Public) {#4.4.10-sellerorgpage}

**Authoring Intent.** SellerOrgPage is the public-facing page entity backing `sourcera.com/sellers/:slug` per Summary §6.15.4. Auto-enriched via the Opus-tier `page_enrichment` capability, which crawls the seller's public surfaces and drafts content for seller review before publication. Verified domain ownership (via the Seller Org's SSO or Seller Profile claim workflow) gates publication.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (public). `org_id` retained as the canonical ownership pointer; however, read access is public and not gated by Org-level ACLs. Write access is restricted to Seller Org members with `seller_org_admin` or `seller_marketing_editor` (new role — added to Appendix J).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Owning Seller Org |
| `seller_profile_id` | UUID | FK → Seller Profile | One-to-one with Seller Profile |
| `slug` | String | 3–80 chars, `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, globally unique across SellerOrgPage | URL segment; immutable once `publication_status=published` |
| `meta_title` | String | 10–60 chars | `<title>` tag |
| `meta_description` | String | 50–160 chars | Meta description |
| `canonical_url` | String | Valid HTTPS URL; ≤ 2000 chars | `rel=canonical` target |
| `og_image_url` | String | Valid HTTPS URL; ≤ 2000 chars; nullable | Open Graph image |
| `hero_copy_markdown` | String | 0–3000 chars | Markdown; above-the-fold copy |
| `body_sections_json` | JSON | ≤ 50000 chars | Ordered section array (heading + body + asset refs); validated against schema in Appendix G |
| `schema_org_payload_json` | JSON | ≤ 20000 chars | Cached Schema.org payload (`Organization` + `Offer` + `AggregateRating` if applicable) |
| `schema_org_payload_refreshed_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | Last payload regeneration |
| `last_enrichment_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Most recent successful Opus enrichment run |
| `last_enrichment_capability_ref` | String | Enum: `page_enrichment` | Always `page_enrichment` (for audit/uniformity with other page entities) |
| `enrichment_cost_center` | Enum | `sourcera_owned` (fixed) | Per Summary §6.16.5; Opus enrichment billed to Platform Marketing, not customer |
| `pending_enrichment_draft_json` | JSON | ≤ 50000 chars; nullable | Draft awaiting seller review; cleared on approve/reject |
| `enrichment_approved_by` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Seller User ID | Who approved the most recent enrichment draft |
| `enrichment_approved_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When the approval happened |
| `publication_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `page_publication_status`: `draft`, `pending_enrichment`, `pending_review`, `published`, `suppressed_by_opt_out`, `archived` | See state machine below |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | First publication time; retained across unpublish/republish |
| `last_published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Most recent publication time |
| `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last registry-evaluation timestamp |
| `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) | Active opt-out if any |

| `seo_last_crawled_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | From Google Search Console API |
| `seo_indexed` | Boolean | Default false | Observed in index |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum | See Appendix J `data_residency_region`: `us`, `eu`, `apac`, `custom` | Inherited from Seller Org Organization record |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID or `system_enrichment_worker` | Creator (may be auto-enrichment) |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete |

**Indexes.** `(slug)` unique, `(seller_profile_id)` unique, `(org_id)`, `(publication_status)`, `(vendor_opt_out_ref_id)` partial, `(last_enrichment_at)`, `(deleted_at)`.

**Scope Isolation.** Publication path is public. Authoring/preview endpoints require seller-console session with the authoring roles above. Buyer-console sessions receive only the public projection (same as anonymous). The `pending_enrichment_draft_json` field MUST NEVER leak into the public projection — enforced by a whitelist-only API serializer.

**State Machine (`publication_status`).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Seller creates | — | Not yet enriched |
| `draft` | `pending_enrichment` | Enrichment requested | `page_enrichment` capability run queued | AI operation billed to Platform Marketing (`sourcera_owned` cost center) |
| `pending_enrichment` | `pending_review` | Enrichment completes | `pending_enrichment_draft_json` populated | Seller must review before publish |
| `pending_review` | `draft` | Seller rejects draft | — | Seller may edit and re-request enrichment |
| `pending_review` | `published` | Seller approves + publishes | `domain_ownership_verified_at` not null; `meta_title`, `meta_description` populated; no active matching opt-out | `schema_org_payload_json` regenerated at publish |
| `published` | `pending_review` | Seller edits (non-trivial) | Seller edits triggering enrichment re-run | Auto re-enrichment optional |
| `published` | `suppressed_by_opt_out` | Matching VendorOptOutRecord activates | — | Public URL returns a "Vendor opted out" stub; cache bust within 15 min |
| `suppressed_by_opt_out` | `published` | Opt-out revoked | — | Republished automatically |
| Any | `archived` | Seller archives OR Org deletion cascade | — | URL 410-gones; 410 response cached for 30 days then purged |

**Retention & DSAR.**

- Published rows retained for Org-life.
- On Seller Org deletion (§7.2): transition to `archived`, 90-day retention, then purge. `schema_org_payload_json` cache purged within 30 days; CDN cache explicitly busted.
- DSAR: authored fields (bios, contact callouts) containing PII are redacted within 30 days; page content is Org-owned and retained unless DSAR targets a specific author.
- Residency: SellerOrgPage stored in the Seller Org's `data_residency_region`; public cache served from global edge; page payload is non-PII by construction (any PII must be explicitly authored and is subject to DSAR sweep).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Domain ownership revoked post-publication.** Trigger: Seller Profile claim revoked → cascade transitions SellerOrgPage to `suppressed_by_opt_out` with synthetic opt-out record (`reason_code=ops_imposed`). Authored extension.
2. **Enrichment returns content that fails content validators (§3.5 anti-spam).** Drafts rejected; Ops alerted; cost not charged to Platform Marketing (reversal per §34.14 Outcome Resolver).
3. **Schema.org cache drift.** Nightly reconciliation worker regenerates `schema_org_payload_json` if `updated_at > schema_org_payload_refreshed_at + 24h`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Publishing without `domain_ownership_verified_at` MUST be rejected with `seller_org_page_requires_domain_verification` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
2. A published SellerOrgPage receiving a matching opt-out MUST transition to `suppressed_by_opt_out` within 15 minutes (measured via `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook chain).
3. Public GET requests for a suppressed page MUST return HTTP 200 with the placeholder body (not 404; 404 would break SEO and invite recrawl thrash); `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header required.
4. `pending_enrichment_draft_json` MUST NOT appear in any public or buyer-console response payload; enforced by serializer test in §13.10-style QA suite.

One-to-one with SellerSoftware (§4.4.9). All fields, state machine, and operational rules mirror SellerOrgPage (§4.4.10) except where noted below.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (public). Write access requires `claim_status=claim_verified` on the parent SellerSoftware.
