**Indexes.** `(kind, slug)` unique, `(kind, parent_id, sort_order)`, `(kind, state)`, `(state)`, `(deleted_at)`, GIN on `aliases` for alias search, `(marketplace_category_ref_id)` partial where not null.

**Scope Isolation.** Taxonomy Node rows are global. FKs to Taxonomy Node from customer-facing entities (Capability Declaration, Seller Profile, Marketplace Listing filter, HeatMapCell facet) do NOT confer any Org-level read access on the customer-facing row. Deleting (soft) a Taxonomy Node MUST NOT orphan referencing rows — the write layer rejects delete when any non-soft-deleted referencing row exists (see Acceptance Criteria). Hard-delete is forbidden; deprecation is the terminal published state. For `kind=marketplace_category`, any write that would diverge from the paired §4.4.7 row (different `slug`, `name`, `state`, `parent_id`, or `successor_id`) is rejected with `taxonomy_marketplace_category_projection_mismatch` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**Cross-Reference to §4.4.7.** Marketplace Category rows are the source of truth for their category-specific fields (parent hierarchy, SEO metadata, icon token). A Taxonomy Node row with `kind=marketplace_category` exists as a shared-registry projection so that any consumer that needs "a taxonomy node" (e.g., Controlled-Vocabulary Tag `taxonomy_dimension=marketplace_category`) can resolve via a single FK target. A nightly reconciliation worker ensures that every Marketplace Category row has exactly one `kind=marketplace_category` Taxonomy Node row and that the paired fields match; mismatches raise `taxonomy_projection_drift` alerts to Ops (new; Appendix F alert class; Ops runbook authored in a subsequent phase).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Ops creates | `kind`, `slug`, `name` valid; `parent_id` (if set) in `active` state and same `kind` | New node; not resolvable on public paths |
| `draft` | `active` | Ops publishes | Name, slug, visibility set; `kind=marketplace_category` requires paired §4.4.7 row in `active` | Node becomes resolvable; downstream caches bust |
| `active` | `deprecated` | Ops deprecates | `deprecation_action` set; if `redirect_to_successor`, `successor_id` set and in `active` state | Public paths honor `deprecation_action`; derived pages archived per each page type's state machine |
| `active` | `merged` | Ops merges | `successor_id` set; merge worker has completed FK-reassignment from this node to successor | No further writes accepted; reads resolve via successor |
| `deprecated` | `active` | Ops reactivates | Within 30 days of deprecation; successor not yet used for FK migration | Reverses redirects; downstream caches bust |
| `draft` | `deleted_at` (soft) | Ops deletes | Zero referencing rows | Only valid from `draft` |

**Merge Workflow.** Merging collapses a Taxonomy Node into its `successor_id`. The merge worker (Convex background job, rate-limited per §31 retry-curve class `taxonomy_merge`) rewrites FKs on all referencing entities (Capability Declaration, Seller Profile industries, Marketplace Listing filters, Controlled-Vocabulary Tag, HeatMapCell facet references) atomically in batches of 500 with bounded lag SLO of 10 minutes for the full merge. Rollback is supported up to the point at which the source node transitions to `merged`; after that, merge is irreversible (new successor merge would be required to undo).

**Retention.** Life of platform. Soft-deleted `draft` rows purged 30 days after soft-delete. `deprecated` and `merged` nodes retained indefinitely to preserve historical FK integrity and redirect continuity. DSAR: not applicable (no PII). Residency: taxonomy served from global edge cache; per-row `residency_scope` only controls whether downstream analytics are admissible to a residency-scoped report, not where the row itself is stored.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Seller-proposed value collides with existing node across kinds.** A proposed capability tag "Kubernetes" could collide with an existing `kind=integration_vendor` row of the same name. Resolved: uniqueness is scoped to `(kind, slug)`, not globally; collision on the `name` field across kinds is allowed but surfaces an Ops advisory note during review.
2. **Ops deletes a taxonomy node still FK-referenced by a soft-deleted row.** The delete check MUST consider only non-soft-deleted referencing rows. A soft-deleted referencing row whose deletion window still covers the taxonomy delete creates a dangling FK on un-delete; resolved by requiring soft-delete recovery to re-validate taxonomy references and fail with `taxonomy_reference_dangling` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409) if the node has been hard-purged.
3. **Merge worker crashes mid-batch.** FK rewrites are performed in idempotent batches keyed by `(source_node_id, successor_node_id, batch_sequence)`; restarted workers resume at the next unprocessed batch. Bounded-lag SLO is 10 minutes; exceeding 10 minutes emits `taxonomy.merge.slo_breach` alert to Ops.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a Taxonomy Node with `kind=marketplace_category` without a paired §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row in the same transaction MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_marketplace_category_projection_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
2. Creating a Taxonomy Node whose `slug` already exists for the same `kind` (case-insensitive) MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_node_slug_conflict` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
3. Deprecating a Taxonomy Node without populating `deprecation_action` MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_node_deprecation_action_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
4. Deprecating with `deprecation_action=redirect_to_successor` without a `successor_id` in `active` state MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_node_successor_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
5. Attempting to soft-delete a Taxonomy Node with ≥ 1 active referencing row (any consumer entity) MUST be rejected with error `taxonomy_node_delete_blocked_by_references` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); error payload includes per-consumer reference count.
6. Resolving a `deprecated` node with `deprecation_action=redirect_to_successor` on any public path MUST 301-redirect to the successor; chain depth MUST NOT exceed 3 hops — the 4th hop MUST return 410 Gone with a canonical fallback to the root Marketplace index.
7. Downstream cache invalidation (for consumers Controlled-Vocabulary Tag, Capability Declaration indexes, Seller Profile filters, HeatMapCell facets, CategoryPage/GuidePage/ComparisonPage caches, Market Intelligence Report materialized views) MUST fire within 60s of the Taxonomy Node `updated_at` bump, observable via the `taxonomy.node.updated` webhook (authored in Phase 4).
8. Merging Node A into Node B MUST rewrite all referencing-row FKs within 10 minutes; merge progress is observable via the Ops Taxonomy CMS dashboard with per-batch sequence indicator; SLO breach emits `taxonomy.merge.slo_breach`.
9. A buyer-console or seller-console write attempt against any Taxonomy Node CRUD endpoint MUST receive HTTP 403 with `taxonomy_node_write_forbidden` (new; Appendix I); read attempts receive the row if `visibility=public` and `state ∈ {active, deprecated}`, otherwise HTTP 404.

### 4.5.5 Controlled-Vocabulary Tag (Marketplace-Domain, Ops-Moderated, Seller-Proposable) {#4.5.5-controlled-vocabulary-tag}

**Authoring Intent.** Controlled-Vocabulary Tag represents the individual, seller-referenceable tag values attached to Capability Declarations, Marketplace Listings, Seller Profiles, and SoftwarePage structured data. Tags are finer-grained than Taxonomy Nodes: a Taxonomy Node represents a taxonomy dimension (e.g., `kind=capability_category`, slug `security_compliance`), while a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag represents an individual published value under a dimension (e.g., "SAML SSO", "SCIM Provisioning"). Per Summary C.60, sellers cannot author free-form tags; they MAY propose new tags via the tag proposal workflow (§27.6), which routes to the `ops_marketing_editor` moderation queue, but tags only become referenceable once Ops approves them. Approved tags are append-only to the published set; tag retirement happens via deprecation (not delete) with successor pointer, identical semantics to Taxonomy Node.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (platform-scoped; no `org_id`; global vocabulary). Read access public for `state ∈ {approved, deprecated}`. Write access: sellers MAY insert rows in `state=submitted` via the proposal API; state transitions beyond `submitted` are Ops-only (`ops_marketing_editor` or `ops_taxonomy_admin`). Buyers have read-only access.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `taxonomy_node_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Taxonomy Node (§4.5.4) | Must be `kind` in the allowed set for Controlled-Vocabulary Tag (see `taxonomy_dimension`) and in `state=active` at write |
| `taxonomy_dimension` | Enum | See Appendix J `vocab_tag_taxonomy_dimension`: `capability_category`, `industry`, `certification`, `integration_vendor`, `language`, `region` | Denormalized from Taxonomy Node.kind for indexing; application enforces match |
| `slug` | String | 3–80 chars, lowercase, `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, unique within `taxonomy_dimension` | URL segment (case-insensitive-unique) |
| `display_name` | String | 1–100 chars | Seller-visible label |
| `canonical_form` | String | 1–100 chars | Ops-canonicalized form; seller proposals are normalized at moderation time |
| `short_description` | String | 0–400 chars | Hover-tooltip text in editor; editorial tone |
| `long_description` | String | 0–4000 chars | Public page body for any derived `/tags/:slug` surface (future) |
| `aliases` | Array[String] | Max 30 items, each 1–80 chars | Synonyms and common misspellings for search indexing |
| `origin` | Enum | See Appendix J `vocab_tag_origin`: `ops_authored`, `seller_proposed`, `imported_from_seed` | Attribution |
| `proposing_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Organization (Seller) | Populated only when `origin=seller_proposed` |
| `proposing_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User | Populated only when `origin=seller_proposed` |
| `proposal_rationale` | String | 0–1000 chars, nullable | Seller-supplied justification at proposal time |
| `state` | Enum | See Appendix J `vocab_tag_proposal_status`: `submitted`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `merged_into_existing`, `withdrawn` | See State Machine below. `approved` is the only state in which a Capability Declaration may reference this tag |
| `rejection_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `vocab_tag_rejection_reason`: `duplicate_of_existing`, `too_specific_to_product`, `too_broad`, `not_generalizable`, `policy_violation`, `insufficient_definition` | Required when `state=rejected` |
| `rejection_note` | String | 0–1000 chars, nullable | Ops note back to the proposer; surfaced in seller notification |
| `merged_into_tag_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Controlled-Vocabulary Tag | Required when `state=merged_into_existing` |
| `deprecated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated on transition out of `approved` to a retirement state |
| `successor_tag_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Controlled-Vocabulary Tag | Used for deprecation-with-successor (distinct from `merged_into_tag_id`: merge is moderation-time; successor is retirement-time) |
| `visibility` | Enum | See Appendix J `taxonomy_node_visibility` (reused): `public`, `internal_ops_only` | Pre-release tags may be `internal_ops_only` during curation |
| `version` | Integer | ≥ 1, auto-incremented on Ops edit after `approved` | Used for cache-bust |
| `reference_count_cache` | Integer | ≥ 0; denormalized | Refreshed nightly; informational (not authoritative) |
| `submitted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When seller submitted proposal |
| `reviewed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When Ops decisioned |
| `reviewed_by` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User | Ops reviewer |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID (Seller for proposal, Ops for direct authoring) | Creator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; only valid from `state ∈ {rejected, withdrawn}` |

**Indexes.** `(taxonomy_dimension, slug)` unique, `(taxonomy_node_id, state)`, `(state, submitted_at)` for the Ops review queue, `(origin, proposing_org_id)`, GIN on `aliases`, `(merged_into_tag_id)` partial where not null, `(successor_tag_id)` partial where not null.

**Scope Isolation.** Controlled-Vocabulary Tag rows are global once `state=approved`. A seller submitting a proposal creates a row with `state=submitted` and `visibility=internal_ops_only`; the row is visible to the submitting Org only until it reaches `approved`. Buyer-console reads only return rows with `state=approved` AND `visibility=public`. Seller-console reads return rows with `state=approved` OR `(state ∈ {submitted, in_review, rejected, withdrawn} AND proposing_org_id = session.org_id)`. Ops sees all rows. Cross-Org read attempts on another Org's submitted proposal MUST return HTTP 404 (not 403); error `vocab_tag_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404).

**Sellers-Cannot-Create-Freeform-Tags Rule Enforcement.** Any write to Capability Declaration, Marketplace Listing filter, Seller Profile industries/certifications, or SoftwarePage structured data that includes a tag value NOT in `(state=approved AND visibility=public)` at the time of write MUST be rejected with error `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). The error payload includes the rejected tag string and, if a close-match approved tag exists (Levenshtein ≤ 2), a "did you mean" suggestion. This rule is enforced uniformly at the write layer, not in the UI; direct API clients receive the same rejection.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `submitted` | Seller proposes | Tag string, dimension, rationale all supplied; no exact-match duplicate; proposing org is Seller with ≥ 1 published Capability Declaration | Seller | Row created; routed to Ops review queue |
| (init) | `approved` | Ops authors directly | All fields valid; no exact-match duplicate | Ops | `origin=ops_authored`; effective immediately |
| `submitted` | `in_review` | Ops picks up | Ops assigns to self | Ops | Review timer started (5-business-day SLA) |
| `in_review` | `approved` | Ops approves | All fields valid; canonicalization done; aliases set | Ops | Available to all sellers; proposing org notified |
| `in_review` | `rejected` | Ops rejects | `rejection_reason` set; rejection note optional | Ops | Seller notified with reason and (if applicable) suggested alternative approved tag |
| `in_review` | `merged_into_existing` | Ops merges | `merged_into_tag_id` set (target must be `approved`); proposing org notified | Ops | Row becomes a non-canonical alias entry for the target |
| `submitted` | `withdrawn` | Proposing seller withdraws | Proposing seller explicit action | Seller | Irreversible; Ops review ended |
| `approved` | `deprecated` | Ops deprecates | `deprecated_at` set; `successor_tag_id` set (or null if hard retire) | Ops | Existing Capability Declaration references migrate via §4.5.4 merge worker semantics |
| `deprecated` | `approved` | Ops reactivates | Within 30 days of deprecation | Ops | Reverses deprecation |
| `rejected` | `deleted_at` (soft) | Ops soft-deletes | Audit-retention window expired (180 days) | Ops | Only valid from `rejected` or `withdrawn` |

**Retention.** `approved` and `deprecated` rows retained for life of platform (FK integrity). `submitted`, `in_review`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, and `merged_into_existing` rows retained for 180 days after terminal state; after that, soft-deletable. DSAR: the seller-supplied `proposal_rationale` is treated as org-level content and purged alongside Org deletion; `proposing_user_id` is cleared (set to a synthetic anonymous-Ops UUID) on user DSAR erasure, preserving audit semantics.

**Review SLA.** 5 business days from `submitted` → `in_review` → terminal decision. Ops dashboard shows per-reviewer queue depth and age. Breach of the 5-business-day SLA emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` (authored in Phase 4) and pages `ops_marketing_editor` on-call.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Seller proposes a tag that already has an approved near-duplicate.** Resolved: Ops moderation flow displays candidate matches (Levenshtein, embedding similarity) and offers `merged_into_existing` as a one-click disposition; proposing seller is notified with the canonical tag.
2. **Seller uses an approved tag that Ops subsequently deprecates.** Resolved: Capability Declaration references to the deprecated tag are migrated by the merge worker to the successor (or retained if `hard_retire`) with provenance preserved in Capability Declaration's audit log. Sellers receive notification of affected declarations.
3. **Direct API client attempts to use a tag string that is not approved.** Resolved: write layer enforces `consumer_requires_approved_tag` at every consumer entity's write path, not at UI layer. Error payload includes suggested approved tag when similarity ≥ 0.85.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A seller without at least one `published` Capability Declaration attempting to propose a new tag MUST be rejected with `vocab_tag_proposer_ineligible` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
2. A seller proposal whose canonicalized slug collides with an `approved` tag in the same dimension MUST be auto-rejected with `vocab_tag_duplicate_of_existing` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409), surfacing the approved tag id and slug in the error payload; the proposing seller is invited to use the approved tag directly.
3. An Ops approval MUST fire `vocab_tag.approved` webhook (authored in Phase 4) with payload including `taxonomy_dimension`, `slug`, `display_name`, `proposing_org_id`, and `reviewed_by`.
4. Any seller or buyer attempting to write to any consumer entity (Capability Declaration, Marketplace Listing filter, Seller Profile industries/certifications, SoftwarePage structured data) with a tag value not in `(state=approved AND visibility=public)` MUST be rejected with `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
5. The Ops review SLA (5 business days) MUST be observable via the Ops dashboard; breach emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` and pages the editorial on-call.
6. Deprecating an `approved` tag with `successor_tag_id` set MUST migrate all consumer-row references within 10 minutes; SLO breach emits `vocab_tag.deprecation_slo_breach`.
7. A buyer-console session reading the `/vocab/tags/proposals` endpoint MUST receive HTTP 403 with `vocab_tag_buyer_access_forbidden` (new; Appendix I).
8. `reference_count_cache` MUST be within ± 5% of the authoritative count at any point (refreshed by nightly worker); UI displays the cached value with a "refreshed N hours ago" hint.

### 4.5.6 Vendor Opt-Out Record — Marketplace-Domain Read & Render Contract (Cross-Reference to §4.4.8) {#4.5.6-vendor-opt-out-record-marketplace-domain}

**Authoring Intent.** The authoritative Vendor Opt-Out Record entity is defined in §4.4.8 (seller-origin, platform-honored). This subsection exists to consolidate the marketplace-domain read and rendering contract in one place so consumers of §4.5 (Marketplace Listing, EOI Record, NDA Record, Marketplace Abuse Report, EOI Acceptance Record, M2 Public Selection Report, M9 Category Page, M10 Guide Page, M11 Comparison Page, M12 Market Intelligence Report, M13 Heat Map, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, and any future marketplace-domain consumer) have a single reference point for the rules. Per Summary C.123, opt-outs are global, retroactive, and honored across all Orgs and all Sourcera-owned public-facing mechanics.

**This subsection does NOT duplicate the entity schema.** The field table, state machine, and write-side acceptance criteria remain in §4.4.8. This subsection authors only the marketplace-domain read/render contract and adds the acceptance criteria that govern marketplace-domain consumers, not opt-out authoring.

**Read/Render Contract.** Every marketplace-domain render path (public HTML, public JSON, Schema.org payload, RSS/sitemap, `/api/public/*`, internal analytics export to derived pages) MUST execute the following precondition pipeline before emitting any row identifying a Seller Org or a SellerSoftware:

1. **Snapshot Acquisition.** Acquire a Vendor Opt-Out snapshot ≤ 60 seconds old. Older snapshots are refused; the render path MUST re-fetch. Snapshot is cached in the edge layer with TTL 60 seconds.
2. **Scope Match.** For each identifying row candidate (Seller Org id, SellerSoftware id, Marketplace Category id, page type, specific page id), resolve the set of matching Vendor Opt-Out rows via the scope-resolution function defined in §4.4.8 (which honors `scope_kind`, `scope_ref_type`, `scope_ref_id`, and `page_type_filter`).
3. **Redaction Decision.** If any matching opt-out row has `ops_review_status ∈ {auto_honored, approved}` AND `effective_from ≤ now` AND no `revoked_at`, emit a "Vendor opted out" redaction placeholder instead of the identifying row. Redaction placeholder is a stable, deterministic token that preserves layout integrity (e.g., Comparison Page emits an "Opted out" column rather than collapsing the column).
4. **Schema.org Builder.** The Schema.org serializer MUST receive a suppressed-ids list and omit those `Product` and `Organization` nodes entirely from structured data (not just blank them); QA test asserts this.
5. **Partial Opt-Out.** If an opt-out targets a specific page type (e.g., `scope_kind=page_type`, `page_type_filter=comparison_page`), the render contract applies only to that page type; other page types still render normally.

**Cache-Bust on Write.** On any write to §4.4.8 that transitions a row into or out of an effective state (create with `auto_honored`, approve, revoke, apply retro backfill complete), the `vendor_opt_out.applied` or `vendor_opt_out.revoked` webhook (authored in Phase 4) fires a fan-out to invalidate edge caches for every referenced page type within 15 minutes. The cache-bust payload contains the minimal invalidation keys (Org id, SellerSoftware id, Marketplace Category id, page type, specific page id) needed to target the affected pages.

**Retroactive Sweep.** When an opt-out with `retro_backfill_status=pending` is persisted, a retroactive sweep worker enumerates every already-published marketplace-domain page that references the opted-out entity and re-renders each with the new contract. Sweep progress is tracked on the §4.4.8 row (`retro_backfill_status` transitions `pending → in_progress → complete` or `failed`). SLO: 15 minutes from opt-out persist to `retro_backfill_status=complete` for global scope; longer for `page_type` scope when page count exceeds 10,000 (the worker batches in groups of 500 with bounded rate-limit per §31 retry-curve class `retroactive_sweep`).

**Consumer-Specific Redaction Rules.**

| Consumer | Redaction Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Marketplace Listing (§4.5.1) | If `seller_profile.org_id` has `scope_kind=global` opt-out with `effective_from ≤ now`, listing is de-listed from public browse; direct-link resolution returns HTTP 410 Gone with a canonical fallback to the listing's Marketplace Category page |
| EOI Record (§4.5.2), NDA Record (§4.5.3), EOI Acceptance Record (§4.5.8) | Opt-outs do NOT suppress EOI/NDA/acceptance records themselves — these are buyer-side private records; opt-outs govern marketplace-domain public mechanics only |
| Marketplace Abuse Report (§4.5.7) | Opt-outs do NOT suppress abuse reports or the report flow; the report subject identity is preserved for Ops review and appeal |
| CategoryPage (§4.4.12), GuidePage (§4.4.13), ComparisonPage (§4.4.14) | Opted-out entities are redacted per the render contract above; Schema.org cache rebuilt |
| MarketIntelligenceReport (§4.4.15), HeatMapCell (§4.4.16) | Opted-out entities are EXCLUDED from the underlying signal cohort at computation time; if exclusion drops cohort below k-anonymity floor, the report cell is suppressed and the next scheduled refresh re-evaluates |
| SellerOrgPage (§4.4.10), SoftwarePage (§4.4.11) | Opted-out entity's own page MUST render `410 Gone` with canonical to Marketplace root; SEO `noindex` applied; sitemap entry removed |
| M2 Public Selection Report (§43) | Opted-out vendor's name redacted to "Vendor Opted Out" with no other identifying info; buyer is notified at render time that their Selection Report contains redactions |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Race: a render begins before opt-out persist, completes after.** Resolved: 60-second snapshot TTL + 15-minute retroactive cache-bust SLO; render consumers MUST NOT cache opt-out snapshots older than 60 seconds.
2. **Partial fan-out fails mid-invalidation.** Resolved: cache-bust webhook fan-out uses Appendix F retry curve (exponential backoff, DLQ after 5 failures); un-invalidated pages are caught by the nightly reconciliation sweep.
3. **Opt-out targeting a hard-purged entity.** Resolved in §4.4.8: the opt-out transitions to `revoked` with reason `scope_target_purged`. Render contract: reads of the purged target return HTTP 410 regardless of opt-out state.
4. **Opt-out breaks a Comparison Page to below-minimum vendor count.** Resolved: ComparisonPage (§4.4.14) has minimum vendor count check; below threshold, the page archives and returns 410 with canonical fallback to the Comparison Index.

**Acceptance Criteria (Marketplace-Domain-Specific; §4.4.8 Acceptance Criteria remain in force for authoring).**

1. No marketplace-domain render path MAY emit an identifying row for an opted-out Seller Org or SellerSoftware more than 15 minutes after an `auto_honored` or `approved` opt-out takes effect. Violation is a P1 data-integrity bug.
2. Schema.org payloads MUST omit opted-out entities entirely (not blank); QA test `schema_org_opt_out_omission` asserts this for ComparisonPage, CategoryPage, SoftwarePage, SellerOrgPage.
3. Any marketplace-domain JSON endpoint that returns a collection of Seller Orgs or SellerSoftware MUST apply the render contract at serialization time; a dedicated acceptance test `vendor_opt_out_marketplace_collection_redaction` asserts this against 5 canonical endpoint paths.
4. Retroactive sweep SLO: global-scope opt-outs MUST reach `retro_backfill_status=complete` within 15 minutes for seller Orgs with ≤ 10,000 referenced pages; ≤ 60 minutes for up to 100,000; > 100,000 pages allowed up to 4 hours with an explicit Ops-visible progress bar.
5. A new Marketplace Abuse Report whose subject is an opted-out SellerOrgPage or SoftwarePage MUST NOT be rejected — the report form accepts the subject via id (not URL crawl) and the rendered subject metadata is redacted in the buyer-visible confirmation screen but retained in Ops view.

### 4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report (Marketplace-Domain) {#4.5.7-marketplace-abuse-report}

**Authoring Intent.** Marketplace Abuse Report formalizes the abuse-escalation workflow referenced in §45.3 with a first-class entity, auditable state machine, and appeal/closure paths. Per §45.3, buyers (and other report-eligible actors) can report a Marketplace Listing as spam, fraud, harmful, competitor sabotage, or otherwise policy-violating. This entity carries the report through Ops triage, seller appeal, and final disposition. The entity is distinct from §4.6.1 Audit Event (which records the actions taken on the report); the Abuse Report is the first-class, queryable business object, while Audit Events record every transition on it.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (platform-scoped; no `org_id` on the record itself, though it carries `reporter_org_id` and `subject_org_id` for routing and notification). Read access: Ops always; reporter can read their own reports (read-only, limited fields); subject Seller Org can read reports filed against them once the report reaches `awaiting_seller_response` (redacted fields per below). Write access: reporter creates; Ops triages and decisions; subject Seller submits appeal only.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `reporter_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_reporter_kind`: `buyer_user`, `seller_user`, `anonymous_public`, `ops_internal`, `automated_signal` | Who filed |
| `reporter_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User | Populated unless `reporter_kind=anonymous_public` or `automated_signal` |
| `reporter_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Organization | Populated for `buyer_user` and `seller_user` reporter kinds |
| `reporter_ip_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | For `anonymous_public`, stored as a one-way hash (rate-limit key); NEVER stored in clear |
| `reporter_contact_email` | String | Nullable; valid email | Optional for `anonymous_public` (for follow-up); PII subject to DSAR |
| `subject_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_subject_kind`: `marketplace_listing`, `seller_org_page`, `software_page`, `category_page`, `comparison_page`, `guide_page`, `capability_declaration`, `eoi_message`, `vendor_response_excerpt` | What is being reported |
| `subject_id` | UUID | FK (polymorphic; application-validated per `subject_kind`) | Target entity id |
| `subject_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Organization | Seller Org being reported; null for sourcera-owned page kinds |
| `subject_snapshot_json` | JSON | ≤ 32000 chars | Immutable snapshot of the subject content at report time; survives subsequent subject edits/deletes |
| `reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_reason`: `spam`, `fraud`, `harmful_content`, `competitor_sabotage`, `misleading_claims`, `trademark_infringement`, `impersonation`, `off_platform_solicitation`, `other` | Primary reason |
| `secondary_reasons` | Array[Enum] | Same enum; ≤ 5 | Secondary reasons for multi-factor reports |
| `report_narrative` | String | 10–4000 chars | Reporter-supplied description |
| `evidence_attachments` | Array[UUID] | Max 10 files; each ≤ 25MB; FK → Convex Storage | Screenshots, emails, links |
| `severity` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_severity`: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | Ops-assigned; defaults to `medium` at create, updated at triage |
| `ops_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_ops_status`: `pending_review`, `awaiting_seller_response`, `upheld`, `dismissed`, `escalated`, `auto_closed_no_appeal` | See State Machine below |
| `ops_assigned_to_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Ops User | Ops reviewer |
| `ops_assigned_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Triage start |
| `ops_decided_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Terminal decision time |
| `ops_decision_note` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-facing rationale; NOT shared with reporter or subject |
| `ops_decision_public_note` | String | 0–2000 chars, nullable | Reporter- and subject-facing summary; shared verbatim in notifications |
| `sla_breach_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated if Ops exceeded the 24-hour triage SLA |
| `appeal_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `abuse_report_appeal_status`: `not_filed`, `submitted`, `in_review`, `upheld`, `overturned` | Seller appeal state |
| `appeal_submitted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `appeal_deadline_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | 7 days from `awaiting_seller_response` transition; enforced; `expired` transitions to `auto_closed_no_appeal` |
| `appeal_narrative` | String | 0–4000 chars, nullable | Seller rebuttal |
| `appeal_evidence_attachments` | Array[UUID] | Max 10 files; each ≤ 25MB | |
| `appeal_decided_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `appeal_decision_note` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-facing |
| `closure_disposition` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `abuse_report_closure_disposition`: `listing_hidden`, `listing_delisted`, `seller_warned`, `seller_banned`, `no_action`, `duplicate_of_prior_report` | Required on terminal Ops status `{upheld, dismissed, auto_closed_no_appeal}` |
| `duplicate_of_report_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Marketplace Abuse Report | Populated when `closure_disposition=duplicate_of_prior_report` |
| `ban_scope` | Enum | Nullable; `listing_level`, `software_level`, `org_level_all_consoles` | Required when `closure_disposition=seller_banned` |
| `subject_effect_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Time at which the closure disposition took effect on the subject (e.g., listing hidden) |
| `reporter_notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `subject_notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID (or synthetic "automated_signal_user" for `reporter_kind=automated_signal`) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; only valid via Ops GDPR-right-to-erasure path |

**Indexes.** `(ops_status, severity, created_at)` for the Ops queue, `(subject_org_id, ops_status)` for the subject-side view, `(reporter_org_id, created_at DESC)` for the reporter-side history, `(duplicate_of_report_id)` partial, `(subject_kind, subject_id)` for duplicate detection, `(appeal_deadline_at)` partial where state demands timer.

**Scope Isolation.** Reporter reads are scoped to `reporter_org_id` and `reporter_user_id`. Subject reads are scoped to `subject_org_id` AND `ops_status ∈ {awaiting_seller_response, upheld, dismissed, auto_closed_no_appeal}` with `ops_decision_note` redacted to `ops_decision_public_note` only. Ops sees all fields. `reporter_contact_email` and `reporter_ip_hash` are NEVER exposed to the subject. `subject_snapshot_json` is redacted on reporter read (only the fields they authored are returned); full snapshot is available to Ops and the subject's Org Owner only.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending_review` | Report filed | Reporter passes rate limit; subject exists and is not already hard-purged | Any eligible reporter | Routed to Ops queue with severity default |
| `pending_review` | `awaiting_seller_response` | Ops confirms report warrants subject notice | Severity assigned; `ops_decision_public_note` drafted | Ops | Subject notified; `appeal_deadline_at` set to now + 7 days; subject content hidden if severity=high/critical, not hidden otherwise |
| `pending_review` | `dismissed` | Ops dismisses outright | `closure_disposition ∈ {no_action, duplicate_of_prior_report}`; `ops_decision_public_note` drafted | Ops | Reporter notified; subject not notified |
| `pending_review` | `upheld` | Ops upholds without seller response (clear-cut cases: banned content, known fraud signature, court order) | `closure_disposition ∈ {listing_hidden, listing_delisted, seller_warned, seller_banned}`; `ops_decision_public_note` drafted; severity ≥ `high` | Ops (dual sign-off required when `seller_banned`) | Subject and reporter notified |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `upheld` | Appeal in, Ops upholds original | `appeal_status=submitted` → `in_review` → `upheld`; `appeal_decision_note` drafted | Ops | Subject and reporter notified |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `dismissed` | Appeal in, Ops overturns | `appeal_status` → `overturned`; closure `no_action`; subject content restored if previously hidden | Ops | Subject and reporter notified |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `auto_closed_no_appeal` | Deadline expired | `appeal_deadline_at < now`; no appeal filed | System | Closure disposition defaults to the one Ops pre-registered at `awaiting_seller_response` entry (typically `listing_hidden`); subject notified |
| `pending_review` or `awaiting_seller_response` | `escalated` | Ops escalates | Manual Ops action; pattern of repeated reports against same subject; severity transition to `critical` | Ops | Escalation routes to Sourcera management; ban consideration |
| `escalated` | `upheld` | Management decision | Dual-signoff; `closure_disposition=seller_banned` with `ban_scope` set | Ops leadership | Permanent; irreversible without Ops leadership action |
| `escalated` | `dismissed` | Management decision | `closure_disposition=no_action` | Ops leadership | |
| `upheld`, `dismissed`, `auto_closed_no_appeal` | `deleted_at` (soft) | GDPR right-to-erasure | Reporter or subject DSAR, approved by DPO | Ops (DPO) | Limited redaction; see Retention below |

**Rate Limiting.** Reporters are rate-limited on create per §32.4: `buyer_user`/`seller_user` → 20 reports per rolling 24 hours per Org; `anonymous_public` → 5 reports per rolling 24 hours per `reporter_ip_hash`; `automated_signal` → no limit but requires service-account auth. Exceeding rate limit returns HTTP 429 with `abuse_report_rate_limited` (new; Appendix I).

**Duplicate Detection.** A new report whose `(subject_kind, subject_id, reason)` tuple matches an existing report in `ops_status ∈ {pending_review, awaiting_seller_response}` is auto-linked via `duplicate_of_report_id` and routed to the same Ops reviewer; the original report is updated (severity may escalate on multiplicity). The new report still enters the system (not silently dropped) so reporters see acknowledgment and can track disposition.

**Appeal Workflow.** Subject seller receives email notification with magic-link to a signed-in appeal form (no public-URL appeal to prevent impersonation). Appeal form shows the `ops_decision_public_note`, reason(s), redacted subject snapshot, and reporter_narrative with PII redacted. Subject submits `appeal_narrative` and optional `appeal_evidence_attachments` within 7 days. On submission, `appeal_status → submitted`; Ops SLA to decision is 24 business hours.

**Retention.** Open (`pending_review`, `awaiting_seller_response`, `escalated`) reports retained indefinitely until closure. Closed (`upheld`, `dismissed`, `auto_closed_no_appeal`) reports retained for 3 years post-closure for legal/compliance/audit. GDPR right-to-erasure: on reporter DSAR, `reporter_user_id`, `reporter_contact_email`, and `reporter_ip_hash` are redacted to synthetic anonymized values; the report record itself is preserved. On subject DSAR (Org deletion), `subject_org_id` is redacted to null, `subject_snapshot_json` reduced to reason-only metadata, and the record transitions to `deleted_at` after 3-year retention window satisfied. Residency: report contents stored per the Org's residency assignment (reporter-side residency) and replicated to Ops for triage only; cross-residency triage requires DPO approval.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Subject hard-purged during an open report.** Resolved: `subject_snapshot_json` preserves content at report time; the report can still reach terminal Ops decision even if the original subject is gone.
2. **Coordinated false-flag campaign against a competitor.** Resolved: rate limits per reporter_org_id; duplicate detection groups related reports; Ops review of reporter patterns; Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) alerts on anomalous reporter velocity or reporter-org clustering.
3. **Seller receives notification via email, magic link intercepted.** Resolved: magic-link requires logged-in session match to the subject_org_id user with `seller_org_admin` role; unauthenticated magic-link click routes to sign-in; magic links expire at `appeal_deadline_at`.
4. **Ops decision reverses after subject took restorative action.** Resolved: `awaiting_seller_response → dismissed` path restores subject content (un-hides listing); reversal audit-logged; subject notified.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A Marketplace Abuse Report MUST be filed via POST from an authenticated buyer, seller, Ops, or rate-limited anonymous session; rate-limit breach MUST return HTTP 429 with `abuse_report_rate_limited`.
2. The Ops 24-hour triage SLA MUST be measured from `created_at` to the first transition out of `pending_review`; SLA breach stamps `sla_breach_at` and emits `abuse_report.sla_breach` webhook (authored in Phase 4).
3. Subject notification on `awaiting_seller_response` MUST be sent within 5 minutes; `appeal_deadline_at` MUST be exactly 7 days after the transition.
4. Appeal submitted after `appeal_deadline_at` MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_appeal_expired` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 410).
5. Closure disposition `seller_banned` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` MUST require dual sign-off (two Ops users with `ops_content_admin` role); single-signoff attempts MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_ban_requires_dual_signoff` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
6. On closure `upheld` with `closure_disposition=listing_hidden`, the subject's listing MUST transition to `hidden` in the `marketplace_listing_status` enum within 60 seconds and SEO noindex applied.
7. Subject read of a report MUST NEVER include `reporter_user_id`, `reporter_contact_email`, `reporter_ip_hash`, `ops_decision_note`, or `ops_assigned_to_user_id`; QA test `abuse_report_subject_redaction` asserts this.
8. Duplicate reports MUST be linked via `duplicate_of_report_id` within 10 seconds of creation; reporter acknowledgement includes the link-to-original notice.
9. Vendor Opt-Out for the subject MUST NOT suppress the Abuse Report flow; Ops can view the full `subject_snapshot_json` regardless of subject opt-out state.

### 4.5.8 EOI Acceptance Record (Marketplace-Domain) {#4.5.8-eoi-acceptance-record}

**Authoring Intent.** EOI Acceptance Record formalizes the one-click EOI acceptance flow referenced in Summary C.62 and §27.5. The existing §4.5.2 EOI Record captures the seller-submitted Expression of Interest; this entity captures the buyer-side acceptance event — the decision moment at which an EOI transitions from a candidate into the Phase 4–5 vendor shortlist, and the audit trail of that decision (who, when, from what surface, with what Capability Declaration verification, with what follow-on actions). Separating the acceptance record from the EOI Record preserves the EOI as the seller-authored artifact while making the buyer-side acceptance independently queryable, auditable, and bulk-actionable.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (crosses the buyer-seller boundary: the acceptance originates in the buyer console, materializes a shortlist entry on the buyer side, and sends a notification to the seller). Scope constants: `buyer_org_id` + `workspace_id` scope the acceptance to a specific Buyer Workspace; `eoi_record_id` links back to the seller-authored EOI. Read access: buyer Workspace members per workspace RBAC; seller via the originating Seller Org (limited fields — `acceptance_action`, `accepted_at`, and the resulting Bid Workspace id). Ops sees all.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `eoi_record_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → EOI Record (§4.5.2); unique | 1:1 with the EOI Record; a given EOI has at most one acceptance record |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization (Buyer) | For scope isolation |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace | Workspace scope |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization (Seller) | Denormalized for query efficiency |
| `seller_profile_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Seller Profile | Denormalized |
| `marketplace_listing_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Marketplace Listing (§4.5.1) | The listing under which the EOI was submitted |
| `acceptance_action` | Enum | See Appendix J `eoi_acceptance_action`: `accept_to_shortlist`, `accept_to_nda_prep`, `accept_and_skip_nda`, `accept_with_conditions` | Determines downstream workflow |
| `acceptance_conditions` | String | 0–2000 chars; required when `acceptance_action=accept_with_conditions` | Free-text conditions surfaced to seller in notification |
| `referenced_capability_declaration_ids` | Array[UUID] | Max 50; FK → Capability Declaration | Subset of seller-declared capabilities the buyer validated at acceptance time; immutable after write |
| `capability_match_method` | Enum | See Appendix J `eoi_acceptance_cap_decl_match_method`: `manual_selection`, `auto_match_all_declared`, `match_score_threshold` | How the buyer selected the capability list |
| `match_score_threshold_value` | Integer | 0–100, nullable | Required only when `capability_match_method=match_score_threshold` |
| `match_score_at_acceptance` | Integer | 0–100, nullable | Snapshot of the computed Marketplace Match Score (§27.4) at acceptance time; null if the buyer plan tier does not expose numeric scoring |
| `source_surface` | Enum | See Appendix J `eoi_acceptance_source_surface`: `eoi_queue`, `marketplace_search_result`, `bulk_accept_queue`, `api` | Where the buyer clicked accept |
| `bulk_accept_batch_id` | UUID | Nullable | Correlates multi-accept actions from the `bulk_accept_queue` surface; max 25 accepts per batch |
| `resulting_target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Target Account | Materialized shortlist entry; 1:1 |
| `resulting_bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Bid Workspace | Populated when `acceptance_action=accept_and_skip_nda` (NDA skipped); otherwise populated on NDA execution via §4.5.3 |
| `nda_required` | Boolean | Computed | Derived from `acceptance_action`; `accept_to_nda_prep` → true; `accept_and_skip_nda` → false; `accept_to_shortlist` → per buyer Org default; `accept_with_conditions` → per condition |
| `nda_record_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → NDA Record (§4.5.3) | Populated when NDA is executed |
| `console_bridge_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Console Bridge Event (§4.7.1) | The bridge event that propagated the acceptance into the seller's Bid Workspace namespace |
| `acceptance_reversal_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-ref → EOI Acceptance Record | If an acceptance is reversed, a reversal record is created (append-only); pointer from reversal to original. Original's `reversed_by_acceptance_id` (below) points back |
| `reversed_by_acceptance_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-ref | Pointer to reversal record |
| `reversal_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `buyer_changed_mind`, `seller_ineligible`, `duplicate_acceptance`, `policy_violation` | Required on reversal |
| `accepted_at` | Timestamp | Immutable; UTC | Decision moment |
| `accepted_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User | Who clicked accept |
| `accepted_by_role_snapshot` | Enum | See Appendix J (workspace_roles): `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`, `guest` | Role at acceptance time (frozen for audit) |
| `notification_seller_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Seller notification dispatch |
| `notification_buyer_team_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Buyer-side team notification dispatch |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC (alias of `accepted_at` for schema consistency) |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC (only updated on reversal or NDA linkage) |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Alias of `accepted_by_user_id` |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete only via Ops GDPR-right-to-erasure path; reversal is the normal inverse operation |

**Indexes.** `(eoi_record_id)` unique, `(buyer_workspace_id, accepted_at DESC)`, `(seller_org_id, accepted_at DESC)`, `(bulk_accept_batch_id)` partial, `(resulting_target_account_id)` unique partial, `(acceptance_reversal_id)` partial, `(reversed_by_acceptance_id)` partial, `(source_surface, accepted_at DESC)` for Ops analytics.

**Scope Isolation.** Writes: only a buyer-console session with Workspace role ∈ `{workspace_owner, workspace_admin, use_case_lead (Phase 3 only)}` and Phase ∈ `{phase_3_vendor_curation, phase_4_nda_execution, phase_5_bid_acceptance}` may create an EOI Acceptance Record. Writes outside this phase window MUST be rejected with `eoi_acceptance_phase_restricted` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Reads: buyer Workspace members per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; seller reads limited to the fields listed in `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` (see below); Ops reads all.

**Seller-Visible Projection.** `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` = `{id, accepted_at, acceptance_action, acceptance_conditions, referenced_capability_declaration_ids, resulting_bid_workspace_id, nda_required, nda_record_id}`. Seller NEVER sees `accepted_by_user_id`, `source_surface`, `bulk_accept_batch_id`, `match_score_threshold_value`, `match_score_at_acceptance`, or any reversal-internal fields. These restrictions are enforced at the API serializer, not UI — direct API callers with seller-session auth receive the same projection.

**Materialization Semantics (One-Click Acceptance Flow).** On successful write:

1. **Target Account created** on the buyer side with `status=nda_pending` (if `nda_required=true`) or `status=active` (if `nda_required=false`), referencing the seller Org and Marketplace Listing. See §4.3 Target Account schema; the new Target Account carries a `created_from_eoi_acceptance_id` pointer.
2. **Console Bridge Event emitted** of kind `eoi_acceptance_propagated` (authored in §4.7.1 enum) with direction `buyer_to_seller`, carrying the `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` fields only (firewall integrity).
3. **Seller notification dispatched** via Loops.so template `eoi_accepted_notification` with the seller-visible projection.
4. **Buyer-team notification dispatched** to the Workspace's watchers/Subscribers per §18 Notifications; `notification_buyer_team_sent_at` stamped.
5. **EOI Record state transition** (§4.5.2): `eoi_status` → `approved` and `eoi_approved_at` stamped.
6. **If `acceptance_action=accept_and_skip_nda`**: Bid Workspace materialized immediately with `status=active`; `resulting_bid_workspace_id` populated. Otherwise, Bid Workspace materialized on NDA execution (§4.5.3 state machine).
7. **Match Score snapshot stamped** into `match_score_at_acceptance` from the current §27.4 computation.

**Bulk Acceptance.** The `bulk_accept_queue` source surface supports accepting up to 25 EOIs in a single batch with shared `bulk_accept_batch_id`. Each EOI in the batch produces its own EOI Acceptance Record; batch-level failure of any single record does not roll back the batch — successes remain, failures are surfaced in a per-record results response. Bulk acceptance is rate-limited to 2 batches per 15 minutes per buyer user to prevent accidental mass-accepts.

**Acceptance Reversal.** A reversal creates a NEW record (append-only) with `reversal_reason` set and pointers populated. The original record remains immutable; the reversal record's `deleted_at` semantics apply only to the reversal row. Reversal cascades:

- Target Account: `status → withdrawn` with reason `acceptance_reversed`.
- Bid Workspace (if materialized): `status → canceled` per §4.4 Bid Workspace state machine; seller notified.
- NDA (if executed): NDA is preserved (cannot un-sign); NDA Record transitions to `revoked`.
- Console Bridge Event (reversal propagation): `eoi_acceptance_reversed` kind emitted.

Reversal is restricted to Workspace Owner or Workspace Admin within 72 hours of the original acceptance; after that, Ops intervention is required (`acceptance_reversal_requires_ops` error; new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `accepted` (implicit; no state enum on this entity — existence = accepted) | Buyer clicks accept | Phase in [3,4,5]; EOI in `submitted` state; seller not disqualified | Buyer (Workspace Owner / Admin / Use Case Lead) | Record created; materialization steps 1–7 execute |
| `accepted` | `reversed` (represented by a reversal record; original remains) | Buyer reverses | Within 72h; role = Workspace Owner/Admin | Buyer | Reversal cascade executes |
| `accepted` | `ops_reversed` | Ops reverses post-72h | Ops action; audit + note required | Ops | Same cascade; reversal record has `source_surface=api` and `accepted_by_role_snapshot` of the Ops user |

(No state enum field; existence of a non-reversed record represents acceptance, presence of a reversal record represents reversal. This avoids a mutable status on the original, preserving the immutable audit anchor.)

**Retention.** Accepted records retained for life of Workspace + 7 years (aligned with §40.2 Workspace retention). Reversal records retained identically. DSAR: user-level erasure redacts `accepted_by_user_id` to a synthetic anonymized id; workspace-level retention is unaffected. Residency: inherits buyer Workspace residency.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Seller Org deleted between EOI submission and acceptance.** Resolved: pre-write check confirms `seller_profile.state=active` and Org not in `deleted_at` state; rejected with `eoi_acceptance_seller_org_missing` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
2. **Workspace advanced past Phase 5 between EOI queue click and write.** Resolved: phase guard at write; rejected with `eoi_acceptance_phase_restricted`.
3. **Bulk batch includes an EOI whose seller has just opted-out globally.** Resolved: per-record validation; individual rejection with `eoi_acceptance_seller_opted_out` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); batch continues for non-rejected records.
4. **Duplicate acceptance race (two Workspace Admins click accept simultaneously).** Resolved: unique index on `eoi_record_id` ensures 1:1; second write gets `eoi_acceptance_duplicate` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); on conflict, UI shows "already accepted by {user} at {timestamp}".
5. **Console Bridge Event fails persistently (DLQ).** Resolved: acceptance record is durable regardless; bridge event re-enqueued per §4.7.1 retry curve; seller-visible Bid Workspace materialization delayed with buyer-visible banner "Seller notification delayed; retrying"; after DLQ, Ops-paged.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating an EOI Acceptance Record when the EOI Record is not in `submitted` state MUST be rejected with `eoi_acceptance_eoi_not_submitted` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
2. The Target Account materialization (step 1) MUST complete atomically with the EOI Acceptance Record write; partial materialization MUST be impossible (single Convex transaction).
3. Seller notification (step 3) MUST dispatch within 60 seconds of the acceptance write; dispatch failure retries per §31 retry curve `transactional_email`; DLQ after 5 failures with Ops alert.
4. Bulk acceptance MUST process up to 25 EOIs in a single API call; per-record failures MUST surface as a per-record error array without failing the batch.
5. Reversal within 72 hours by the Workspace Owner MUST cascade Target Account withdrawal, Bid Workspace cancellation (if materialized), and NDA revocation (if signed) within 10 seconds; cascade observable via the `eoi_acceptance.reversed` webhook (authored in Phase 4).
6. Seller read of the EOI Acceptance Record MUST return only the `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` fields; QA test `eoi_acceptance_seller_projection_redaction` asserts this.
7. The Marketplace Match Score snapshot stored in `match_score_at_acceptance` MUST equal the current §27.4 computation at the moment of write (± 1 second); subsequent score recomputation does NOT alter the snapshot.
8. An EOI Acceptance whose seller has a global Vendor Opt-Out effective at acceptance time MUST be rejected with `eoi_acceptance_seller_opted_out`; a page-type opt-out that does not cover `marketplace_listing` MUST NOT block acceptance.
9. Ops-initiated reversal after 72 hours MUST require the Ops user to supply a note (min 20 chars) recorded in `reversal_reason` extended notes.
10. The audit event (§4.6.1) for `create` on EOI Acceptance Record MUST include `{eoi_record_id, seller_org_id, acceptance_action, source_surface, bulk_accept_batch_id}` in the `changes` payload.
