## 4.7 Cross-Console Bridge Entities {#4.7-cross-console-bridge-entities}

**Authoring Intent.** §4.7 consolidates the entities that materialize the cross-console data flow defined in §25 (Console Bridge / Firewall / Disqualification). Two entities live here: Console Bridge Event, the per-change sync unit between a Buyer Workspace and linked Seller Bid Workspaces per Summary C.116 and C.117; and Vendor Disqualification Record, the first-class audit object for the disqualification workflow per Summary C.118 and §25.3. Both entities straddle the Dual-Console Firewall by design, and both carry explicit, testable field-level redaction rules so the firewall remains intact. Authored per PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md Conventions #1–#10.

### 4.7.1 Console Bridge Event (Cross-Console, Firewall-Bounded Sync Unit) {#4.7.1-console-bridge-event}

**Authoring Intent.** Console Bridge Event is the authoritative materialization of a single atomic cross-console change. Every Buyer-Workspace Requirement edit, Use Case re-structure, phase advancement, Q&A post, Amendment, NDA execution, EOI acceptance, and Disqualification that must reach the linked Seller Bid Workspace(s) produces one (or, for fan-out events, N) Console Bridge Event rows. Each row is the durable record of the sync attempt; it carries the redacted payload, retry state, bounded-lag SLO metadata, conflict resolution disposition, and cross-Workspace correlation. Per Summary C.116 the bridge is the only mechanism that carries buyer data into a seller's Bid Workspace without breaching the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2).

**Scope:** Cross-Console. The row's logical home is the Buyer Workspace (`buyer_workspace_id` primary scope) but the row is also readable by the linked Seller Org's `bid_workspace_id` for the seller-side rendering. The row itself lives in the platform-shared bridge-event storage partition with strict authoring-side isolation: seller-console reads are filtered at the serializer to the `seller_visible_projection` (see below); seller writes to this table are REJECTED uniformly (HTTP 403; `console_bridge_event_seller_write_forbidden`). Ops has full read and state-machine transition authority.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Buyer-side Org |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Seller-side Org |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace | Source Workspace |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Bid Workspace | Target Bid Workspace (1 per row; fan-out events create N rows, one per Bid Workspace) |
| `fanout_group_id` | UUID | Nullable | Correlation id for fan-out events (e.g., Amendment broadcast to N vendors) |
| `event_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind`: `requirement_created`, `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`, `requirement_locked`, `use_case_structure_changed`, `qa_thread_post_appended`, `phase_advanced`, `nda_executed`, `response_submitted`, `response_locked`, `disqualification_issued`, `workspace_canceled`, `amendment_broadcast`, `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor`, `eoi_acceptance_propagated`, `eoi_acceptance_reversed`, `revert_propagated`, `workspace_reopened_ops` | Bridge operation kind; immutable after write |
| `direction` | Enum | See Appendix J `console_bridge_event_direction`: `buyer_to_seller`, `seller_to_buyer` | Dataflow direction |
| `source_entity_type` | Enum | `requirement`, `use_case`, `qa_thread_post`, `workspace`, `nda_record`, `response`, `target_account`, `eoi_acceptance_record` | Source entity kind |
| `source_entity_id` | UUID | FK (polymorphic; application-validated per `source_entity_type`) | Source id in the Buyer Workspace namespace |
| `source_entity_version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Version of source at emit time (carries through amendments/reverts for ordering) |
| `payload_json` | JSON | ≤ 256000 bytes (256 KB hard cap per §31) | Redacted, firewall-compliant payload; see Field-Level Redaction below |
| `payload_content_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | Hash of `payload_json` for idempotency; 2nd emit with identical hash is deduplicated |
| `payload_schema_version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Schema version for the kind-specific payload shape |
| `idempotency_key` | String | 1–128 chars; unique per `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, event_kind, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` | Used by retries to avoid duplicate application |
| `sync_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `console_bridge_event_sync_status`: `pending`, `synced`, `retrying`, `failed`, `dlq`, `superseded` | See State Machine |
| `synced_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When target Bid Workspace acknowledged application |
| `last_attempt_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Most recent apply attempt |
| `next_retry_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Next scheduled retry per exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, then abort to `dlq` at attempt 5); §31 retry-curve class `console_bridge_standard` |
| `retry_count` | Integer | 0–5 | Attempts; capped at 5 before `dlq` |
| `failure_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `console_bridge_event_failure_reason`: `target_bid_workspace_missing`, `target_bid_workspace_disqualified`, `vendor_withdrawn`, `bid_workspace_readonly`, `schema_mismatch`, `payload_too_large`, `downstream_timeout`, `persistent_firewall_violation_suspected`, `other_transient`, `other_permanent` | Populated on every failed/retrying/dlq transition |
| `failure_note` | String | 0–2000 chars | Diagnostic note; MUST NOT contain buyer-internal content (redaction check) |
| `conflict_resolution` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `console_bridge_event_conflict_resolution`: `last_write_wins`, `buyer_origin_wins`, `operation_non_idempotent_dlq`, `merge_op` | How concurrent edits on the same source were reconciled; null when no conflict |
| `superseded_by_event_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-ref → Console Bridge Event | For `superseded` state: newer event for the same source supersedes this one |
| `slo_bounded_lag_ms` | Integer | ≥ 0, nullable | Observed lag in milliseconds between source-write and `synced_at`; populated at transition to `synced` |
| `slo_breach_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when `slo_bounded_lag_ms > 30000` (30-second SLO per C.117) |
| `redaction_verification_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | Hash over canonicalized `payload_json` asserting that no forbidden field (see below) is present; verified at write and re-verified on every retry |
| `cross_console_audit_trail` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Denormalized summary: who authored source, who triggered bridge, timestamps, for Ops forensics |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID (buyer-side author) or synthetic Ops/system UUID | Originator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last updater (typically system) |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete via Ops GDPR path only |

**Indexes.** `(buyer_workspace_id, created_at DESC)`, `(bid_workspace_id, created_at DESC)`, `(sync_status, next_retry_at)` for the retry scheduler, `(idempotency_key)` unique, `(fanout_group_id)` partial, `(slo_breach_flag, created_at)` partial where true for SLO dashboards, `(source_entity_type, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` for ordered-application queries, `(superseded_by_event_id)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** `buyer_workspace_id` MUST match `session.workspace_id`; workspace RBAC applies. Returned payload is the full `payload_json` (buyer authored it).
- **Seller-console reads:** `bid_workspace_id` MUST match `session.bid_workspace_id`; bid-workspace RBAC applies. Returned payload is filtered to `seller_visible_projection` (see below) — even though the `payload_json` on the server is already redaction-compliant, the seller serializer performs an additional whitelist pass on the kind-specific fields to defense-in-depth the firewall.
- **Ops reads:** All fields; Ops impersonation requires §35 impersonation audit (C.98).
- **Cross-Org reads:** Blocked. A buyer-console session for Org A attempting to read events for a `buyer_workspace_id` owned by Org B MUST receive HTTP 404 (not 403) with `console_bridge_event_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404). Same rule for seller cross-Org.
- **Seller writes:** Unconditionally blocked; HTTP 403 with `console_bridge_event_seller_write_forbidden`.
- **Buyer direct writes:** Not permitted through public API. Events are emitted by server-side side-effect handlers of source-entity mutations (Requirement, Use Case, Q&A Post, etc.). Direct POST to a bridge-event endpoint MUST return HTTP 403 with `console_bridge_event_direct_write_forbidden` (new; Appendix I).

**Field-Level Redaction Rules (Firewall Integrity).** The `payload_json` is REQUIRED to be firewall-compliant at write time. The write-layer redaction validator enforces, by kind:

| Event Kind | Fields CARRIED | Fields NEVER CARRIED |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `requirement_created`, `requirement_amended` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `title`, `description`, `response_type`, `weight`, `priority`, `order`, `status`, `amendment_diff_summary`, `buyer_workspace_phase` | Internal scores, rubric definitions, scoring scenarios, internal-comment threads, selection-report drafts, intelligence-brief drafts, AI operation prompts, buyer-authored private notes, buyer Team's AgentInstructions, buyer's cost/TCO computations not part of a pricing requirement |
| `requirement_reverted`, `revert_propagated` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `revert_target_version`, `reverted_by_user_role_snapshot`, `reason_snippet (≤200 chars public)` | Full revert rationale, internal-comment threads around the revert |
| `requirement_locked`, `response_locked` | `requirement_id`, `locked_at`, `locked_reason_public` | Internal rationale; who scored; Agent Pre-Scoring drafts |
| `use_case_structure_changed` | `use_case_id`, `title`, `description_public`, `lead_role_kind`, `included_requirement_ids`, `order` | Lead user identity (role-only), internal-comment threads, scoring scenarios |
| `qa_thread_post_appended` | `qa_thread_id`, `post_id`, `author_role_snapshot`, `body_markdown`, `attachments_urls` (Convex Storage signed URLs) | Internal comment bodies, Internal Comment Thread ids, mention expansions for buyer-internal users, buyer-internal thread replies |
| `phase_advanced` | `workspace_id`, `from_phase`, `to_phase`, `advanced_at`, `advanced_by_role_snapshot` | User identity (only role), reasons (only phase-specific public message) |
| `nda_executed` | `nda_record_id`, `nda_type`, `executed_at`, `nda_document_url`, `signatory_email_buyer_public`, `signatory_email_seller_public`, `expires_at` | Custom terms NOT auto-redacted (terms ARE carried; NDA content is by definition cross-console); buyer-internal notes about the signatory |
| `response_submitted` | `response_id`, `requirement_id`, `vendor_org_id` (same as seller_org_id), `submitted_at`, `version`, `response_payload` (seller authored; not buyer-internal) | N/A (seller→buyer direction; same redaction rules apply in reverse for buyer-internal data) |
| `disqualification_issued` | `bid_workspace_id`, `disqualified_at`, `notification_body_to_vendor` (vendor-visible copy only; rationale withheld) | Rationale, rationale author, any internal comment context |
| `workspace_canceled`, `workspace_reopened_ops` | `workspace_id`, `canceled_at` or `reopened_at`, `canceled_reason_public` (≤500 chars), `acting_role_snapshot` | Full rationale, internal-comment context |
| `amendment_broadcast` | `amendment_id`, `diff_summary`, `affected_requirement_ids`, `amended_at`, `broadcast_to_vendor_count` | Internal rationale, buyer-internal discussion |
| `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` | `qa_thread_post_id` reference (the Q&A post that surfaced the comment) | Raw Internal Comment content (the Internal Comment Thread is NEVER carried; only the externalized Q&A post that a buyer explicitly promoted to vendor-visible is carried) |
| `eoi_acceptance_propagated` | `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` (see §4.5.8) | All other EOI Acceptance fields |
| `eoi_acceptance_reversed` | `eoi_acceptance_id`, `reversed_at`, `reversal_reason_public` (≤200 chars) | Full reversal rationale |

**Redaction Verification.** `redaction_verification_hash` is computed over a canonicalized JSON serialization of `payload_json` with the kind's whitelist applied. At write, the validator (a) confirms no forbidden field is present at any depth, (b) confirms the hash matches, (c) rejects with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) on any mismatch. Violations additionally alert Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) — a persistent pattern of firewall-violation events from the same buyer session is a potential security incident.

**Seller-Visible Projection.** A secondary kind-specific whitelist is applied by the seller serializer. This is a defense-in-depth layer: even if a malformed event slipped past write-time validation, the seller read layer still strips any field not in the kind's whitelist. QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` asserts this for each event kind.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending` | Buyer-side mutation handler emits event | Redaction validation passed; idempotency check passed (no prior row for same idempotency_key within 24h) | Scheduler picks up within 5s |
| `pending` | `synced` | Bid Workspace applies event successfully | Apply handler returned success; `synced_at` stamped; `slo_bounded_lag_ms` computed | SLO breach flag set if `> 30000ms` |
| `pending` | `retrying` | Apply failure, retryable | `failure_reason ∈ {downstream_timeout, other_transient}`; `retry_count < 5`; `next_retry_at` scheduled per backoff curve | |
| `retrying` | `synced` | Retry succeeds | | `slo_bounded_lag_ms` may exceed 30000; `slo_breach_flag=true` |
| `retrying` | `retrying` | Retry fails, retryable, `retry_count < 5` | `retry_count++`; new `next_retry_at` | |
| `retrying` | `dlq` | 5 failed attempts | `retry_count=5`; transitions to DLQ with Ops alert | Manual re-drive from Ops Console |
| `pending` or `retrying` | `failed` | Apply failure, non-retryable | `failure_reason ∈ {target_bid_workspace_missing, target_bid_workspace_disqualified, vendor_withdrawn, bid_workspace_readonly, schema_mismatch, payload_too_large, persistent_firewall_violation_suspected, other_permanent}` | Buyer workspace surface shows bridge failure note |
| `pending` or `retrying` | `superseded` | A newer event for the same source arrives | `superseded_by_event_id` set; the newer event takes precedence per `conflict_resolution=last_write_wins` | Useful for rapid successive Requirement edits |
| `dlq` | `pending` | Ops manual re-drive | Ops resets `retry_count=0`, `failure_reason=null`, `failure_note` cleared | Re-queues |
| `failed` | `pending` | Ops manual re-drive after fixing underlying issue | Same conditions as from `dlq` | |

**Retry Curve.** Exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s — 5 attempts total. `next_retry_at = last_attempt_at + (2^retry_count seconds)`. Bounded-lag SLO is 30 seconds from `created_at` to `synced_at` per C.117; the 30-second SLO excludes `dlq` and `failed` terminal states (those surface in dashboards as separate anomalies). Retry curve class is `console_bridge_standard` in §31.

**DLQ Handling.** DLQ-state rows are visible in (a) the buyer Workspace's "Bridge Health" panel with per-event detail, (b) the seller Bid Workspace's "Sync Health" panel with redacted detail, and (c) the Ops Console's cross-Workspace bridge dashboard. Ops one-click re-drive transitions back to `pending`; automated re-drive is NOT permitted (human approval required) to prevent infinite loops on persistent underlying failures. If a buyer-side source edit is made while an event is in DLQ, the new event supersedes (the DLQ event transitions to `superseded`, new event enters `pending`) — no duplicate apply.

**Conflict Resolution.** Concurrent buyer-side edits on the same source entity produce multiple events. The default rule is `last_write_wins` — the newer event supersedes older events in `pending`/`retrying`. For non-idempotent operations (e.g., `requirement_reverted` on a version that has since been further amended), the rule is `operation_non_idempotent_dlq` — the event is routed directly to `dlq` for Ops resolution. Amendments (`requirement_amended`) use `merge_op` — the semantic diff is recomputed against the most recent applied state and applied as a single rebased amendment. `buyer_origin_wins` is used in the rare case of bidirectional conflict (buyer amends and vendor submits response against the pre-amendment version simultaneously) — the buyer-origin event applies; the vendor's response is marked `needs_reverification` per §4.4 Response state machine.

**Daily Reconciliation.** Per §25.2, a 2am UTC job scans for stale bridge entries across all workspaces. Stale = `pending` or `retrying` > 24 hours. Stale entries are escalated to DLQ if not transient, or re-driven if the underlying infrastructure is known-healthy; the job emits `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` webhook (authored in Phase 4) with per-workspace counts.

**Retention.** Bridge events retained for Workspace life + 7 years per §40.2 (aligned with Workspace retention). Soft-deleted only via Ops GDPR path with DPO approval; even then, the row is redacted (payload reduced to kind + timestamps + redaction_verification_hash) rather than hard-deleted, to preserve firewall audit integrity. Residency: each row lives in the buyer Workspace's residency region; reads from the seller Bid Workspace are served from the buyer region with a latency-permitting cross-region read path, with exceptions per §45 Data Privacy for EU-only residency scopes.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Vendor Bid Workspace disqualified mid-event.** Resolved: target check at apply time; `failure_reason=target_bid_workspace_disqualified`; event transitions to `failed` (non-retryable); buyer-side "Bridge Health" panel flags; no re-drive possible until disqualification is reversed.
2. **Vendor withdraws during a pending event.** Resolved: `failure_reason=vendor_withdrawn`; transitions to `failed`; buyer-side notification (optional based on buyer preference) that vendor withdrew.
3. **Payload exceeds 256KB (e.g., massive use-case restructure).** Resolved: write-time check rejects with `console_bridge_event_payload_too_large` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 413) and surfaces a buyer-visible "payload too large" banner that links to the §25.1 guidance on chunked updates. The mutation handler is responsible for emitting multiple smaller events (e.g., per-requirement amendments) rather than one massive batch.
4. **Firewall violation detected at write.** Resolved: `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` + SIM alert + Ops investigation; recurring violations from the same buyer session may block bridge emission until Ops reviews (hard-block is a last resort; defaults to soft-warn + Ops escalation).
5. **Concurrent edits produce rapid-fire events.** Resolved: `last_write_wins` + supersede semantics; older events transition to `superseded` rather than being applied out of order.
6. **Seller-side apply handler is slow (downstream timeout).** Resolved: 30-second SLO; retry curve; DLQ after 5 attempts; Ops page on DLQ depth > 100.
7. **Daily reconciliation job fails to run.** Resolved: job heartbeat alert; missed-run triggers Ops page; manual re-run is idempotent (idempotency_key prevents duplicate apply).
8. **Ops re-drive of DLQ event on a disqualified vendor.** Resolved: re-drive re-evaluates target state; rejected with `console_bridge_event_cannot_redrive_disqualified` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A Console Bridge Event MUST be written within 100ms of the source-entity mutation being committed (event emission is a Convex transaction side-effect on the source mutation).
2. Bounded-lag SLO (`synced_at - created_at ≤ 30000ms`) MUST be observable via the `slo_breach_flag` field and the `console_bridge.slo_summary` Ops dashboard; breach rate > 1% over a rolling 15-minute window MUST page Ops.
3. A write with `payload_json` exceeding 256KB MUST be rejected with `console_bridge_event_payload_too_large` (HTTP 413); mutation handler falls back to chunked events.
4. A write whose `redaction_verification_hash` does not match a recomputed hash over canonicalized `payload_json` MUST be rejected with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` (HTTP 422) and SIM-alerted.
5. A seller-console session reading a Console Bridge Event MUST receive only the `seller_visible_projection` fields for the event kind; QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` runs against every event kind.
6. A buyer-console or seller-console session attempting cross-Org read MUST receive HTTP 404 with `console_bridge_event_cross_org_access`.
7. A DLQ transition MUST emit `console_bridge.dlq_entered` webhook within 10 seconds and surface in the buyer and seller Health panels within 60 seconds.
8. Daily reconciliation at 2am UTC MUST emit `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` with per-workspace stale counts; a missed run MUST page Ops within 2 hours.
9. Ops manual re-drive MUST require the Ops user to supply a note (min 20 chars) and MUST NOT automatically cascade to other related DLQ events without explicit per-event re-drive.
10. The `idempotency_key` unique constraint MUST prevent duplicate application across restarts and retries; a duplicate write attempt MUST return HTTP 200 with the existing row's id (idempotent replay), not HTTP 409.

### 4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record (Cross-Console, Buyer-Initiated, Seller-Visible-with-Redaction) {#4.7.2-vendor-disqualification-record}

**Authoring Intent.** Vendor Disqualification Record makes the disqualification workflow (§25.3, Summary C.118) a first-class entity. Today §25.3 describes the transitions as prose on Target Account and Bid Workspace state; this entity captures the disqualification as a queryable, auditable, appealable business object, supports three severities (workspace-local soft, account-level across the buyer Org's Workspaces, and Ops-imposed global ban), and binds the rationale (buyer-private) to the notification body (vendor-visible) with explicit asymmetric-visibility fields. This separation is necessary because disqualification has implications that extend beyond the originating Workspace (Organization Intelligence vendor history per §25.3; Seller Signal suppression downstream; Marketplace Listing eligibility interactions with Vendor Opt-Out; and Ops escalation paths).

**Scope:** Cross-Console. Scope anchors: `buyer_org_id` + `buyer_workspace_id` for workspace-level disqualifications; `buyer_org_id` only for account-level disqualifications; platform-scoped for Ops-imposed global bans. Seller reads are limited to the vendor-visible fields (`notification_body_to_vendor`, `disqualified_at`, and the Bid Workspace status transition) — the rationale and rationale author are NEVER exposed.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `severity` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_severity`: `soft` (workspace-local), `account_level` (buyer Org's Workspaces, forward-looking), `global_ban` (Ops-imposed across platform) | Determines cascade scope |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity=global_ban`; FK → Organization | Disqualifying Buyer Org |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Workspace | Workspace (if soft) |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Disqualified seller |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Bid Workspace | Target Bid Workspace (soft) |
| `target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Target Account | Target Account (soft) |
| `trigger` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_trigger`: `workspace_owner_manual`, `automated_policy_violation`, `ops_compliance_action`, `vendor_non_responsive`, `vendor_withdrew_then_blocked`, `duplicate_bid_submission` | Why |
| `rationale_internal` | String | 10–4000 chars, required | Buyer-private rationale; audit trail; NEVER shown to vendor |
| `rationale_author_user_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User | Who authored the rationale |
| `rationale_author_role_snapshot` | Enum | See Appendix J (workspace_roles / ops_roles) | Frozen at write |
| `notification_body_to_vendor` | String | 1–1000 chars; templated | Vendor-visible copy; defaults per severity (neutral "Your participation in '{Workspace Title}' has ended. Thank you for your interest."); editable per-disqualification by Workspace Owner |
| `notification_style` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_notification_style`: `neutral_no_rationale` (default), `rationale_shared_with_vendor` (only if buyer explicitly opts in and Ops approves), `silent_no_vendor_notification` (global_ban Ops-only) | How the vendor is notified |
| `notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor received notification |
| `vendor_acknowledgement_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor session first loaded the disqualification banner |
| `appeal_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_appeal_status`: `not_offered`, `eligible`, `submitted`, `under_review`, `upheld`, `overturned`, `expired` | Appeal state |
| `appeal_window_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Deadline for appeal (default 14 days for `account_level`; not_offered for `soft`; 30 days for `global_ban`) |
| `appeal_narrative` | String | 0–4000 chars, nullable | Vendor's rebuttal |
| `appeal_decided_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `appeal_decision_note_internal` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-facing decision rationale |
| `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible` | String | 0–2000 chars | Vendor-visible decision summary |
| `cascade_status` | Enum | `pending`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `failed` | Cascade of downstream effects (response lock, Q&A orphaning, Scoring exclusion, etc.) |
| `cascade_completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When cascade finished |
| `cascade_actions_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Structured record of each cascade action + timestamp + success/failure; for Ops forensics |
| `console_bridge_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Console Bridge Event (§4.7.1) | The bridge event of kind `disqualification_issued` that propagated the disqualification to the seller's Bid Workspace (soft severity) or to the Seller Console banner (account_level / global_ban) |
| `related_abuse_report_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Marketplace Abuse Report (§4.5.7) | Populated when disqualification is a downstream of an upheld abuse report (trigger=`ops_compliance_action`) |
| `reversed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated only for overturned appeals or Ops manual reversal |
| `reversed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User | |
| `reversal_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `appeal_overturned`, `ops_manual_reversal`, `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h`, `system_error_rollback` | Required when `reversed_at` set |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Alias of `rationale_author_user_id` for most cases; Ops-user for `global_ban` |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft-delete only via Ops GDPR path |

**Indexes.** `(seller_org_id, created_at DESC)` — Vendor history view per §25.3, `(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial where `severity='soft'` — prevents duplicate soft-disqualifications in the same Workspace, `(buyer_org_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial where `severity='account_level'`, `(severity, reversed_at)` partial where null — for the "active disqualifications" queries, `(appeal_status, appeal_window_at)` partial for appeal-expiry scans, `(related_abuse_report_id)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, and Use Case Leads of the originating Workspace see all fields; Ops sees all. Other buyer Org users see a redacted projection without `rationale_internal`.
- **Seller-console reads:** Only a redacted vendor-visible projection `{id, severity, disqualified_at, notification_body_to_vendor, appeal_status, appeal_window_at, appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible, reversed_at}`. `rationale_internal`, `rationale_author_user_id`, and `cascade_actions_json` are NEVER returned.
- **Cross-Workspace seller reads:** For `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`, the Seller Org sees one row in their Seller Console Account Status surface with the vendor-visible projection; `buyer_workspace_id` is null, preserving workspace-specific privacy even when account-level disqualification originated from a specific Workspace.
- **Org Intelligence surface (§25.3 vendor history):** Reads disqualification records for the buyer Org's past Workspaces; `rationale_internal` is visible only to the disqualifying Workspace Owner and to Org Admins; other viewers see "Rationale restricted to Workspace Owner".

**Cascade Actions (Soft Severity).**

1. `target_account.status → disqualified` (aligns with §25.3 and existing enum in Appendix J).
2. `bid_workspace.status → disqualified`.
3. Vendor notification dispatched via Loops.so template per `notification_style`; `notification_sent_at` stamped.
4. All vendor responses in this Bid Workspace → `locked`; vendor cannot edit or add; banner displayed on vendor side.
5. Q&A threads initiated by this vendor → orphaned (read-only for vendor; no reply capability).
6. Vendor excluded from Scoring phase; scoring matrix renders with red "Disqualified" badge.
7. Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` emitted; `seller_visible_projection` includes only `{notification_body_to_vendor, disqualified_at}` (rationale NEVER carried).
8. SLA timer for this vendor in any open Team queue cancelled.
9. Seller Signal (§4.4.18) suppresses this buyer-vendor pair from the affected buyer Org's signals to this Seller Org for 90 days (avoids noisy post-disqualification signal).

**Cascade Actions (Account-Level Severity).** In addition to steps 1–6 for EVERY `bid_workspace` this seller is currently active in within the buyer Org's Workspaces, plus:

- All open Marketplace Listings by this buyer that this seller matches → seller is auto-excluded from future match-score calculations for this buyer for 12 months.
- Seller's future EOI submissions to any Workspace of this buyer Org → auto-rejected with reason `buyer_account_level_disqualification` (new enum value for `abuse_report_closure_disposition` is NOT appropriate; use a new enum `eoi_rejection_reason.buyer_account_level_disqualification` — authored in Phase 4 when EOI rejection reasons are added to Appendix J).
- Bridge event fans out to all affected Bid Workspaces (N events, one per active engagement).

**Cascade Actions (Global Ban, Ops-Only).** In addition to the account-level cascade for the triggering buyer Org (if applicable):

- Seller Org's Marketplace Listings → `hidden` across the platform.
- SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage → `410 Gone` (like Vendor Opt-Out render contract).
- Seller Profile delisted from Marketplace search; Capability Declarations remain but `published=false` is forced.
- Seller Signal delivery suspended platform-wide.
- Seller's account is placed in a `banned` state (new Organization state; `organization.state=banned` — authored in Phase 4 when Organization state machine is extended).
- Notification style is MUST be `silent_no_vendor_notification` for Ops-covert investigations OR `neutral_no_rationale` with Ops leadership approval; `rationale_shared_with_vendor` is disallowed for `global_ban` (legal).

**Appeal Workflow.**

- `soft`: appeal NOT offered by default. Workspace Owner MAY reverse within 72 hours (see Reversal below). `appeal_status=not_offered`.
- `account_level`: appeal eligible for 14 days from `created_at`. Vendor receives magic-link (authenticated Seller Org Admin) appeal form; 4000-char narrative. Ops reviews within 10 business days; decision renders `upheld` or `overturned`. Appeal form displays vendor-visible projection only.
- `global_ban`: appeal eligible for 30 days. Dual sign-off by Ops leadership required for both upholding and overturning. Overturning requires a documented audit path.

**Reversal.** Soft disqualifications MAY be reversed by the Workspace Owner within 72 hours with reason `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h`; beyond 72 hours, requires Ops with `ops_compliance_admin` role. Account-level disqualifications are reversed only through appeal-overturned or Ops manual reversal (`ops_manual_reversal`). Global bans are reversed only via Ops leadership dual-signoff. Reversal cascades (reverse of the severity's cascade): Target Account un-disqualified, Bid Workspace un-disqualified (returns to prior status, typically `active`), responses un-locked (returning to prior state, not necessarily `submitted` — §4.4 Response state machine handles this), Q&A threads reopened, scoring inclusion restored (if Scoring phase has not already concluded — see Known Gap below), vendor notification sent. Reversal emits a new Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` with a reversal flag in the payload (not a separate kind — reversal is semantically a new disqualification-state event with `reversed=true`).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active` (existence, no state field) | Buyer or Ops creates | Rationale ≥ 10 chars; seller not already in same-severity disqualification from same buyer; severity-specific preconditions | Buyer (soft), Buyer Org Admin (account_level with dual-signoff), Ops (global_ban with Ops leadership dual-signoff) | Cascade begins; bridge event emitted |
| `active` | `appeal_submitted` (appeal_status transition) | Vendor submits appeal | `appeal_status=eligible`; within `appeal_window_at` | Seller Org Admin | Ops review SLA starts |
| `appeal_submitted` | `appeal_upheld` | Ops upholds | Ops decision | Ops | Disqualification remains; vendor notified |
| `appeal_submitted` | `appeal_overturned` (reversal cascade) | Ops overturns | Ops decision; `reversed_at` set | Ops | Reversal cascade executes |
| `active` | `reversed` | Workspace Owner reverses within 72h | `severity=soft`; within 72h | Buyer Workspace Owner | Reversal cascade executes |
| `active` | `expired` (appeal_status) | Appeal window expired without submission | `appeal_window_at < now`; no appeal filed | System | Appeal no longer available |

(No top-level state field on this entity; the lifecycle is represented by the presence/absence of `reversed_at`, `appeal_status`, and the cascade state.)

**Retention.** `active` and `reversed` disqualifications retained for Workspace life + 7 years. Appeal narratives retained similarly. Soft-delete only via Ops GDPR path with DPO approval; even then, the fact of the disqualification and its severity are preserved (only PII fields redacted).

**Residency.** Buyer-origin disqualifications stored in buyer Workspace residency. Ops-originated global bans stored in platform-global residency. Seller reads served from their home residency with cross-region read path.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Rationale contains accidental buyer-internal content (scoring, selection-report draft excerpt).** Resolved: `rationale_internal` is explicitly buyer-private and firewall-isolated; redaction validator on Console Bridge Event ensures it does NOT cross the firewall; the vendor sees `notification_body_to_vendor` only.
2. **Concurrent disqualification and scoring phase.** Resolved: cascade includes "exclude from scoring matrix" only if phase ≤ `phase_11_scoring_review_consensus`; post-Phase-12 disqualification is allowed (emergency Ops-driven only) but does NOT rewrite the historical Selection Report — it adds a post-hoc annotation (see Known Gap below).
3. **Reversal after Scoring phase has concluded.** Known Gap: reversing a soft disqualification after Phase 11 ends is permitted but scoring cannot be retroactively reopened (per §12 Scoring semantics); the vendor is reinstated to the shortlist but not to scoring. Flagged in Authored Extensions for human review.
4. **Vendor Org deleted between disqualification and appeal.** Resolved: appeal flow disabled with `vendor_org_deleted` note; `appeal_status=not_offered`; disqualification record preserved for audit.
5. **Global ban overlaps with an open soft disqualification.** Resolved: global ban supersedes; existing soft records stay in place (audit integrity) but are annotated with `superseded_by_global_ban=true` and surfaces redacted to Ops-only.
6. **Rationale author's role changes after disqualification.** Resolved: `rationale_author_role_snapshot` is frozen at write; role change does not rewrite history.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a Vendor Disqualification Record with `severity=soft` but without a `buyer_workspace_id` and `bid_workspace_id` MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_soft_requires_workspace_scope` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
2. Creating `severity=global_ban` without Ops leadership dual-signoff MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_global_ban_requires_dual_signoff` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
3. Vendor notification dispatch MUST occur within 60 seconds of create; failure retries per §31 retry curve `transactional_email`; DLQ after 5 failures with Ops alert.
4. The full cascade (Target Account, Bid Workspace, responses, Q&A, scoring exclusion, bridge event, Seller Signal suppression) MUST complete within 10 seconds for soft severity and 60 seconds for account_level (because fan-out may touch N workspaces). Completion is observable via `cascade_status=complete`.
5. Seller read of the disqualification record MUST return only the vendor-visible projection; QA test `vendor_disqualification_seller_projection_redaction` asserts this.
6. The Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` emitted on create MUST NOT carry `rationale_internal` or `rationale_author_user_id`; QA test `vendor_disqualification_bridge_firewall` asserts this against the redaction verification hash.
7. Workspace Owner reversal within 72 hours MUST fully reverse the cascade within 10 seconds (seller-visible restoration) and MUST emit a Console Bridge Event reflecting the reversal.
8. Account-level disqualification MUST auto-reject incoming EOIs from the disqualified seller to the buyer Org for 12 months from `created_at`; the EOI rejection uses `buyer_account_level_disqualification` as reason and the seller is notified.
9. Global ban MUST force `organization.state=banned` on the seller Org (authored in Phase 4 when Organization state machine is extended) and MUST hide all Marketplace Listings, SellerOrgPages, SoftwarePages, and suspend Seller Signal delivery within 15 minutes.
10. Appeal window expiry MUST transition `appeal_status → expired` exactly at `appeal_window_at` (± 1 minute); system job runs every minute to sweep expirations.
11. A write attempt by a non-Workspace-Owner/Admin/Use-Case-Lead buyer user with `severity=soft` MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
12. Historical Selection Reports (§43) that reference a vendor later disqualified post-Phase-12 MUST render a banner "This vendor was subsequently disqualified on {date}" at next report access, without rewriting the report body (preserves Phase-12 immutability).
