| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete on Org closure; financial records preserved |

**Indexes.** `(org_id)` unique, `(wallet_state, current_period_ends_at)` for the period-rollover sweep, `(auto_topup_trigger_state, updated_at)` partial for top-up scheduler, `(payment_failed_grace_until)` partial where `wallet_state=payment_failed_grace` for grace-expiry sweep, `(committed_spend_contract_id)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** `org_id = session.org_id`; `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` see all fields; `member` and `guest` see HTTP 403 `wallet_role_forbidden`.
- **Seller-console reads:** Same as above (the wallet is shared).
- **Public reads:** Forbidden.
- **Ops reads:** All; `ops_finance_admin` may also write (manual adjustment).
- **Cross-Org reads:** HTTP 404 `wallet_cross_org_access`.

**Wallet State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active` | Org first publishes a paid plan OR Free Org first invokes a customer-billed capability | Stripe customer created; `budget_value_dollars` set per plan tier | Free Orgs receive a $5/mo budget per Pricing Strategy §4 |
| `active` | `soft_warned_50` | Consumed crosses 50% of `(budget + overage_cap)` | Email + in-app notification to Org Owner + Billing Admin | One-shot; `notification_50pct_sent_at` stamped |
| `soft_warned_50` | `soft_warned_80` | Consumed crosses 80% | Same notification recipients | One-shot; auto-topup may fire here if enabled |
| `soft_warned_80` | `hard_capped_100` | Consumed crosses 100% AND auto-topup unavailable / disabled / capped-out | All subsequent customer-billed AIOperation writes return HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` (new; Appendix I); Sourcera-owned operations continue | Customer-visible banner with one-click upgrade or top-up CTAs |
| `hard_capped_100` | `active` | Top-up succeeds OR billing period rolls over OR plan upgrade | Wallet headroom restored | All counters relevant to current period reset only at rollover |
| `active` (or any soft_warned state) | `payment_failed_grace` | Auto-topup charge fails | `payment_failed_grace_until = now + 48h` | Wallet remains active during grace; billing admin emailed hourly |
| `payment_failed_grace` | `active` | Top-up retry succeeds | | |
| `payment_failed_grace` | `suspended` | Grace expires without successful top-up | | All customer-billed operations rejected; Ops alert |
| `suspended` | `active` | Manual Ops resolution OR customer updates payment method + retry succeeds | | |
| Any | `closed` | Org deletion OR Ops closure | `closed_at` stamped; wallet read-only afterward | Financial records (AIOperations) survive |

**§4.8.3.A Top-Up State Machine.** Encapsulates the auto-topup state machine for clarity:

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `idle` | `pending_charge` | `auto_topup_trigger_utilization_pct` reached | `auto_topup_enabled=true`; `auto_topup_consumed_monthly + auto_topup_increment ≤ auto_topup_max_monthly` | Stripe charge initiated |
| `pending_charge` | `completed` | Stripe charge succeeds | `last_topup_at` stamped; `overage_cap_value_dollars += increment`; `auto_topup_consumed_monthly += increment` | |
| `pending_charge` | `failed_retry` | Stripe charge fails (transient) | Retry per `auto_topup_charge` retry-curve class (1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m; DLQ at attempt 5) | Wallet enters `payment_failed_grace` |
| `failed_retry` | `completed` | Retry succeeds | | |
| `failed_retry` | `abandoned` | DLQ at attempt 5 | Wallet enters `suspended` after grace expiry | Ops alert |
| `completed` | `idle` | Period rolls over | `auto_topup_consumed_monthly` resets | |

**Free Allowance Interaction.** When an Org invokes a customer-billed capability for which it has unconsumed FreeAllowanceCounter units, the AIOperation is written with `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`; the FreeAllowanceCounter atomically decrements. Wallet counters are NOT touched. On exhaustion, subsequent operations follow standard wallet-draw semantics.

**Committed Spend Interaction.** When `committed_spend_contract_id` is set, AIOperations preferentially burn down `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` before drawing `budget_value_dollars`/`overage_cap_value_dollars`. The commit is the customer's pre-paid commit pool — billing the wallet first would be an accounting error.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Currency change mid-period.** Resolved: `billing_currency` is immutable post-create except via Ops Finance with explicit migration runbook (out of scope for entity; flagged).
2. **Stripe webhook fires twice (idempotency violation).** Resolved: `stripe_invoice_lookup_token` deduplication + Stripe's `event.id` outbox dedup at the webhook handler layer.
3. **Period rollover at midnight UTC for an Org with `billing_period_anchor_day_utc=31` in February.** Resolved: month-end normalization (Feb 28 / Feb 29); `current_period_ends_at` always equals the next anchor day.
4. **Customer disables auto-topup mid-charge.** Resolved: in-flight Stripe charges complete; the disable takes effect for future triggers; UI shows "Top-up in progress; auto-topup disabled effective next period."
5. **Wallet enters `suspended` while a `pending` AIOperation is open.** Resolved: pending operations may settle normally (the wallet hold was placed at write time and is honored through settlement); only NEW operations are blocked.
6. **Org changes residency mid-period.** Resolved: `residency_locked_entity` change requires Ops with re-invoicing runbook; in-period residency changes do not retroactively reissue invoices.
7. **Free allowance and wallet both insufficient simultaneously.** Resolved: AIOperation write is rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`; UI surfaces upgrade or top-up CTAs.
8. **Concurrent decrements from two AI invocations consuming the last $0.05 of headroom.** Resolved: optimistic locking on `(id, consumed_value_dollars)`; second writer retries with re-evaluation; if headroom now insufficient, the second operation receives HTTP 402.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The wallet MUST be Org-scoped (one row per Org) regardless of console plan combinations; QA test `wallet_org_unique` asserts.
2. `consumed_value_dollars` MUST reset exactly at `current_period_ends_at`; cron-based with idempotent retry; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour.
3. Customer-billed AIOperation writes MUST be rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` when the wallet is `hard_capped_100` AND no commit pool AND no free allowance is applicable.
4. Auto-topup MUST NEVER be enabled by default; an admin action with explicit confirmation MUST be required to set `auto_topup_enabled=true`.
5. `auto_topup_increment_value_dollars` MUST be ≥ $50 and ≤ $10,000; values outside this range MUST be rejected with HTTP 422 `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I).
6. The 50%, 80%, and 100% notifications MUST be one-shot per period (idempotency stamps prevent duplicate emails); QA test `wallet_notifications_idempotent` asserts.
7. Free Allowance consumption MUST atomically decrement the FreeAllowanceCounter and write `billed_against_free_allowance=true` on the AIOperation; QA test `wallet_free_allowance_atomicity` asserts no double-spend.
8. Commit-pool burn-down MUST precede wallet-budget burn-down for Orgs with an active CommittedSpendContract; QA test `wallet_commit_burn_priority` asserts.
9. A wallet in `suspended` state MUST NOT block in-flight `pending` AIOperations; only new operations are blocked.
10. The wallet MUST never hold a non-USD `budget_value_dollars` value internally; presentation in the customer's `billing_currency` is via `fx_rate_locked` at presentation time only.

### 4.8.4 OutcomeContract (Per-Capability, Versioned, Ops-Managed) {#4.8.4-outcomecontract}

**Authoring Intent.** OutcomeContract defines, per capability, the precise, machine-readable rules under which an AIOperation transitions from `pending` to `accepted` or `rejected`. It is the canonical location for the Pricing Strategy §6 / §10 outcome-signal tables (Appendix B in the Buyer Pricing Strategy, §10 in the Seller Pricing Strategy). Because the Outcome Resolver is the single source of truth for Sourcera's margin protection, the contract is versioned: a contract change does NOT retroactively reclassify settled operations, and `pending` operations always resolve under the contract version that was active at AIOperation write time.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; many-to-one with CapabilityRegistryEntry (a capability has one active contract version at a time but a history of prior contracts).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id`; required | The capability this contract governs |
| `version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Monotonic per `capability_id` |
| `accepted_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Structured rule referencing one or more `outcome_contract_signal_type` values; supports composite (AND/OR) rules |
| `rejected_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars; nullable | Optional explicit rejection rule; absence means rejection only via timeout (auto-accept fires) or explicit user reject button |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | Integer | ≥ 60 (1 minute floor); ≤ 7776000 (90-day ceiling) | The auto-accept timer; copied to AIOperation.`auto_accept_after_seconds` at write time |
| `contest_window_days` | Integer | Default 14 (Summary C.78); ≥ 1; ≤ 90 | Per-capability contest window override (default 14 used if not overridden); copied to AIOperation `contest_window_at` derivation |
| `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` | Integer | Default 30 | Time after `auto_accept_after_seconds` during which a late `accepted` signal still counts (race-condition mitigation) |
| `requires_explicit_user_signal` | Boolean | Default false | When true, no auto-accept — the operation hangs in `pending` until an explicit accept/reject signal arrives or 90 days pass (then auto-rejected as `rejected_timeout_no_signal`) |
| `signal_subject_entity_kinds` | Array[Enum] | Subset of AIOperation entity kinds | Which downstream entities the resolver watches for retention/edit signals |
| `min_retention_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | For "retention" signal types; e.g., "≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid" |
| `max_edit_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | For "edit-distance" signal types; e.g., "≤ 20% edit" |
| `state` | Enum | `draft`, `active`, `superseded`, `retired` | Lifecycle |
| `superseded_by_contract_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → OutcomeContract | When state=superseded, the next-version contract |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this contract version became active |
| `superseded_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; UTC | |
| `published_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; only allowed in `draft` state |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Hard-delete forbidden |

**Indexes.** `(capability_id, version DESC)`, `(capability_id, state)` partial where `state=active` (a capability has at most one active contract; enforced as a partial unique index), `(superseded_by_contract_id)` partial.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Ops creates new version | `version = MAX(prior versions) + 1` | Editable in draft |
| `draft` | `active` | Ops publishes | Prior `active` (if any) transitions to `superseded`; `effective_at` stamped | Atomic swap |
| `active` | `superseded` | New version published | `superseded_at` stamped; `superseded_by_contract_id` set | Pending operations under prior contract resolve under prior contract |
| `superseded` | `retired` | After 90 days | All operations under this contract have settled or expired | Permanent terminal state |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Contract change retroactively reclassifies settled operations.** Resolved: AIOperations record `outcome_contract_id` of the active contract at write time (denormalized via the resolver query plan); resolution always uses the original contract.
2. **`accepted_signal_rule` JSON malformed.** Resolved: write-time JSON-schema validation against `outcome_contract_rule_schema` (versioned schema in Appendix J extension); rejection with `outcome_contract_rule_invalid` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
3. **No active contract for a customer-billed capability.** Resolved: AIOperation write rejected with HTTP 402 `capability_no_active_outcome_contract` (new; Appendix I); operation does not begin.
4. **A signal arrives during the `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` window after auto-accept.** Resolved: late `accepted` signals are no-ops if already auto-accepted; late `rejected` signals trigger automatic ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Exactly one OutcomeContract per `capability_id` MUST be in `state=active` at any time; partial unique index enforces.
2. AIOperation resolution MUST use the OutcomeContract version that was active at the AIOperation `created_at`, not the currently active version.
3. `auto_accept_after_seconds` MUST be ≥ 60; lower values rejected with HTTP 422 `outcome_contract_auto_accept_too_short`.
4. Contract publication MUST atomically transition the prior active contract to `superseded` (single transaction); concurrent publication attempts rejected with HTTP 409 `outcome_contract_concurrent_publish`.
5. Default-on-timeout MUST be `rejected` per Pricing Strategy §6 unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`; auto-accept produces `auto_accepted` (a distinct settlement_state) for product-quality dashboards.

### 4.8.5 ContestRecord (Per-AIOperation, Customer-Initiated, Ops-Reviewed) {#4.8.5-contestrecord}

**Authoring Intent.** ContestRecord materializes the 14-day customer-initiated dispute window per Summary C.78. Any settled `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation can be contested by the Org's `billing_admin` within `contest_window_at`; the contest routes to Ops Finance, which approves (and credits) or rejects (and restores). The 14-day default is overridable per capability via OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days`. Contests are also auto-filed by the system when a late outcome signal arrives after auto-accept (`auto_filed_late_signal`) — this is a margin-protection / customer-trust mechanism that catches outcome-resolver bugs without requiring the customer to notice.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one-to-one with the contested AIOperation (a single AIOperation can be contested at most once; second contest attempts return HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed`).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required | Mirrors AIOperation.org_id; denormalized for query performance |
| `ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIOperation; unique | The contested operation |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `system` | Mirrors AIOperation.console for cross-console firewall enforcement on read |
| `filed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User with `billing_admin` role; nullable for `system` (auto-filed) | |
| `filed_by_role_snapshot` | Enum | Role at file time | Frozen |
| `reason_code` | Enum | See Appendix J `contest_reason_code`: `accidental_trigger`, `outcome_resolver_bug_suspected`, `model_quality_defect`, `duplicate_operation`, `wrong_capability_invoked`, `auto_filed_late_signal`, `customer_other` | Categorical reason |
| `reason_narrative` | String | 50–4000 chars; required for non-`auto_filed_late_signal` | Customer's explanation |
| `original_settlement_state` | Enum | `accepted`, `auto_accepted` | Snapshot at file time; restored if contest rejected |
| `original_charge_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of `effective_charge_cents` at file time |
| `provenance_hash_at_file` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | MUST match AIOperation.`provenance_hash`; mismatch rejects file with HTTP 422 `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch` |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `contest_status`: `open`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, `escalated` | See state machine |
| `ops_reviewer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | Assigned via Ops queue |
| `ops_review_started_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `ops_decision_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `ops_decision_note_internal` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-private rationale |
| `ops_decision_note_customer_visible` | String | 0–2000 chars | Returned in API and Billing Ledger UI |
| `resolution_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `contest_resolution_reason`: `outcome_resolver_bug`, `model_quality_defect`, `duplicate_operation_confirmed`, `accidental_trigger_acknowledged`, `customer_education_provided_no_credit`, `ops_discretion_credit`, `ops_discretion_no_credit`, `withdrawn_by_customer` | Drives `approved` vs `rejected` interpretation |
| `credit_amount_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | When `status=approved`, the credit returned to wallet (typically equals `original_charge_cents`; partial credits permitted) |
| `credit_posted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `escalation_target` | Enum | Nullable; `ops_finance_lead`, `cfo`, `legal` | When status=escalated |
| `sla_breach_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when `ops_review_started_at` not set within SLA (default 5 business days from `created_at`); pages Ops Finance |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR system | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial record |

**Indexes.** `(ai_operation_id)` unique, `(org_id, created_at DESC)` for customer Billing Ledger Contest tab, `(status, sla_breach_at)` partial for Ops queue, `(ops_reviewer_user_id, status)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.** Customer reads scoped per console (mirrors AIOperation); `billing_admin` and `org_admin` see all of their Org's contests. Ops sees all. Cross-Org reads return HTTP 404 `contest_cross_org_access`.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `open` | Customer files OR system auto-files | AIOperation.`settlement_state ∈ {accepted, auto_accepted}` AND `now ≤ AIOperation.contest_window_at` AND no prior ContestRecord | AIOperation transitions to `contested`; soft credit to wallet |
| `open` | `in_review` | Ops picks up from queue | `ops_reviewer_user_id` set; `ops_review_started_at` stamped | |
| `in_review` | `approved` | Ops approves credit | `resolution_reason ∈ {outcome_resolver_bug, model_quality_defect, duplicate_operation_confirmed, accidental_trigger_acknowledged, ops_discretion_credit}`; `credit_amount_cents` set | AIOperation transitions to `reversed`; final credit posted |
| `in_review` | `rejected` | Ops rejects credit | `resolution_reason ∈ {customer_education_provided_no_credit, ops_discretion_no_credit}` | AIOperation restores to `original_settlement_state`; soft credit reversed |
| `in_review` | `escalated` | Ops escalates | `escalation_target` set | Ops Finance lead picks up |
| `escalated` | `approved` / `rejected` | Escalation owner decides | | |
| `open` | `withdrawn` | Customer withdraws | Customer initiated | AIOperation restores to `original_settlement_state`; soft credit reversed |

**SLA.** Default 5 business days from `created_at` to `ops_review_started_at`; breach pages Ops Finance with `contest.sla_breach` webhook. Default 10 business days to `ops_decision_at`; breach escalates to `ops_finance_lead`.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Contest filed past window.** Resolved: write-time check; HTTP 410 `ai_operation_contest_window_expired`.
2. **AIOperation already in `contested` state.** Resolved: HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed`.
3. **Customer files contest, then deletes wallet (Org closure).** Resolved: contest preserved as financial record; on approval, credit posts to a Stripe credit note (not the closed wallet); customer-visible note explains.
4. **Provenance hash mismatch (e.g., AIOperation re-derived after contest filed).** Resolved: write-time check; HTTP 422 `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch`.
5. **Auto-filed contest from late signal arrives during DSAR redaction.** Resolved: auto-file rejected with `contest_locked_for_dsar` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 423); Ops alerted to handle out-of-band.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A ContestRecord MUST be filed only against an AIOperation with `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, auto_accepted}` AND `now ≤ contest_window_at`.
2. Filing MUST atomically transition the AIOperation to `contested` and place a soft credit on the wallet.
3. Approval MUST atomically transition the AIOperation to `reversed`, post the final credit, and stamp `credit_posted_at`.
4. Rejection MUST atomically restore the AIOperation to `original_settlement_state` and reverse the soft credit.
5. Auto-filed contests MUST set `filed_by_user_id=null`, `reason_code=auto_filed_late_signal`, and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes.
6. SLA breaches MUST emit `contest.sla_breach` webhook within 10 minutes of breach.

### 4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog (Platform-Scoped, Nightly Audit Record) {#4.8.6-costbaserecalculationlog}

**Authoring Intent.** CostBaseRecalculationLog is the per-run audit record of the nightly job that re-derives `cost_base_cents` for every active capability from actual Anthropic billing, Convex compute attribution, and external-provider billing. Per Summary C.77 the job runs nightly; drift > 10% triggers a Finance alert; the margin floor is enforced at price-update time with explicit override audit. Per Pricing Strategy §11 the cost_base re-derivation is the mechanism that holds the customer-visible value-dollar pricing constant across underlying Anthropic price moves. The log is the authoritative trail that every cost_base value an AIOperation locks against was approved (auto or manual) at a known time with a known approver.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; one row per recalc run per `(capability_id, model_tier)` pair. Reads gated to `ops_finance_admin`. Public Pricing API publishes a digest derived from this log (effective_at, capability_id, value_price_cents, cost_price_cents) — never the raw cost_base.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `run_batch_id` | UUID | Required | Groups all rows produced by a single nightly run |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id` | |
| `model_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_model_tier` | |
| `prior_cost_base_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Cost basis prior to this recalc |
| `new_cost_base_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Newly computed cost basis |
| `prior_value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot for diff |
| `new_value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Newly published value price |
| `prior_cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | |
| `new_cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | |
| `drift_percent` | Decimal(8,4) | Signed | `(new - prior) / max(prior, 1) × 100`; can be negative if prices fell |
| `drift_severity` | Enum | See Appendix J `cost_base_recalc_drift_severity`: `normal` (`|drift| ≤ 5%`), `warning_5_10` (`5 < |drift| ≤ 10`), `alert_10_25` (`10 < |drift| ≤ 25`), `critical_gt_25` (`|drift| > 25`) | Drives notification routing |
| `approval_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `cost_base_recalc_approval_status`: `auto_applied`, `pending_finance_approval`, `approved`, `overridden`, `rolled_back` | See state machine |
| `auto_applied_reason` | String | ≤ 500 chars; required when `approval_status=auto_applied` | E.g., "drift within 5% threshold; auto-applied per policy" |
| `approver_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Ops with `ops_finance_admin` | Required when `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` |
| `approver_decision_note` | String | 0–4000 chars | Required when `approval_status=overridden` |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this cost_base became effective for new AIOperations |
| `rolled_back_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; UTC | Set if a subsequent run rolled back this row |
| `rollback_reason` | String | 0–4000 chars; nullable | |
| `inputs_summary_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Snapshot of inputs used (Anthropic billing line items, Convex compute aggregates, external provider billings, sample size) |
| `model_id_at_recalc` | String | ≤ 120 chars | Anthropic model id observed during the sample period |
| `sample_size_operations` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Number of AIOperations contributing to the sample (per capability + tier) |
| `sample_window_started_at` | Timestamp | UTC | |
| `sample_window_ended_at` | Timestamp | UTC | |
| `margin_at_value_price_pct` | Decimal(6,3) | Computed | Margin floor check: must remain ≥ 88% per Pricing Strategy §2.6 |
| `margin_floor_breach` | Boolean | Default false | True if `margin_at_value_price_pct < 88` even at the new price; routes to Ops Finance for explicit override or capability deprecation |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (cron) OR Ops (manual recalc trigger) | |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops on approval | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | |

**Indexes.** `(capability_id, model_tier, effective_at DESC)` for the AIOperation cost-base lookup, `(run_batch_id)` for run-level queries, `(approval_status, drift_severity)` partial for the Ops queue, `(margin_floor_breach)` partial where true.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `auto_applied` | Recalc run with `drift_severity ∈ {normal, warning_5_10}` AND `margin_floor_breach=false` | Auto-applied; capability rate card published in next minute | |
| (init) | `pending_finance_approval` | Recalc run with `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` OR `margin_floor_breach=true` | Approver assigned via Ops queue; AIOperations continue at prior price until approval | |
| `pending_finance_approval` | `approved` | Ops Finance approves | New price effective at approval timestamp | |
| `pending_finance_approval` | `overridden` | Ops Finance overrides (e.g., deprecates capability instead of accepting margin breach) | `approver_decision_note` required (≥ 50 chars) | |
| `auto_applied` / `approved` | `rolled_back` | Subsequent recalc detects the prior recalc was wrong (e.g., Anthropic billing data revised) | `rollback_reason` required | |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Anthropic billing data delayed (sample window has insufficient data).** Resolved: recalc skips capabilities with `sample_size_operations < 10` for the window; logs `insufficient_sample` warning; prior cost_base remains.
2. **Margin floor breach on a critical capability.** Resolved: requires Ops Finance override OR capability deprecation; never silently accepted.
3. **Two recalc runs fire concurrently (cron + manual).** Resolved: optimistic lock on `(run_batch_id)` uniqueness; second run rejected with HTTP 409.
4. **Drift calculation on a brand-new capability with `prior_cost_base_cents=0`.** Resolved: `prior_cost_base_cents=0` produces `drift_percent=NULL` (sentinel); routed to `pending_finance_approval` regardless.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The recalc job MUST run nightly at 03:00 UTC with idempotent retry on failure; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour.
2. `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` MUST require explicit `ops_finance_admin` approval before publication.
3. A `margin_floor_breach=true` row MUST NEVER auto-apply; it MUST require explicit override or deprecation.
4. AIOperation writes MUST lock against the most recent `approved` or `auto_applied` log row for `(capability_id, model_tier)` at the time of the AIOperation `created_at`.
5. The Public Pricing API publish MUST occur within 60 seconds of any new approved/auto-applied row; QA test `cost_base_recalc_publish_latency` asserts.

### 4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter (Org-Scoped, Per-Capability) {#4.8.7-freeallowancecounter}

**Authoring Intent.** FreeAllowanceCounter implements Summary C.80: every customer-billed capability grants 10 free operations on signup as a PLG lever. The counter is per-Org per-capability with a default lifetime quota (no period reset) overridable by Ops or by capability-level settings (`free_allowance_resets_per_period=true` for capabilities where Ops has configured a per-period replenishment). Exhaustion surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the ROI of the operations already run.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one row per `(org_id, capability_id)` pair. Reads scoped to Org members per console rules; writes are atomic decrement-and-return via the AI invocation handler.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id` | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `cross_console` | When `cross_console`, the counter applies regardless of which console invokes (e.g., KB Suggestion); console-specific counters allow per-console PLG levers |
| `quota_total` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Total allowance; default 10 (Summary C.80); Ops-overridable |
| `quota_consumed` | Integer | ≥ 0; ≤ quota_total | Used count |
| `quota_remaining` | Integer | Computed (`quota_total - quota_consumed`) | Denormalized for read-path; reconciled at write |
| `resets_per_period` | Boolean | Default false | Mirrors CapabilityRegistryEntry.`free_allowance_resets_per_period` |
| `current_period_started_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | When `resets_per_period=true` |
| `current_period_ends_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | |
| `last_consumed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last decrement |
| `last_consumed_ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → AIOperation | |
| `exhaustion_cta_surfaced_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamped on first exhaustion event for ROI-on-exhaustion UI |
| `roi_value_dollars_at_exhaustion` | Integer | Nullable | Sum of `value_price_cents` of the consumed operations at exhaustion (the "ROI of free ops") |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `free_allowance_counter_status`: `active`, `exhausted`, `reset` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (on first invocation of the capability by the Org) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete on Org closure |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, capability_id)` unique, `(status, current_period_ends_at)` partial for period-reset sweep.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Race between two concurrent operations consuming the last free unit.** Resolved: atomic decrement (`UPDATE ... WHERE quota_remaining > 0 RETURNING quota_remaining`); loser's invocation transitions to wallet-billed without retry overhead.
2. **Ops increases `quota_total` mid-flight.** Resolved: increase takes effect immediately for future operations; in-flight operations unaffected.
3. **Counter for a deprecated capability.** Resolved: counter remains; if the capability is still invokable within deprecation grace, decrement continues.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The first invocation of a customer-billed capability by an Org MUST atomically create a FreeAllowanceCounter row with `quota_total = CapabilityRegistryEntry.free_allowance_quantity_default`.
2. Decrement MUST be atomic and consistent: no two operations may simultaneously consume the last unit.
3. Exhaustion MUST stamp `exhaustion_cta_surfaced_at` and `roi_value_dollars_at_exhaustion` on first exhaustion only; subsequent attempts skip directly to wallet-bill flow.
4. AIOperation rows consumed against this counter MUST set `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`.

### 4.8.8 CommittedSpendContract (Org-Scoped, Enterprise) {#4.8.8-committedspendcontract}

**Authoring Intent.** CommittedSpendContract represents an Enterprise customer's annual AI value-dollar commit per Summary C.81 and Pricing Strategy §6: 10% discount at $25K commit, 15% at $50K, 20% at $100K, 25% at $250K+. The commit replaces the static Enterprise tier's token budget (v6.0.0 §34 model) with a per-Org pre-paid commit pool that AIOperations preferentially burn down before drawing the AIWallet's standard `budget_value_dollars`.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; many active contracts permitted in theory but typically one (overlapping commits handled below).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `contract_external_ref` | String | ≤ 200 chars | DocuSign / Salesforce / CRM external reference; preserved for audit |
| `commit_value_dollars` | Integer | ≥ 1200000 (per Pricing Strategy §6: $12K/yr floor) | In USD cents, integer |
| `discount_band` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_discount_band`: `none`, `band_25k_10pct`, `band_50k_15pct`, `band_100k_20pct`, `band_250k_25pct` | Derived from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; locked |
| `effective_discount_pct` | Integer | 0–25 | Mirrors `discount_band` for query convenience |
| `commit_period_start` | Timestamp | UTC | Annual contract start |
| `commit_period_end` | Timestamp | UTC | Annual contract end |
| `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Live burn-down |
| `shortfall_policy` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_shortfall_policy`: `forfeit`, `partial_credit_next_year`, `rollover_capped` | Sales-negotiated; default `forfeit` |
| `shortfall_rollover_max_pct` | Integer | 0–25 | When `shortfall_policy=rollover_capped`, max % of commit that may roll forward |
| `auto_renew` | Boolean | Default false | When true, contract auto-renews 30 days before expiry at the same band |
| `auto_renew_notice_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When the auto-renewal notice was issued |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_status`: `pending_signature`, `active`, `expired`, `terminated`, `auto_renewed` | See state machine |
| `signed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; user from customer side | |
| `signed_by_sourcera_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Sourcera Sales Ops user | |
| `linked_wallet_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIWallet | The wallet this commit funds |
| `linked_legal_entity` | Enum | mirrors AIWallet | |
| `linked_billing_currency` | Enum | mirrors AIWallet | |
| `terminated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `terminated_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `customer_request`, `sourcera_breach`, `customer_breach`, `acquisition`, `bankruptcy` | |
| `posthog_event_published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamps `commit.signed` event publish |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Sales Ops user | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Sales Ops or System (auto-renew) | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, status, commit_period_end DESC)`, `(linked_wallet_id, status)` partial where `status=active`, `(commit_period_end, auto_renew)` partial for the auto-renew sweep.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending_signature` | Sales Ops drafts | DocuSign envelope sent | |
| `pending_signature` | `active` | Both parties sign | Wallet linked; commit pool funded | AIOperations begin burn-down |
| `active` | `expired` | `commit_period_end < now` AND no auto-renew | `shortfall_policy` applied (forfeit / partial credit / rollover) | |
| `active` | `auto_renewed` | `auto_renew=true` AND 30 days before `commit_period_end` | New CommittedSpendContract row created with new period; this row transitions to `expired` on period end | |
| `active` | `terminated` | Contract terminated mid-period | `terminated_at` stamped; remaining commit handled per termination clause (typically forfeit) | |

**Overlapping Commits.** When two commits are simultaneously `active` for the same Org (rare, e.g., an early-renewal scenario), AIOperations burn down the commit with the **earlier `commit_period_end`** first; this prevents stranded balances on the expiring contract.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Customer terminates mid-period with unspent commit.** Resolved: `shortfall_policy=forfeit` is default; alternative policies require Sales Ops explicit configuration at signature.
2. **Auto-renewal with FX move.** Resolved: auto-renewal preserves the prior `linked_billing_currency`; FX is locked at the time AIOperations charge against the new commit, not at renewal.
3. **Two commits both active and AIOperation burns from one — race against contract overlap window.** Resolved: deterministic burn-priority (earlier `commit_period_end` first); single-row update with optimistic lock.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. `commit_value_dollars` MUST be ≥ $12,000 (1,200,000 cents) — per Pricing Strategy §6 Enterprise floor.
2. `discount_band` MUST be derived deterministically from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; manual override rejected with HTTP 422 `committed_spend_discount_band_mismatch` (new; Appendix I).
3. AIOperations from Orgs with an active commit MUST burn down the commit pool before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`.
4. Overlapping active commits MUST burn earlier-ending first; QA test `committed_spend_overlap_burn_priority` asserts.
5. Auto-renewal MUST issue a customer notification 30 days before `commit_period_end`; opt-out window is 7 days before renewal.

### 4.8.9 PricingTableVersion (Platform-Scoped, Public-API-Backing) {#4.8.9-pricingtableversion}

**Authoring Intent.** PricingTableVersion is the publish-time snapshot that backs the Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Each new active CapabilityRegistryEntry change, each approved CostBaseRecalculationLog, and each plan-tier price change produces a new PricingTableVersion. The version is immutable once published; customers can pin a version for forecasting reproducibility.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped. Publicly readable (no auth) for `status=published` rows; Ops-only for drafts.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `version_label` | String | semver-like, e.g., `2026.04.15.001` | Human-readable; chronological |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `pricing_table_version_status`: `draft`, `published`, `superseded`, `rolled_back` | |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this version becomes the canonical Public Pricing API response |
| `superseded_by_version_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | |
| `published_payload_json` | JSON | ≤ 1,048,576 bytes (1 MB) | Full rate card snapshot: capabilities, value_price_cents, cost_price_cents, currencies, plan tiers, free allowances, retry curves, deprecation banners |
| `published_payload_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | For client-side change detection |
| `included_currencies` | Array[Enum] | mirrors `billing_currency` | Currencies for which conversions are precomputed |
| `included_capability_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized for monitoring |
| `triggering_change_summary` | String | 0–4000 chars | Free text describing what changed since prior version |
| `triggering_changes_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Structured diff: capability_id → field → prior → new |
| `breaking_change_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when a customer-visible price increase or capability removal occurs; triggers 30-day-advance customer notification per Pricing Strategy §11 |
| `customer_notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Required when `breaking_change_flag=true`; sent ≥ 30 days before `effective_at` |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | UTC; null while draft |
| `published_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; only mutable in `draft` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial / audit record |

**Indexes.** `(status, effective_at DESC)`, `(version_label)` unique, `(superseded_by_version_id)` partial.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Publish race with concurrent capability change.** Resolved: publish takes a snapshot at the publish transaction commit time; subsequent changes produce a new version.
2. **Customer pins a `superseded` version then expects current behavior.** Resolved: pinning is a forecasting tool only; AIOperation pricing always uses the current `published` version, not the pinned one.
3. **`breaking_change_flag=true` without 30-day notification.** Resolved: publish rejected with HTTP 422 `pricing_table_breaking_change_requires_30d_notice` (new; Appendix I); Ops must schedule notification first.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The Public Pricing API MUST return the `published_payload_json` of the row with the most recent `effective_at` ≤ `now` and `status=published`.
2. A new published row MUST atomically transition the prior row to `superseded`.
3. `breaking_change_flag=true` MUST require `customer_notification_sent_at ≥ effective_at - 30 days`.
4. The endpoint MUST be cacheable for 60 seconds with the `published_payload_hash` as the ETag.
5. Cursor-based pagination MUST follow §32 patterns; default 50, max 250 (rate cards may grow large).

### 4.8.10 DowngradeExcessDataBucket (Org-Scoped, 90-Day Read-Only Preservation) {#4.8.10-downgradeexcessdatabucket}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary C.85 and Pricing Strategy §9 / Seller §17.4, plan downgrades preserve excess data in **read-only mode for 90 days** before archival; customers may upgrade back and restore active access without data loss. DowngradeExcessDataBucket is the per-Org-per-data-class record of what was preserved when the downgrade occurred. It is the single source of truth for "what would I lose if I let the 90-day clock run out" and powers the customer-visible preservation banner.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one row per `(org_id, data_class)` pair per downgrade event. Cross-console: a downgrade on the seller plan creates seller-data buckets; a downgrade on the buyer plan creates buyer-data buckets; an Org with both plans downgrading independently has independent buckets.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller` | Which console the downgrade affects |
| `data_class` | Enum | See Appendix J `downgrade_excess_data_class`: `workspaces`, `requirements_over_cap`, `kb_entries_over_cap`, `vendors_over_cap`, `capability_declarations_over_cap`, `seller_software_over_cap`, `firecrawl_sources_over_cap`, `concurrent_bids_over_cap`, `seller_signals_over_cap`, `evaluations_over_cap` | What's preserved |
| `entity_ids_preserved` | Array[UUID] | ≤ 100,000 elements | The specific entity ids made read-only |
| `entity_count_preserved` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized for UI |
| `prior_plan_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J Plan Tiers | Plan held before downgrade |
| `new_plan_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J Plan Tiers | Plan after downgrade |
| `downgrade_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When downgrade took effect |
| `preservation_until` | Timestamp | UTC | `downgrade_at + 90 days` (Summary C.85) |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `downgrade_excess_bucket_status`: `active_preservation`, `notice_sent_d60`, `notice_sent_d80`, `archive_pending`, `archived`, `restored` | |
| `notice_d60_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | 30-day-prior notice |
| `notice_d80_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | 10-day-prior notice |
| `archived_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When entities were hard-archived |
| `archive_storage_ref` | String | ≤ 500 chars; nullable | Cold-storage pointer (S3 Glacier or equivalent); 7-year retention for legal |
| `restored_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When customer upgraded back and restored access |
| `restored_by_plan_tier` | Enum | Nullable | Which plan tier they upgraded to |
| `restoration_partial` | Boolean | Default false | True when only a subset of entities fit under the restored plan |
| `restoration_partial_kept_ids` | Array[UUID] | Nullable | Subset restored to active; remainder remain in bucket |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (downgrade handler) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Audit record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, status)`, `(preservation_until)` partial where `status IN (active_preservation, notice_sent_d60, notice_sent_d80)` for the daily sweep, `(console, data_class)` for reporting.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active_preservation` | Downgrade handler runs | Entities transitioned to read-only; `preservation_until` stamped | Customer-visible banner |
| `active_preservation` | `notice_sent_d60` | 60 days post-downgrade (30 days remaining) | Email + in-app notification | |
| `notice_sent_d60` | `notice_sent_d80` | 80 days post-downgrade (10 days remaining) | Email + in-app | |
| `notice_sent_d80` | `archive_pending` | `preservation_until` reached | Hard-archive cron picks up next run | |
| `archive_pending` | `archived` | Cron archives entities to cold storage | `archive_storage_ref` set; entities hard-deleted from hot storage; metadata preserved | |
| `active_preservation` / `notice_sent_*` / `archive_pending` | `restored` | Customer upgrades back AND restoration eligible | Entities restored to active; `restored_at` stamped; partial restoration marked when applicable | |
| `archived` | `restored` | Customer upgrades AND requests restore-from-cold within 90 days post-archive | Cold-storage rehydration; SLA: 24 hours; Ops-assisted | Beyond 180 days post-archive: data is permanently lost (legal-retention only) |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Customer upgrades to a tier insufficient to re-cover all preserved entities.** Resolved: `restoration_partial=true`; remaining entities stay in bucket; UI surfaces upgrade-to-cover-all CTA.
2. **Hard-archive cron crashes mid-archive.** Resolved: idempotent archiving via `archive_storage_ref` checkpoint; restart resumes at the next unarchived entity.
3. **DSAR right-to-erasure for an Org with `archived` data.** Resolved: DSAR handler purges cold-storage rows in addition to hot-storage; legal-retention exception preserved per `data_retention_tier=extended_financial` if applicable.
4. **Org deleted during preservation.** Resolved: bucket transitions to `archived` immediately on Org deletion; no preservation hold survives Org deletion.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Plan downgrade MUST transition affected entities to read-only within 5 minutes of downgrade; QA test `downgrade_readonly_latency` asserts.
2. The 60-day and 80-day notices MUST be one-shot per bucket; idempotency stamps prevent duplicates.
3. Hard-archive MUST occur exactly at `preservation_until` (± 1 hour) via daily sweep; missed sweep alerts Ops.
4. Restoration on upgrade MUST be atomic: either all eligible entities restore or none; partial restoration is a separate flow with explicit user confirmation.
5. Archive cold-storage MUST retain entities for 7 years (legal); restoration window is 90 days post-archive.

### 4.8.11 BillingSeatSnapshot (Org-Scoped, Reporting-Only, Periodic) {#4.8.11-billingseatsnapshot}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary C.86, Sourcera does NOT charge per seat — but the billing layer counts active seats for reporting and plan-gate enforcement (`max_members` in §4.2.1). BillingSeatSnapshot is the periodic point-in-time count of active seats per Org per console for analytics, plan-gate enforcement, and Stripe invoice line-item context (informational only — no per-seat charge). Guests and API-only identities are excluded.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; rows are immutable snapshots (one per `(org_id, console, taken_at)` tuple). Many snapshots over time; older snapshots downsampled per retention rules.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `both` | `both` for combined snapshots; per-console for plan-gate evaluations |
| `taken_at` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | Snapshot moment |
| `trigger` | Enum | See Appendix J `billing_seat_snapshot_trigger`: `monthly_cron`, `plan_change`, `manual_audit`, `stripe_invoice_generation`, `dsar_request`, `ops_capacity_review` | Why the snapshot was taken |
| `active_seats_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Excludes guests, API-only identities, deleted users |
| `guest_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Reported separately; not billable but visible for context |
| `api_only_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | API-only identities (token-only users); also non-billable |
| `deleted_count_30d` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Members deleted in the trailing 30 days; preserved for audit |
| `seat_breakdown_by_role_json` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Per-role breakdown (e.g., `{"org_owner":1,"org_admin":3,"member":47,"guest":12}`) |
| `seat_breakdown_by_team_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Per-team rollup for the console |
| `plan_max_members_at_snapshot` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of `Organization.max_members` at the moment |
| `plan_gate_breach_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when `active_seats_count > plan_max_members_at_snapshot` (a soft-gate condition that surfaces an upgrade prompt) |
| `linked_stripe_invoice_id` | String | Nullable; ≤ 200 chars | Set when `trigger=stripe_invoice_generation` |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; equal to `taken_at` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Reporting record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, console, taken_at DESC)` for the time-series read, `(plan_gate_breach_flag, taken_at)` partial where true for the breach-cohort dashboard, `(trigger, taken_at)` for trigger-correlated reporting.

**Retention.** Daily snapshots retained for 90 days; weekly downsamples retained for 1 year; monthly downsamples retained for 7 years. Snapshots tied to a specific `linked_stripe_invoice_id` retained as long as the invoice (7 years for SOC-2).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Snapshot taken during a bulk-import (1,000 users in 60 seconds).** Resolved: snapshot uses the database snapshot-isolation level; a long bulk-import is captured at the snapshot moment, not as a transient mid-state.
2. **Plan downgrade between snapshot and Stripe invoice.** Resolved: `plan_max_members_at_snapshot` is the snapshot-time value; subsequent downgrade does not retroactively rewrite the snapshot.
3. **Snapshot for an Org with no `seller` console plan.** Resolved: per-console snapshots only when the Org has the corresponding plan active; `console=both` snapshots always taken.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Monthly snapshots MUST run on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC for every active Org.
2. Plan-change events MUST trigger an immediate snapshot within 60 seconds.
3. `active_seats_count` MUST exclude guests, API-only identities, and members with `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`.
4. `plan_gate_breach_flag` MUST be informational only — Sourcera does not block invoicing when seat counts exceed the soft cap; the breach surfaces as an upgrade prompt to `org_owner` and `billing_admin`.
5. Snapshots MUST be immutable post-creation; any update attempt rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_seat_snapshot_immutable` (new; Appendix I).
6. The Public Pricing API MUST NOT expose per-seat pricing; QA test `pricing_api_no_per_seat_pricing` asserts.

# 5\. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) {#5.-rbac-(role-based-access-control)}

## 5.1 RBAC Architecture {#5.1-rbac-architecture}

Sourcera implements role-based access control at two levels:

1. **Org-Level Roles:** Govern access to organization-scoped resources (members, teams, billing, org settings).  
2. **Console-Level Roles:** Govern access to console-scoped resources (workspaces, requirements, bids, marketplace).

Each user can hold multiple roles across different orgs and workspaces. Guest roles are workspace-scoped and configurable with permission profiles.

## 5.2 Org-Level Roles {#5.2-org-level-roles}

| Role | Permissions | Capabilities |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Org Owner** | All org-scoped resources | Create/edit/delete orgs, create/delete workspaces, manage team members, manage billing, manage SSO, view audit logs, manage integrations |
| **Org Admin** | All org-scoped resources except billing | Create/delete workspaces, manage team members, manage SSO, view audit logs, manage integrations (cannot change plan, cannot manage billing) |
| **Member** | Limited org-scoped visibility | View team membership, view shared team resources (no org management) |
| **Billing Admin** | Org-scoped, console-pooled billing & AI-accounting surface only; orthogonal to `org_admin` | Read AIWallet, AIOperation ledger, FreeAllowanceCounter, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, BillingSeatSnapshot, PricingTableVersion across both consoles; mutate wallet overage, caps, manual top-ups, and auto-topup configuration; file, withdraw, and respond to ContestRecord; change plan tier (Free/Business/Enterprise; Enterprise tier-changes still gated on Sales-Ops sign-off per §34.12.5); accept or reject Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side (§34.13); opt out of or opt back into CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal (§4.8.8); pin a PricingTableVersion for forecasting (§4.8.9); export Billing Ledger and Pricing Ledger CSVs. EXPLICITLY denied: workspace data access (Use Cases, Requirements, Responses, Scores, Selection Reports, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, Capability Declarations); SSO/SCIM/IP-restriction configuration; org-membership management (granting roles, inviting members); Audit Log access outside the Billing Admin Audit View (see §5.2.1.4); cross-Org billing access; any Ops Console action. |

### 5.2.1 Billing Admin (Authored Extension — Phase-4 RBAC Integration) {#5.2.1-billing-admin}

**Authoring Intent.** Billing Admin is the org-scoped, console-pooled role that owns the billing-and-AI-accounting surface authored in §4.8 (AIWallet, AIOperation ledger, FreeAllowanceCounter, OutcomeContract observation, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, BillingSeatSnapshot). The role is introduced in v7.0.0 per Master Summary §6.22.1 and Summary C.75–C.87 to separate billing authority from organizational administration: a Finance or Procurement-Ops user can be granted Billing Admin without inheriting workspace, member, SSO, or integration management. The role is orthogonal to `org_admin` (a user MAY hold both, but neither implies the other), and it is the single role permitted to mutate billing configuration, file contests, change plan tier, or accept Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side per §34.14.7 acceptance criterion 33.

**Scope.** Org-scoped. The role is held against an Organization, applies uniformly across the buyer and seller consoles (the AIWallet, billing ledger, and contest queue are pooled per §4.8.3; the Dual-Console Firewall does not partition billing authority). The role is NOT bid-workspace-scoped, workspace-scoped, or marketplace-domain-scoped; a Billing Admin sees no workspace contents. Cross-Org reads are denied: a Billing Admin attempting any read against another Org's billing surface receives HTTP 404 with `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404 to avoid leaking Org existence).

#### 5.2.1.1 Permission List (Operation-by-Operation)

Each line below maps to a concrete API operation, Convex mutation, or scheduled job that enforces the permission. Operations marked "API" map to public REST surfaces in §32; operations marked "Convex" are server-side mutations callable only via the in-app surfaces; operations marked "Stripe webhook ingress" are not directly invocable by humans but the Billing Admin's configuration changes drive the parameters that the webhook handler consumes.

| # | Operation | Surface | RBAC Check | Audit Action (§5.2.1.4 / Appendix J) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Read AIWallet (own Org) | API: `GET /v1/billing/wallet`; Convex: `billing.wallet.get` | `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin (read-only), billing_admin}` | `org.wallet_viewed` |
| 2 | Mutate `auto_topup_enabled` | API: `PATCH /v1/billing/wallet/auto-topup`; Convex: `billing.wallet.setAutoTopupEnabled` | `role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin}` | `org.wallet_autotopup_enabled` / `org.wallet_autotopup_disabled` |

**Explicit Non-Permissions.** The following operations MUST return HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient` (new; Appendix I) when attempted by a user holding only `billing_admin`:

| Disallowed Operation | Surface | Reason |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Read or write any Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Score, Scenario, Selection Report, Selection Record | §32 workspace endpoints | Workspace data is firewalled from billing surface; Billing Admin has no workspace membership |
| Read or write any Bid Workspace, Bid Response, Bid Task, Capability Declaration, KB entry, Document Library item | §32 seller endpoints | Same as above; seller data is firewalled |
| Grant or revoke any role (including `billing_admin` itself) | API: `POST /v1/organizations/me/members/{user_id}/roles` | Role assignment is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority per §11947 |
| Configure SSO, SCIM, MFA enforcement, IP restrictions, dynamic API key issuance | §6 endpoints | Identity-and-security configuration is `org_owner` authority |
| Create / delete a workspace; create / delete a Bid Workspace | §32 workspace endpoints | Workspace lifecycle is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority |
| Read full Audit Event log (cross-namespace) | API: `GET /v1/audit-events` (no namespace filter) | Cross-namespace audit log is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority; Billing Admin sees only the Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 |
| Cross-Org read of any billing entity | All billing endpoints with cross-Org `org_id` | HTTP 404 `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (no leakage of Org existence) |
| Ops Console actions of any kind (impersonation, manual wallet adjustment, contest decision, cost-base recalc approval, etc.) | Ops Console surface | Ops Console authority is governed by `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_compliance_admin`, etc., per Appendix J Ops roles |

#### 5.2.1.2 Assignment, Concurrency, and Deprovisioning

**Assignment.** The `billing_admin` role is granted by `org_owner` or `org_admin` via `POST /v1/organizations/me/members/{user_id}/roles` with body `{"role": "billing_admin"}`. Grant requires the target user to be an active member of the Org (not a guest, not an API-only identity, not a deleted user). Assignment is audit-logged as `org.billing_admin_role_granted` with grantor user attribution. The role is NEVER granted by default at Org provisioning; the first Billing Admin (if any) is an explicit Org Owner action. An Org may have zero or more Billing Admins concurrently; there is no maximum cap, but a soft warning surfaces in the Org Owner UI when more than ten Billing Admins are concurrently active (potential blast-radius signal).

**Replacement Pattern.** When an Org has zero Billing Admins (the role is empty), all Billing-Admin-only operations (file ContestRecord, withdraw ContestRecord, change plan tier, accept Pro Trial Seat, opt-out of CommittedSpendContract renewal, etc.) MUST fall back to `org_owner` authority — `org_owner` always retains de facto Billing Admin permissions (per §11947 "granted by org_owner and org_admin; it is not granted by default"). This guarantees the Org is never operationally locked out of its billing surface even if every named Billing Admin departs.

**Deprovisioning.** When a `billing_admin` is deprovisioned (role revoked, member deleted, SSO deactivation), per §34.12.7 Failure Mode #3:

1. The role-revocation transaction stamps `org.billing_admin_role_revoked` with revoker user attribution and a snapshot of the prior assignment (`grantor_user_id`, `granted_at`).
2. Any in-flight Stripe charges initiated by the deprovisioned user complete normally (Stripe's webhook handler is idempotent and does not re-validate caller identity at settlement).
3. Any open ContestRecord filed by the deprovisioned user remains `open` and is owned by the Org's pool of remaining Billing Admins (or `org_owner` if none); the `filed_by_user_id` field is preserved as a historical record but withdrawal authority transfers to the remaining Billing Admin pool.
4. Any pending CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal opt-out request remains active (the request was on the contract, not on the user).
5. Notification routing is recomputed: the deprovisioned user is removed from the recipient union; if the recipient union becomes empty (no `org_owner` either, an inconsistent state by §4.2 invariants), notifications fall back to `ops_finance_admin` for triage.

**SCIM Provisioning Interaction.** Per §6.1 (Authentication Architecture / WorkOS SCIM), the `billing_admin` role is NOT auto-provisioned via SCIM by default — SCIM-provisioned users default to `member`. An Org may opt in (SCIM Role Mapping is an Authored Extension flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` pending §6 SCIM Role Mapping authoring) to map a SAML/SCIM `BillingAdmin` group attribute to the `billing_admin` role; this is an Org Owner action and is audit-logged as `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_enabled` / `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_disabled`. Default-deny is preserved for security.

#### 5.2.1.3 Scope Isolation

| Surface | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Own Org's billing entities (AIWallet, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion pin, BillingSeatSnapshot, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, FreeAllowanceCounter, AIOperation ledger) | Yes | Per Permission List §5.2.1.1 |
| Own Org's workspace data (any console, any bid workspace) | No | HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient` |
| Other Org's billing entities | No | HTTP 404 `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (no Org-existence leakage) |
| Public Pricing API (`api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing`) | Yes | No auth; same as any anonymous reader |
| Ops Console | No | HTTP 403 `ops_role_required` |
| Audit Log (full cross-namespace) | No | HTTP 403 `audit_log_full_view_requires_org_admin`; Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 only |
| Marketplace Listings (read public listings) | Yes | Same as `marketplace_viewer` global access; no special billing privilege |
| Marketplace Listings (publish / edit own Org's listings) | No (unless also `marketplace_publisher`) | Marketplace publication is its own role per §5.6 |

**Cross-Console Pooling.** Because AIWallet is Org-scoped and console-pooled per §4.8.3, a single Billing Admin sees the unified billing position across both consoles in one place (Buyer Growth + Seller Starter Org sees the unified $330/mo budget per Pricing Strategy §11). The Billing Admin Audit View also pools events from both consoles. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) does NOT apply to billing entities — billing is shared by design; workspace content is not.

#### 5.2.1.4 Audit Semantics

Every Billing-Admin-mutated operation MUST emit one Audit Event with `action` ∈ Billing Admin Audit Action Types (Appendix J — new sub-enum), `user_id = caller`, `entity_type ∈ {ai_wallet, contest_record, committed_spend_contract, pricing_table_version, pro_trial_seat_grant, organization_plan, free_allowance_counter, billing_seat_snapshot, downgrade_excess_data_bucket}`, `entity_id = subject id`, and `changes` JSON populated for state mutations (per §4.6.1 Audit Event field semantics). Read operations on billing entities by Billing Admin emit `org.*_viewed` audit events at sample rate 1.0 (no sampling — billing reads are forensic-grade auditable).

The Billing Admin Audit View (Operation #21) is a server-side filter over the Audit Event entity that returns only rows where `action` matches the regex `^org\.(wallet|contest|committed_spend|plan|pro_trial_seat|billing|downgrade_bucket|free_allowance|pricing|scim_billing|billing_admin)_*` AND `org_id = session.org_id`. The view is paginated per §32.3 (cursor-based, default 50, max 250). Filter parameters: `action_namespace`, `entity_type`, `user_id`, `from`, `to`, `status`. Export to CSV is permitted (Operation #8 / `org.billing_audit_exported`).

**Audit Retention.** Billing Admin audit events follow §40.2 standard retention plus §6.24 plan-tier extension: Free 30 days, Business 1 year, Enterprise 7 years. CommittedSpendContract-related audits retain for 7 years on every plan (financial-record exception per §40.2 `extended_financial`). Any audit event tagged `org.contest_*` retains for 7 years on every plan (regulatory contest-trail requirement).

#### 5.2.1.5 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **A user holds both `billing_admin` and `member` (no `org_admin` or `org_owner`); session.org_id matches the wallet's org_id.** Resolved: union-of-permissions semantics — the user gets every permission of every held role; `billing_admin` permissions activate without needing `org_admin`.
2. **A user holds `billing_admin` in Org A and is added to Org B as a `member` only.** Resolved: roles are per-Org-membership; the user has no Billing Admin privileges in Org B; switching the active Org via `X-Sourcera-Active-Org` header re-evaluates.
3. **A `billing_admin` files a ContestRecord, then is deprovisioned 1 second later.** Resolved: filing is atomic; the contest persists; subsequent withdrawal authority transfers to the remaining Billing Admin pool per §5.2.1.2.
4. **Two Billing Admins simultaneously file contests against the same AIOperation.** Resolved: per §4.8.5 the unique constraint on `(ai_operation_id)` permits exactly one ContestRecord; the second filer receives HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed` with the prior contest ID exposed.
5. **A `billing_admin` attempts to read a workspace's audit log to investigate a billing-related dispute.** Resolved: HTTP 403 `audit_log_full_view_requires_org_admin`; the Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 is the sanctioned alternative; if the dispute requires workspace-scope audit, an `org_owner` or `org_admin` must perform the read or the Billing Admin must be granted `org_admin` (auditable).
6. **A `billing_admin` attempts to change plan tier from Buyer Enterprise to Buyer Free without Sales-Ops sign-off.** Resolved: per §34.12.5 Enterprise downgrades are gated on `ops_finance_admin` co-signoff; the API returns HTTP 423 `enterprise_plan_change_requires_ops_signoff` with the Ops ticket creation link.
7. **A `billing_admin` attempts to file a contest 15 days after settlement (1 day past window).** Resolved: per §4.8.5 the write-time check returns HTTP 410 `ai_operation_contest_window_expired`; the response body includes `contest_window_at` and `original_settlement_at` for client-side messaging.
8. **A `billing_admin` is granted to a user whose email domain is not a verified Org domain.** Resolved: assignment proceeds (the user is already an Org member by definition of role-grant prerequisites); the soft warning "Billing Admin granted to a user outside your verified domains" surfaces to the grantor (Org Owner / Admin); audit event captures the warning acknowledgement.
9. **A `billing_admin` triggers a manual top-up that fails Stripe charge 5 times (DLQ).** Resolved: per §4.8.3 Top-Up State Machine the wallet enters `payment_failed_grace`; the Billing Admin receives hourly grace alerts; the audit event sequence is `org.wallet_topup_manual_initiated` → `org.wallet_topup_failed` (system) → `org.wallet_payment_failed_grace_entered` (system) → eventual recovery or `org.wallet_suspended` (system).
10. **A `billing_admin` accepts a Pro Trial Seat grant on the vendor side, but the vendor Org is already on a paid Seller plan.** Resolved: per §34.13.5 the API returns HTTP 409 `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid`; no state transition; audit event `org.pro_trial_seat_acceptance_rejected` records the failed acceptance attempt with reason code.
11. **A `billing_admin` opts out of CommittedSpendContract renewal less than 60 days before `commit_period_end`.** Resolved: per §4.8.8 the API returns HTTP 422 `committed_spend_renewal_opt_out_window_expired`; the contract auto-renews per its `shortfall_policy`.
12. **An Org has zero `billing_admin` users and the `org_owner` user is locked out of MFA.** Resolved: the Org enters a billing-administration deadlock; per §6 (Identity & Security) account-recovery flow, an `ops_finance_admin` may impersonate the `org_owner` under §35 impersonation audit (cross-referenced from §3.8 / §4.8.1 Scope Isolation; the dedicated impersonation-audit section is a long-standing Known Gap and is preserved as the canonical reference per existing spec usage) to reset MFA; alternative: another `org_admin` may re-grant `billing_admin` to themselves and proceed.

#### 5.2.1.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. The `billing_admin` role MUST be enumerated in Appendix J Global Organization Roles; a deploy-time validator asserts the enum contains `billing_admin`.
2. Granting `billing_admin` MUST require the caller to hold `org_owner` OR `org_admin`; HTTP 403 `role_grant_requires_org_admin` otherwise.
3. Granting `billing_admin` MUST be idempotent: re-granting to a user who already holds the role returns HTTP 200 with no audit event re-emit.
4. Revoking `billing_admin` MUST emit `org.billing_admin_role_revoked`; if the revocation reduces the active Billing Admin count to zero AND there is no `org_owner` for the Org, the revocation MUST be rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_admin_revocation_would_leave_org_unmanaged`.
5. Every Permission List operation in §5.2.1.1 MUST emit its declared audit action on success; failure paths emit `<action>` with `status=failure` and `failure_reason`. QA test `billing_admin_audit_completeness` asserts no operation can succeed without a paired audit event.
6. The Billing Admin Audit View MUST exclude all non-billing audit rows; QA test `billing_admin_audit_view_isolation` asserts that workspace, response, score, KB, and capability-declaration audit rows never appear in the view regardless of filter parameters.
7. Cross-Org access attempts by a `billing_admin` MUST return HTTP 404 (not 403); QA test `billing_admin_cross_org_404` asserts.
8. Workspace-data access attempts (any of the explicit non-permissions in §5.2.1.1) MUST return HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient`; QA test `billing_admin_workspace_403` asserts.
9. The Org Owner's de facto Billing Admin authority MUST hold even when the Org has zero `billing_admin` users; QA test `org_owner_billing_fallback` asserts.
10. The 50% / 80% / 100% wallet notifications MUST be delivered to the union of `org_owner` and `billing_admin` users; recipient deduplication MUST occur at dispatch time; QA test `wallet_notification_recipient_union` asserts.
11. The Billing Admin role MUST be assignable to a user holding `org_admin` simultaneously; the union-of-permissions principle holds; QA test `dual_role_org_admin_billing_admin` asserts both role's permissions are active.
12. The Billing Admin role MUST NOT be inherited by `org_owner` or `org_admin`; explicit assignment is required for billing-admin-ONLY operations (Operation #9 file ContestRecord, Operation #11 withdraw ContestRecord) — except that `org_owner` retains the de facto fallback per §5.2.1.2 Replacement Pattern; QA test `billing_admin_role_non_inherited` asserts the matrix.
13. Pinning a PricingTableVersion MUST stamp `org.pricing_table_version_pinned` with `version_label` in the `changes` payload; unpinning MUST emit `org.pricing_table_version_unpinned`.
14. The role MUST be removable by Org Owner or Org Admin without requiring confirmation flows (no soft-delete, no archived state — the role is an active assignment that is either present or absent); deletion is the audit event `org.billing_admin_role_revoked`.
15. SCIM mapping (when opted in) MUST follow the same audit semantics; auto-grants from SCIM MUST stamp `org.billing_admin_role_granted_via_scim` (subset of `org.billing_admin_role_granted` for filter convenience).

#### 5.2.1.7 Glossary Note

The term **Billing Admin** is added to Appendix B Glossary as: "Org-scoped role with billing-and-AI-accounting authority across both consoles. Orthogonal to `org_admin`. Required for filing ContestRecords, mutating wallet configuration, changing plan tier, and accepting Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side. See §5.2, §5.2.1, §4.8, §34.12.6, Appendix J Global Organization Roles."

## 5.3 Console-Level Roles (Buyer Console) {#5.3-console-level-roles-(buyer-console)}

| Role | Workspace-Scoped | Responsibilities | Accessible Features |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Workspace Owner** | Yes | Own & manage workspace, decide on vendors, final approval | Full access to all workspace resources, configuration, team management, phase transitions |
| **Evaluation Lead** | Yes | Oversee evaluation timeline, coordinate scorers, escalate issues | Full access to requirements, responses, scores, phase management (cannot delete workspace) |
| **Evaluator** | Yes | Author requirements, review responses, score requirements, attend demos | Create/edit/delete requirements in assigned Use Cases, score (Phases 10–11), view responses, comment |
| **Scorer** | Yes | Score vendor responses, provide rationale | View requirements and responses, score (Phases 10–11), add score notes, cannot edit requirements |
| **Guest** | Yes | Limited, configurable via Guest Permission Profile | See 5.4 |

## 5.4 Guest Role & Permission Profiles (Gap S-2) {#5.4-guest-role-&-permission-profiles-(gap-s-2)}

Guest is a **workspace-specific role** with **configurable permission profiles** assigned at invitation time. When inviting a Guest to a workspace, the Workspace Owner selects one of four permission profiles:

### 5.4.1 Guest Permission Profile: `read_only`

**Default profile. Maximum restrictions.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| View workspace name, description, phase | Yes | Read-only |
| View Use Cases (assigned only) | Yes | If in `assigned_use_case_ids` |
| View requirements (assigned only) | Yes | If Use Case assigned |
| View vendor responses | Yes | Read-only; assigned requirements only |
| View scores | Yes | Read-only summary; no individual scorer details |
| View Selection Report | No | Report access restricted to Workspace Owner only |
| Create/edit requirements | No |  |
| Delete requirements | No |  |
| Score requirements | No |  |
| Edit workspace settings | No |  |
| Manage team members | No |  |
| Export evaluation | No |  |
| View audit log | No |  |
| View/resolve comments | Yes | Can view and reply to comments; cannot delete others' comments |
| Add comments | Yes | Can comment on assigned requirements |

### 5.4.2 Guest Permission Profile: `contributor`

**Allows requirement authorship within assigned Use Cases.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `read_only`) | Yes |  |
| Create requirement in assigned Use Case | Yes | Must belong to assigned Use Cases |
| Edit requirement (own or any) | Yes | Within assigned Use Cases |
| Delete requirement (own only) | Yes | Within assigned Use Cases |
| View workspace configuration | Yes | Read-only |
| Score requirements | No | Use `scorer` profile for this |
| View Selection Report | No |  |
| Manage settings | No |  |

### 5.4.3 Guest Permission Profile: `scorer`

**Allows requirement scoring only; no authorship.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `read_only`) | Yes |  |
| Score requirements (Phases 10–11) | Yes | Cannot score before Phase 10 |
| Score requirements after Phase 11 (Phase 12\) | No | Scores locked at Phase 12 entry |
| Add score notes | Yes | Notes help explain scoring rationale |
| View score history | Yes | Limited to own scores and aggregated results |
| Create/edit requirements | No |  |
| Delete requirements | No |  |
| View Selection Report | No |  |

### 5.4.4 Guest Permission Profile: `full_participant`

**Combines contributor \+ scorer; maximum guest capability.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `contributor` \+ `scorer`) | Yes |  |
| View Selection Report | Yes | Can view final recommendation and rationale |
| Manage comments (own only) | Yes | Can edit/delete own comments |
| Export evaluation (limited) | Yes | Can export as PDF/CSV (not sensitive metadata) |
| (Workspace management, audit logs, etc.) | No | Still cannot manage workspace or see admin features |

### 5.4.5 Guest Scope Isolation

- **Use Case Scoping:** Guests assigned to specific Use Cases see only those Use Cases and their requirements (if assigned).  
- **Empty Assignment:** If `assigned_use_case_ids` is empty, guest can see all Use Cases and requirements (full visibility within permission profile).  
- **Workspace Isolation:** Guests cannot see other workspaces in the org; invitation is workspace-specific.  
- **Cross-Org:** Guest is always a single-org guest; cannot access other org workspaces.

## 5.5 Console-Level Roles (Seller Console) {#5.5-console-level-roles-(seller-console)}

| Role | Bid-Workspace-Scoped | Responsibilities | Accessible Features |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Bid Owner** | Yes | Own & manage bid workspace, assign team, track responses, interface with buyer | Full access to Bid Workspace, Bid Tasks, Bid Responses, Team management (see Section 2.7 for term definition) |
| **Bid Contributor** | Yes | Complete assigned bid responses, collaborate with team | Create/edit Bid Responses assigned to them, view team collaboration, cannot manage workspace or team |
| **Bid Viewer** | Yes | Track bid status, provide feedback | View Bid Responses (read-only), view Bid Tasks, cannot edit or score (Seller-side; scoring is Buyer-side) |

## 5.6 Marketplace Roles {#5.6-marketplace-roles}

| Role | Scope | Responsibilities | Access |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Marketplace Publisher** | Org-scoped | Create/edit Marketplace Listings, manage Seller Profile | Full access to Seller Profile, Capability Declarations, Marketplace Listings, EOI/NDA records |
| **Marketplace Viewer** | Global | Browse public listings, submit EOI | View published Marketplace Listings, search, filter, submit EOI, no edit access |
