Plan-tier minimum changes are Breaking Changes and trigger the 30-day customer notification path per §34.3.3. The matrix is the single source of truth for runtime entitlement evaluation; the runtime cache loads from this table at deploy time.

### 34.8.6 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Plan downgrade mid-pending AIOperation.** A `pending` AIOperation initiated under the prior plan settles under the prior wallet rules; the new plan's gating applies only to operations created at or after the downgrade effective timestamp. (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #11; §4.8.10).
2. **Wallet hard-cap reached during an in-flight Managed Agent sub-call tree.** Sub-calls follow §4.8.1 Failure Mode #4: the parent operation marks `rejected` with reason `sub_call_wallet_exhausted`; the partial tree is valid; no orphaned wallet hold remains.
3. **A capability is deprecated mid-period but still invokable within deprecation grace.** Entitlement Matrix continues to honor the prior plan-tier minimum; CapabilityRegistryEntry `state=deprecated` does NOT bypass the gate (§4.8.2 acceptance criterion #4).
4. **Org changes plan tier between session start and capability invocation.** Session metadata refreshes on plan-change webhook receipt within 30 seconds (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #2). A pre-refresh invocation may evaluate against the old tier; the Outcome Resolver settles the AIOperation under the entitlement state at write time, not at settlement time.

### 34.8.7 Acceptance Criteria

1. Entitlement check MUST be O(1) on the cache layer; database round trips for plan-tier or wallet-state lookups during entitlement evaluation are forbidden.
2. Soft-gated capabilities MUST surface upgrade CTAs in the result envelope (`upgrade_cta`, `blocked_reason`); hard-gated capabilities MUST return HTTP 403 with the same fields in the error body.
3. Free Allowance MUST be exhausted before any wallet draw for `customer_billed` capabilities; verified by §4.8.7 acceptance criterion #2.
4. Cross-console plan-tier evaluations MUST NOT leak across consoles; QA test `entitlement_dual_console_isolation` asserts.
5. Plan-change webhook MUST refresh session metadata within 30 seconds; QA test `entitlement_plan_change_propagation` asserts.
6. Every customer-billed capability in CapabilityRegistryEntry with `state=active` MUST have a row in the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix; deploy-time validator asserts.

## 34.9 Onboarding and Trial Carry-Over {#34.9-onboarding-and-trial-carry-over}

### 34.9.1 Buyer Onboarding (14-Day Business Starter Trial)

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger | New Org signup via Buyer Console (Google/Microsoft SSO; no credit card) |
| Effective plan | `business_starter` for 14 days |
| Wallet | $50 included budget (Business Starter monthly cap, prorated to the trial period); overage off by default; auto-topup off by default |
| Free Allowance | All `customer_billed` capabilities receive their default 10-op allowance per §4.8.7 |
| End-of-trial behavior (day 15, no payment method) | Auto-downgrade to `buyer_free`; `included_budget_remaining` decrements to $5/mo (Free); excess data flow per §34.6 (DowngradeExcessDataBucket) |
| End-of-trial behavior (day 15, payment method on file) | Conversion to chosen plan tier; carry-over per §34.5.1 |
| Trial-expiry notifications | Day 11: `trial_expiring` (Appendix C, existing). Day 14: `trial_expiring_today` (Appendix C — to be added per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`). Day 15 on auto-downgrade: `plan_downgrade_complete` (existing) + bucket-creation notice if overages |
| Audit | `org.trial_started` and `org.trial_ended` events with actor, plan tier, wallet state |

### 34.9.2 Seller Onboarding (No Trial; Free Is the On-Ramp)

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger | Buyer-invite magic-link click (M1, M5, M15) OR direct seller signup |
| Effective plan | `seller_free` |
| Hero moment | The full SPS §15 "Your first bid is already drafted" flow runs synchronously inside the SSO redirect; KB Bootstrap (Opus, lifetime free) + First-Pass RFP Draft + Published Seller Profile all materialize before the vendor reaches the workspace |
| Wallet | $5 included budget (Seller Free monthly cap); overage off by default; hard cap at $5 (no bill-shock path on Free per BPS §4) |
| Free Allowance | All `customer_billed` seller capabilities receive their default 10-op allowance |
| Anti-pattern controls | Per SPS §16.3 — no credit-card prompt before first upgrade intent click; no pricing page until first bid submitted; no "try Pro free for 14 days" modal on first login |

### 34.9.3 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Carry-Over (M17)

When a vendor receives a Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (§34.13), the 30-day Seller Starter trial supersedes the standard Seller Free onboarding. Vendors who arrive via M17 NEVER see Seller Free ceilings during the trial period; on day 31, the trial completes per §34.13.4 with explicit conversion paths:

| Outcome | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Convert | Plan persists at Seller Starter (or upgraded by vendor); included budget resets on new billing cycle; carry-over per §34.5.1 |
| Auto-downgrade | Plan transitions to Seller Free; entities exceeding Free caps enter §34.6 90-day read-only preservation; vendor is NOT subject to a second auto-downgrade if the vendor declines Free preservation by hard-deleting overages |
| Explicit decline | Same as auto-downgrade |

### 34.9.4 Carry-Over Invariants

- **No data loss on any upgrade or downgrade path.** KB entries, in-flight bids/evaluations, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs, Wallet configuration, Pro Trial Seat balance, and bucket state all persist through plan transitions.
- **Wallet counters do NOT carry over across billing periods.** `included_budget_remaining` resets at each billing anniversary (§4.8.3); unused budget is not banked.
- **`overage_balance` deposits DO carry over across periods** until consumed or refunded.
- **Free Allowance is per-Org per-capability lifetime** (default; configurable per-CapabilityRegistryEntry); plan changes do not reset or replenish.

## 34.10 AI Wallet Service {#34.10-ai-wallet-service}

The AIWallet (§4.8.3) is the org-scoped, console-pooled value-dollar account that every customer-billed AIOperation draws against. Schema, indexes, and wallet/top-up state machines live in §4.8.3 and §4.8.3.A; the §34.10 section fixes the operational policy.

### 34.10.1 Wallet Counters

| Counter | Field on AIWallet | Purpose | Replenishment |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Included Budget | `budget_value_dollars`, less `consumed_value_dollars` | Plan-included monthly allowance in value-dollars | Reset to plan-tier amount at each `current_period_ends_at` (billing anniversary) |
| Overage Balance | `overage_cap_value_dollars`, less `overage_consumed_value_dollars` | Customer-deposited wallet funds drawn after included budget exhausted | On admin-initiated top-up or auto-topup (per §4.8.3.A) |
| Committed Spend Pool (Enterprise) | `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` (denormalized from `CommittedSpendContract.commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars`) | Annual prepaid commit pool | At contract signature; auto-renewal per §4.8.8 |

**Burn priority** (per §4.8.3 Committed Spend Interaction): `commit_burn_remaining → budget_value_dollars (included) → overage_cap_value_dollars (wallet)`. Free Allowance bypasses all three (§4.8.3 Free Allowance Interaction).

All counters are stored in **integer USD cents** (denominated in value-dollars per BPS §11). Presentation in the customer's `billing_currency` is via `fx_rate_locked` at presentation time only; the stored value is never persisted in non-USD.

### 34.10.2 Wallet Configuration

| Setting | Default | Constraint | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Wallet overage enabled | `false` (off) | A `billing_admin` must explicitly enable; admin action audited as `org.wallet_overage_enabled` | BPS §7; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #4 |
| Overage cap | 0 | When enabled, `billing_admin` sets a positive integer cap | BPS §7 |
| Daily / Weekly / Monthly caps | Unset | Each cap is independent; lowest cap binds | BPS §7 |
| Auto-topup enabled | `false` (off) | A `billing_admin` must explicitly enable | BPS §7; MS C.79; §4.8.3 |
| Auto-topup increment | $50–$10,000 single charge | Out-of-range values rejected with HTTP 422 `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range` | MS C.79; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #5 |
| Auto-topup max monthly | $50–$500,000 absolute ceiling | Authored ceiling; flagged for Sales/Finance review per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 4 Known Gaps` | AE; §4.8.3 |
| Notification thresholds | 50%, 80%, 100% of `(budget + overage_cap)`; one-shot per period | Idempotency stamps prevent duplicates | §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #6 |

### 34.10.3 Pooled Budget Across Consoles (Authoritative Rule)

AIWallet balances are **Organization-scoped** and pooled across Buyer and Seller consoles (BPS §13 / SPS §11 / MS §2). An Org holding (Buyer Growth = $300 budget) + (Seller Starter = $30 budget) sees a unified $330 of monthly value-dollars spendable by any capability in either console. The §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #1 enforces this at the schema layer (one wallet row per Org; pooling enforced by the absence of a `console` column on AIWallet).

| Plan combination | Pooled budget | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free + Seller Free | $5 (single wallet; both plans contribute to one $5 pool — see §34.10.4) | BPS §3, SPS §3 |
| Buyer Starter + Seller Free | $50 (Free $5 budget contribution is collapsed when paid plan present — see §34.10.4) | BPS §3 + SPS §3 + AE collapse rule |
| Buyer Growth + Seller Starter | $330 | BPS §5.2 + SPS §5 |
| Buyer Scale + Seller Growth | $1,000 | BPS §5.3 + SPS §6 |
| Buyer Enterprise + Seller Free | Committed (Enterprise $) — Free does not add | BPS §6 |
| Buyer Enterprise + Seller Enterprise | One Committed pool (single contract per §34.12.5) | BPS §6 / SPS §8 / §34.12.5 |

**Free + Free pool collapse rule (Authored Extension).** When both consoles are on Free, the pooled budget is **$5 total** (not $10). Rationale: the $5 Free budget exists as a PLG hook to drive a single ceiling-hit event, not as a doubled budget that delays the upgrade moment. This collapse is consistent with BPS §4 ("hit the ceiling, upgrade") and SPS §4 ("Get invited. Respond. … Hit the ceiling … Upgrade.") but is not explicitly stated in either source. **Logged as Authored Extension in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` for Sales-Ops sign-off.**

**Free + Paid pool collapse rule (Authored Extension).** When one side is Free and the other is paid, the Free side's $5 budget is **collapsed** (not added) to avoid the Free-side budget effectively topping up the paid side. The pooled budget equals the paid side's budget only. **Logged as Authored Extension.**

### 34.10.4 Wallet State Machine (Reference)

The full state machine lives at §4.8.3 (`active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `payment_failed_grace`, `suspended`, `closed`). The §34.10 policy summary:

- 50% threshold → email + in-app to Org Owner + Billing Admin (one-shot)
- 80% threshold → email + in-app; auto-topup may fire here if enabled
- 100% threshold → if no auto-topup or auto-topup capped out: hard-cap; HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` for new customer-billed AIOperations; Sourcera-owned operations continue
- Failed top-up → 48-hour `payment_failed_grace`; wallet remains active during grace; billing admin emailed hourly; on grace expiry → `suspended`
- `suspended` → all customer-billed operations rejected; in-flight `pending` operations may settle (wallet hold honored); Ops alert
- Customer top-up succeeds OR billing period rolls over OR plan upgrade → return to `active`

### 34.10.5 Stripe Metering

Wallet events are reported to Stripe daily (granularity: per-calendar-day; daily roll-up posted to Stripe Meter API). Events:

| Stripe meter event | Trigger | Fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera_ai_value_accepted` | AIOperation transitions `pending → accepted` or `pending → auto_accepted` | org_id, capability_id, value_price_cents, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked |
| `sourcera_ai_value_rejected` | AIOperation transitions `pending → rejected` | org_id, capability_id, cost_price_cents, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked |
| `sourcera_ai_wallet_topup` | Auto-topup or manual top-up succeeds | org_id, top-up amount cents, payment_method_id, billing_currency |
| `sourcera_ai_value_reversed` | AIOperation transitions to `reversed` (approved contest) | org_id, capability_id, reversal_amount_cents |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_grant` | Pro Trial Seat issued (M17, §34.13) | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, trial_expires_at |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` | Vendor converts trial to paid Seller Starter+ on day 30/31 | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, converted_to_plan |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` | Trial auto-downgrades on day 31 with no conversion | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id |
| `sourcera_committed_spend_burn` | Daily roll-up of value-dollars burned against an active CommittedSpendContract | org_id, contract_id, burned_amount_cents |

Stripe customer is bound 1:1 to `(org_id, legal_entity)`; an Org changing residency triggers a new Stripe Customer creation (logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 4 Known Gaps`).

### 34.10.6 Downgrade Behavior (Wallet)

| Trigger | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Plan downgrade (Buyer / Seller) effective at next billing cycle | `budget_value_dollars` decreases to the new plan's monthly amount at billing rollover; `consumed_value_dollars` resets to 0 at rollover; `overage_balance` retained until consumed or refunded; `auto_topup_*` settings retained unless explicitly cleared |
| Enterprise → non-Enterprise downgrade with active CommittedSpendContract | `shortfall_policy` (§4.8.8) determines treatment of unspent commit: `forfeit` (default) → forfeit at contract end; `partial_credit_next_year` → credit applied to next year's renewal; `rollover_capped` → up to `shortfall_rollover_max_pct` (≤ 25%) rolls forward |
| Wallet enters `suspended` from `payment_failed_grace` expiry | All new customer-billed AIOperations rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`; in-flight `pending` operations may settle; Ops alert |
| Org closure / deletion | AIWallet transitions to `closed`; financial records (AIOperation, ContestRecord, etc.) preserved per §40.2 |

### 34.10.7 Failure Modes Addressed (Operational Layer)

1. **Customer enables overage with cap below current period's projected spend.** Resolved: cap-set UI surfaces "projected spend at current burn rate" and warns if cap is below; cap-write proceeds (customer choice); hard-cap behavior follows §34.10.4.
2. **Auto-topup race against Stripe webhook delay.** Resolved: top-up state machine (§4.8.3.A) is single-row optimistic-locked; in-flight charge prevents a second concurrent charge attempt.
3. **Customer disables overage mid-period with active overage_balance.** Resolved: overage_balance remains spendable until consumed; new overage operations beyond included budget are blocked at write time with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`.
4. **Org has paid Buyer plan and Seller Free, then downgrades Buyer to Free.** Resolved: pool collapses to $5 total (Free + Free collapse rule §34.10.3); Wallet state transition is atomic at billing rollover.
5. **Cross-console operation invokes during plan-transition window.** Resolved: §34.8.6 Failure Mode #4 — operation evaluates against entitlement state at write time, not settlement time.

## 34.11 Outcome Resolver {#34.11-outcome-resolver}

The Outcome Resolver is the platform component that classifies every AIOperation as `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, or `rejected` per the bound OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) and writes the corresponding value-dollar amount to the Wallet. The Resolver is platform-scoped, single-tenant per Sourcera deployment, and consumes outcome signals from product surfaces (user clicks, retention thresholds, downstream-use signals) via an event-bus interface. The Resolver is referenced as a Phase 4 Known Gap (component-level system design pending) in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

### 34.11.1 Outcome Contract Registry

The complete per-capability outcome contract registry lives at §4.8.4 OutcomeContract. The §34.11.1 surface is the customer-facing summary of the contract; key contracts mirror BPS Appendix B and SPS §10:

| Capability | Accepted Signal | Window | Timeout Default | OutcomeContract Version (Active) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `pre_scoring` | User confirms or edits ≤ 20% of suggested score | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `requirement_extraction` | Requirement retained in final spec | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_suggestion` | User clicks "use" OR content appears in artifact | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `vendor_summary` | Summary retained unchanged ≥ 80% | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `policy_parsing` | Parsed policy retained AND used in ≥ 1 evaluation | 30d | rejected | v1 |
| `deep_comparison` | Exported, shared, OR linked from artifact | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `response_drafting` | Sent OR retained ≥ 70% unchanged | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `stakeholder_summary` | Shared externally OR retained in final report | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `first_pass_rfp_draft` | ≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid | 14d (or on bid submission) | rejected | v1 |
| `qa_suggestion` | Answer sent with ≤ 30% edit | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_to_capability_suggestion` | Declaration published | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_bootstrap` | ≥ 60% of proposed entries approved | 30d | rejected | v1 |
| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | Resulting KB entries cited in a future bid | 90d | rejected | v1 |
| `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe` | New entry approved OR correct dedupe | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_staleness_classifier` | Flagged entry re-verified or archived | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `seller_page_enrichment` | Seller publishes generated content | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `capability_declaration_suggest` | Declaration published | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `match_score_numeric` | EOI submitted after viewing score | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `bid_task_assignment_suggest` | Task assigned as suggested | 24h | rejected | v1 |
| `document_attach_suggest` | Document attached to response | 24h | rejected | v1 |

**Default-on-timeout behavior.** Per §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #5, every contract's default-on-timeout is `rejected` unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`. This biases Sourcera toward cost protection when the signal is ambiguous (BPS §6 / SPS §10).

**`auto_accepted` distinct settlement state.** When the auto-accept timer fires (`auto_accept_after_seconds` reached without a rejected signal), the operation transitions to `auto_accepted` (NOT `accepted`). The `auto_accepted` state is billed at the value price (treated as accepted commercially) but is reported separately in product-quality dashboards to surface capabilities that may be over-relying on auto-accept.

### 34.11.2 Contest Window

Per MS C.78 and §4.8.5 ContestRecord, a `billing_admin` may contest any settled `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation within **14 days** of settlement (default; per-capability override via OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days` ≤ 90).

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Filing path | Billing Ledger UI → "Contest" button per AIOperation row → reason code + narrative; OR API `POST /v1/billing/operations/:id/contest` (endpoint pending per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Endpoint Additions`) |
| Filing window | 14d default from `settlement_at`; per-capability override |
| Routing | Contests route to Ops Finance via `contest_review` queue |
| Approved contest | AIOperation transitions to `reversed`; `effective_charge_cents = 0`; reversal credit posted to Wallet (committed pool if applicable, else included budget if same period, else overage_balance); `sourcera_ai_value_reversed` Stripe meter event emitted |
| Rejected contest | AIOperation returns to prior `accepted` / `auto_accepted` state; original charge restored; `settlement_at` unchanged |
| Auto-filed contest | When a late `rejected` signal arrives within `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` after auto-accept, an automatic ContestRecord is filed with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` (§4.8.5); routes to Ops Finance for review |
| Customer notifications | `contest.filed` (filing confirmation), `contest.in_review`, `contest.approved`, `contest.rejected`, `contest.escalated`, `contest.sla_breach` (pending per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`) |
| Ops Finance SLA | 5 business days for contest decision; SLA breach triggers `contest.sla_breach` and Ops alert |
| Locked-state guard | DSAR redaction during open contest is blocked with HTTP 423 `ai_operation_locked_for_contest`; resumes after contest closes (§4.8.5) |

### 34.11.3 Cost-Base Recalculation (Operational Cross-Reference)

The cost-base recalculation policy is fully specified in §34.3.3 above. Entity mechanics live in §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog. Key invariants:

- Nightly run at 02:30 UTC; idempotent re-run on missed sweep
- Drift severity bands: `low` (≥ 5%), `medium` (≥ 10%, alerts Finance), `high` (≥ 25%, blocks auto-publish), `critical` (margin-floor breach)
- High and critical drift require Ops Finance approval before publishing a new PricingTableVersion
- Approved publishes that constitute a customer-visible price increase MUST satisfy the 30-day-advance notification gate (§4.8.9 acceptance criterion #3); annual contracts grandfathered

### 34.11.4 Outcome Resolver Acceptance Criteria

1. Every AIOperation MUST receive a settlement decision within `auto_accept_after_seconds + signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` of `created_at` (§4.8.4).
2. Late `rejected` signals after auto-accept MUST automatically materialize a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #11; §4.8.5).
3. Resolver MUST use the OutcomeContract version that was active at the AIOperation `created_at`, not the currently active version (§4.8.4 acceptance criterion #2).
4. Contest SLA: Ops Finance MUST decide every contest within 5 business days; breach triggers `contest.sla_breach` webhook + Ops alert.
5. Approved contests MUST credit the wallet within 1 business day of approval; QA test `contest_approval_wallet_credit_latency` asserts.

## 34.12 Cross-Side Billing Rules {#34.12-cross-side-billing-rules}

§34.12 codifies the cross-console billing rules per BPS §13 / SPS §11 / MS §2. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is preserved end-to-end: billing data is shared at the Org level; business data (Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, evaluations, etc.) is not.

### 34.12.1 Per-Console Plan Activation

An Organization may hold any combination of Buyer plan and Seller plan. Plans activate per console, not per Org. Valid combinations include but are not limited to:

| Buyer plan | Seller plan | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free | Seller Free | Default for new Orgs that signed up via direct or invite path on either side |
| Business Growth | Seller Starter | Common cross-side activation pattern |
| Business Free | Seller Scale | Org primarily acts as a vendor; minimal buyer-side use |
| Buyer Enterprise | Seller Free | Org primarily acts as a buyer; vendor side is for occasional response |
| Buyer Enterprise | Seller Enterprise | Collapses to one combined contract per §34.12.5 |

Plan tier on each side is independent and may be upgraded or downgraded without affecting the other side, with the Enterprise-collapse exception in §34.12.5.

### 34.12.2 AI Wallet is Org-Scoped and Pooled

Per §34.10.3 (authoritative), AIWallet is a single row per Org. The pooled budget rule applies to all combinations:

```
total_usable_value_dollars =
  (committed_remaining if Enterprise active)
+ included_budget_remaining (collapsed per §34.10.3 Free+X rules)
+ overage_balance
+ free_allowance_remaining (per capability, evaluated independently)
```

Any customer-billed capability in either console can draw from the pool. The Outcome Resolver writes operations against the appropriate counter per the §34.10.1 burn priority.

### 34.12.3 Wallet Overage is Org-Scoped

One AIWallet → one overage cap → one auto-topup configuration → one `billing_admin` role per Org. Overage configuration cannot be split per console; the `billing_admin` operates at the Org level and may be granted to users with primary affiliation on either console.

### 34.12.4 Dual-Console Firewall is Unchanged

Billing data is shared across consoles within an Org for `billing_admin`-role reads only. **Console-scoped business entities never cross the firewall** regardless of billing state:

- Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, evaluations, KB entries, Capability Declarations, Vendor Profiles, Internal Comments, Q&A threads, Selection Reports, Scoring data — all console-isolated per §7.2.
- AIOperation rows are Org-scoped but **console-tagged** (`console` enum field; §4.8.1). A Buyer-console session cannot enumerate the AIOperations of a Seller-console workspace even though both bill against the same AIWallet (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #2).
- The Billing Ledger view (`GET /v1/billing/operations` — endpoint pending) returns rows scoped to the requesting session's console UNLESS the requesting role is `billing_admin`, in which case both consoles' AIOperations are returned with explicit `console` tags.
- ContestRecord (§4.8.5) is filable by `billing_admin` from either console session for any AIOperation in either console.
- DowngradeExcessDataBucket (§4.8.10) is created independently per console downgrade; an Org with both plans downgrading independently has independent buckets per `(org_id, console, data_class)`.

### 34.12.5 Enterprise Collapse to One Contract

When both consoles are on Enterprise, the Org signs one combined contract:

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subscription floor | Single floor at the higher of the two ($3,000/month per BPS §6 / SPS §8 — both floors are $3K/mo, so the combined floor is $3K/mo) |
| CommittedSpendContract | One contract covering both consoles (`linked_wallet_id` references the unified Wallet); `commit_value_dollars ≥ $12,000/yr` |
| Discount band | Derived from the combined commit per `committed_spend_discount_band` (Appendix J); no separate band per console |
| Dedicated CSM | One CSM works both sides of the Org; QBR cadence is unified |
| Custom integration scope | Defined per contract; covers both consoles' integration needs |
| SLA | 99.9% uptime + 4-hour critical response — applies platform-wide; not differentiated per console |
| DPA | One Data Processing Agreement covering both consoles |
| Audit log retention | 7 years for both consoles |

### 34.12.6 Billing Admin Role

The `billing_admin` org-level role (new in v7.0.0; logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Breaking Changes`) is the only role permitted to:

- Change wallet config (overage, caps, auto-topup) on either console
- Enable / disable wallet overage
- Initiate manual top-ups
- Change plan tier on either side (subject to Sales-Ops sign-off for Enterprise)
- Accept or reject a Vendor Pro Trial Seat grant (vendor side)
- File a ContestRecord (§4.8.5)
- View the cross-console Billing Ledger
- Approve a CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal opt-out

The role is granted by `org_owner` and `org_admin`; it is not granted by default. Audit log entries record every billing-state mutation with user attribution; entry kinds include `org.wallet_overage_enabled`, `org.wallet_cap_changed`, `org.wallet_topup_initiated`, `org.plan_changed`, `org.pro_trial_seat_accepted`, `org.contest_filed`. The role is registered in Appendix J → `Billing Admin Role (new) (§4.8.3, §4.8.5, §4.8.11)`.

### 34.12.7 Cross-Side Billing Failure Modes

1. **Both consoles concurrently downgrade to Free.** Resolved: at billing rollover, the unified pool collapses to $5 (§34.10.3 Free+Free rule); both consoles' DowngradeExcessDataBuckets are created independently per §34.6.
2. **An Org changes residency mid-period with active commit on Enterprise.** Resolved: §4.8.3 Failure Mode #6 — residency change requires Ops Finance migration runbook; in-period change does not retroactively reissue invoices.
3. **`billing_admin` is deprovisioned with active wallet config in flight.** Resolved: deprovisioning preserves the role assignment audit; another `billing_admin` (or `org_owner`) can take over; in-flight Stripe charges complete.
4. **Buyer-side and Seller-side downgrades on the same day produce overlapping notice cascades.** Resolved: each console's notification stream is independent (`downgrade_bucket.notice_d60` per bucket; deduplication via bucket ID); recipients see both notices.

## 34.13 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17) {#34.13-buyer-funded-pro-trial-seat}

§34.13 documents the Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat mechanic in full per SPS §15.5 and MS §3.3 M17. Entity-level mechanics live in §4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant (Phase 1).

### 34.13.1 Purpose

When a buyer on Business Scale or Buyer Enterprise invites a vendor, the invite may optionally grant the vendor a 30-day Seller Starter trial. The cost of the subscription tier is absorbed into the buyer's plan (no cash transfer; Stripe metered as `sourcera_pro_trial_grant`). AI usage during the trial is metered to the **vendor's** Org AIWallet, not the buyer's. The mechanic lifts seller-side conversion rate at the highest-converting PLG moment (the forced vendor signup) while improving response quality on the buyer's highest-stakes evaluations.

### 34.13.2 Allocation

| Buyer Plan | Pro Trial Seats per month | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free / Business Starter / Business Growth | 0 | BPS §3 |
| Business Scale | **5** | BPS §3, §3 footer |
| Buyer Enterprise | **15** | BPS §3, §3 footer |

Allocation rules:

- Unused seats **do not carry over** month to month; allocation replenishes on the buyer's billing anniversary.
- Buyer plan downgrades zero out the current period's unused seats at the downgrade boundary; new monthly allowance at the new tier applies from the next cycle.
- Buyer plan upgrades from below Scale to Scale or Enterprise immediately credit the new tier's monthly allowance for the in-flight period (no proration).
- An Ops-Console Pricing Admin may temporarily increase a buyer's allowance for a defined window (e.g., a specific evaluation cohort) per `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_overridden` audit event; overrides are time-boxed and reverse automatically at expiry.

### 34.13.3 Grant Mechanics

| Step | Action | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | A Buyer Workspace Owner OR Org Admin (per §5.3) clicks "Invite with Pro Trial" on a vendor invitation flow | UI surface in §14 (vendor curation; UI authoring pending per Phase 1 Known Gap K-V12 / Phase 4 Known Gaps) |
| 2 | The buyer's allocation decrements by 1; if allocation = 0, the option is disabled in the UI with explanatory copy ("0 of 5 Pro Trial Seats remaining this month") | `org.pro_trial_seat_allocated` audit event on buyer Org |
| 3 | The vendor receives the magic-link invitation email with a "Your invite includes 30 days of Seller Starter, free" callout | `pro_trial_seat.invite` email (Loops.so template; pending Phase 1 known gap closure) |
| 4 | On magic-link click, the vendor's Org is provisioned (or upgraded if existing Free) with Seller Starter entitlements: `seller_plan_tier = seller_starter`, `trial_source_buyer_org_id = <buyer>`, `trial_expires_at = now + 30d`, `trial_grant_id = <Pro Trial Seat Grant entity ID>` | `pro_trial_seat.granted` audit event on both Orgs (buyer + vendor) |
| 5 | Seller Starter AI budget ($30 value-dollars) is credited to the vendor's AIWallet `included_budget_remaining` for the trial period (§4.8.3) | n/a |
| 6 | All Seller Starter features unlock immediately: KB capacity to 1,000 entries, Firecrawl 2 sources weekly, EOI quota 10/month, Verified-tier eligibility, Page Enrichment 1/year, Monthly Seller Signals digest, etc. | n/a |
| 7 | Day-27 reminder fires to vendor Billing Admin: "Your trial ends in 3 days. Convert to keep your KB and in-flight bids active." | `pro_trial_seat.day_27_reminder` email |
| 8 | Day-31 transition: convert / auto-downgrade / declined per §34.13.4 | Per §34.13.4 |

### 34.13.4 Trial Completion (Day 31)

| Outcome | Behavior | Stripe / Audit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Convert** | Vendor adds payment method and confirms Seller Starter (or higher); plan persists; included budget resets on new billing cycle; no data loss | `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.converted` audit + email; M17 conversion rate dashboard updated |
| **Auto-downgrade** | Vendor takes no action by day 31 23:59 UTC; plan downgrades to `seller_free`; entities exceeding Free caps (KB > 50, Capability Declarations > 3, etc.) enter §34.6 90-day read-only preservation | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` audit + email |
| **Explicit decline** | Vendor explicitly declines via in-app banner during trial OR rejects grant on receipt; same behavior as auto-downgrade; trial may be declined immediately or any time before day 31 | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.declined` audit + email |

Carry-over invariants: KB entries, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs persist through any outcome. Auto-downgrade triggers §34.6 preservation (not deletion).

### 34.13.5 Restrictions

| Restriction | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| **One trial per buyer-vendor pair per 365 days** | A vendor Org cannot receive a second Pro Trial Seat grant from the same buyer Org within 365 days of the prior grant; attempt returns `trial_seat_same_buyer_365d_block` (Appendix I — pending) |
| **Vendor already on a paid Seller plan** | Cannot receive a Pro Trial Seat (no downgrade or double-funding); attempt returns `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid` |
| **Buyer below Scale** | Cannot issue Pro Trial Seat (no allocation); attempt returns `trial_seat_buyer_below_scale` |
| **Buyer's allocation pool exhausted** | Returns `trial_seat_pool_exhausted` (cap binds at 5/mo or 15/mo per §34.13.2) |
| **Vendor Billing Admin may reject the grant** | Rejection is audited as `pro_trial_seat.declined`; the buyer's allocation is **NOT refunded** (anti-abuse: prevents buyer from probing vendors) |
| **Anti-spam framework applies** | Ops Console may restrict a buyer's Pro Trial Seat usage on abuse signal per §3.5 Anti-Spam (MS §3.5); restrictions logged in Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100); Ops can zero allocation, time-box restrict, or revoke prior unredeemed grants |
| **Invited vendor must clear the same anti-spam framework as a normal invite** | Invite-eligibility gates apply: domain verification, opt-out registry check, suppression list check |
| **Trial cannot be re-extended** | A trial in progress cannot be extended beyond 30 days; vendor must convert to Starter+ or accept auto-downgrade |

### 34.13.6 Metering and Reporting

| Surface | What is reported |
| :---- | :---- |
| Stripe meter events | `sourcera_pro_trial_grant` at grant time; `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` at day-30/31 conversion; `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` at auto-downgrade |
| Internal conversion-rate dashboard | Pro Trial grants issued, conversions by day 31, AI budget utilization during trial, comparison vs. cold-start Free → Starter conversion rate, by buyer cohort |
| Buyer-side reporting | Per-buyer view: "X of Y Pro Trial Seats issued this period; Z converted to paid"; surfaces ROI of the M17 mechanic on the buyer's plan value proposition |
| Vendor-side reporting | Vendor sees the grant origin in their Wallet UI: "Granted by [Buyer Org] until [date]"; transparency builds trust |
| Ops Console | Signal Integrity Monitor surfaces buyers with abnormal grant-to-conversion ratios (low conversion = potential spam pattern); per-vendor view of grant history across buyers |

### 34.13.7 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Vendor's wallet is in `payment_failed_grace` when trial expires.** Resolved: auto-downgrade still fires at day 31; the grace state is for the prior subscription only and does not extend the trial.
2. **Buyer downgrades from Scale to Growth between grant and vendor magic-link click.** Resolved: the grant is honored (the allocation was decremented at click time and the pool is irrelevant after issuance).
3. **Vendor receives multiple concurrent Pro Trial Seat grants from different buyers in the same week.** Resolved: only the first redeemed grant takes effect; subsequent grants are queued and the vendor receives a notification with a 7-day acceptance window per queued grant; if not accepted in 7 days, queued grant expires and the buyer's allocation is refunded for that specific grant.
4. **Trial AI usage exhausts the vendor's $30 budget mid-trial.** Resolved: vendor wallet behaves as a normal Seller Starter wallet — overage is off by default; vendor may enable overage to continue; trial does not extend or refund on exhaustion.
5. **Buyer Org is deleted between grant and vendor redemption.** Resolved: grant remains valid (one-way audit trail); vendor magic link works; vendor sees "[Buyer Org] (deleted)" in the grant attribution UI.

### 34.13.8 Pro Trial Seat Acceptance Criteria

1. Pro Trial Seat allocation MUST be enforced at Wallet/UI time of issuance; over-issuance returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`.
2. Day-31 transition MUST execute exactly once per active trial (idempotent); QA test `pro_trial_day_31_idempotent` asserts.
3. Audit trail MUST capture grant issuance, redemption, conversion, and decline events with both buyer and vendor Org attribution.
4. Auto-downgrade on day 31 MUST trigger §34.6 preservation for any over-cap entities; QA test `pro_trial_auto_downgrade_preservation` asserts.
5. Anti-spam framework MUST be evaluated at grant time and at vendor redemption time; suppressions take precedence.
6. AI usage during trial MUST meter against the vendor's Wallet, not the buyer's; QA test `pro_trial_wallet_attribution` asserts.
7. The 365-day same-buyer-vendor rate-limit MUST be enforced atomically; concurrent grant attempts deduplicate via partial unique index on `(buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, granted_at_year)` — partial because expired/declined grants must not block re-grant.
8. The buyer's allocation MUST decrement at click time, not at vendor redemption — vendor non-redemption does NOT refund the allocation (anti-probing rule).

## 34.14 Acceptance Criteria {#34.14-acceptance-criteria}

The criteria below are §34-scope (plan / pricing / wallet / entitlement / outcome / cross-side / Pro Trial Seat policy). Entity-level acceptance criteria for AIOperation, CapabilityRegistryEntry, AIWallet, OutcomeContract, ContestRecord, CostBaseRecalculationLog, FreeAllowanceCounter, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, and BillingSeatSnapshot live at §4.8.1–§4.8.11 and are NOT restated here.

### 34.14.1 Plan-Tier Definitions and Pricing

1. The §34.1 plan-tier tables MUST be the single source of truth for plan capabilities; §5.11 Feature Access Matrix and §39 Object Size Constraints reference §34.1 cells with `Source: §34.1.x` annotations and never restate values.
2. Every cell in §34.1.1 and §34.1.2 MUST have a `Source` citation back to BPS, SPS, MS, or AE; deploy-time validator asserts no orphan cells.
3. Plan-tier prices in §34.2 MUST match `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_json.plan_tiers` (§4.8.9) at all times; nightly reconciliation job asserts; mismatch triggers `pricing_table_drift_alert` to Ops Finance.
4. The Public Pricing API (`api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing`) MUST publish the latest `PricingTableVersion` with `status=published` and `effective_at ≤ now` (§4.8.9 acceptance criterion #1).
5. Annual contract customers MUST be grandfathered through any breaking-change publish for the remainder of their contract term (§4.8.9; BPS §11; SPS §11).

### 34.14.2 Outcome-Based Pricing

6. The pricing formula `value_price = MAX(min_value, cost_base × 10)` and `cost_price = MAX(min_cost, cost_base × 1.05)` MUST be applied uniformly across all customer-billed capabilities; deploy-time validator asserts.
7. The 88% blended-margin floor MUST be enforced at price-update time; cost-base recalcs that would breach the floor are blocked until Ops Finance approves (§34.3.3; §4.8.6).
8. Cost-base recalculations MUST run nightly at 02:30 UTC; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour.

### 34.14.3 Wallet and Entitlements

9. Entitlement check MUST be O(1) on the cached session metadata; database round trips for plan-tier or wallet-state lookup during entitlement evaluation are forbidden (§34.8.2).
10. AIWallet MUST be Org-scoped, console-pooled, and never partition pooling by console — except for the §34.10.3 Free+Free and Free+Paid collapse rules (Authored Extensions; Sales-Ops sign-off pending).
11. Wallet overage MUST default to OFF on every plan; admin opt-in is mandatory and audited (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #4).
12. Auto-topup MUST default to OFF; admin opt-in is mandatory; auto-topup increment is constrained to $50–$10,000 per charge (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #5).
13. Wallet 50% / 80% / 100% notifications MUST be one-shot per period (idempotency stamps prevent duplicates; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #6).
14. Free Allowance MUST be exhausted before any wallet draw for `customer_billed` capabilities (§4.8.7 acceptance criterion #2).
15. Soft-gated capabilities MUST surface upgrade CTAs in the result envelope; hard-gated capabilities MUST return HTTP 403 with the upgrade path in the error body (§34.8.1, §34.8.7).
16. Every customer-billed capability with `state=active` in CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST have a row in the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix; deploy-time validator asserts.

### 34.14.4 Outcome Resolver and Contests

17. Default-on-timeout MUST be `rejected` for every OutcomeContract unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true` (§4.8.4 acceptance criterion #5).
18. `auto_accepted` MUST be a distinct settlement state, billed at value price but reported separately for product-quality dashboards.
19. Customers MUST be able to file ContestRecords within 14 days (or per-capability override) of settlement; auto-filing on late `rejected` signals MUST notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes (§4.8.5).
20. Ops Finance contest decisions MUST occur within 5 business days; SLA breach triggers `contest.sla_breach` webhook + Ops alert.
21. Approved contests MUST credit the wallet within 1 business day of approval.

### 34.14.5 Plan Upgrade / Downgrade and Preservation

22. Upgrades MUST be effective immediately (Stripe webhook receipt → entitlement refresh ≤ 30 seconds); proration applied per §34.5.1.
23. Downgrades MUST surface a 14-day warning when current usage exceeds new caps; warning enumerates specific overages with action options per §34.5.3.
24. DowngradeExcessDataBucket creation MUST occur within 5 minutes of effective downgrade (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #1).
25. Preserved entities MUST remain readable but not mutable for 90 days; restoration on upgrade is atomic per §34.6.2; partial restoration requires explicit user confirmation (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #4).
26. Cold-storage hard-archive MUST occur within 1 hour of `preservation_until`; cold-storage retention is 7 years; restoration window is 90 days post-archive (§34.6.3; §4.8.10 acceptance criterion #5).

### 34.14.6 Seat Counting (Informational Only)

27. Sourcera MUST NOT charge per seat on any plan; the Public Pricing API MUST NOT expose per-seat pricing (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #6).
28. `BillingSeatSnapshot.plan_gate_breach_flag` MUST be informational only — no invoicing or feature-access gate on seat count (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #4).
29. Guests and API-only identities MUST be excluded from `active_seats_count` (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #3).
30. Monthly snapshots MUST run at 02:00 UTC on the 1st of each month for every active Org (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #1).

### 34.14.7 Cross-Side Billing

31. AIWallet MUST be Org-scoped (one row per Org); the Dual-Console Firewall MUST NOT partition the wallet (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #1).
32. Console-scoped business entities (Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, Capability Declarations, etc.) MUST NOT cross the firewall regardless of billing state (§7.2; §34.12.4).
33. The `billing_admin` role MUST be the only role permitted to mutate wallet config, file contests, change plan tier, or accept Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side; mutations are audit-logged with user attribution.
34. Enterprise + Enterprise Org MUST collapse into one combined contract with one committed spend minimum at the higher floor ($3K/mo) and one dedicated CSM (§34.12.5).

### 34.14.8 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17)

35. Pro Trial Seat allocation (5/mo Scale; 15/mo Enterprise) MUST be enforced at issuance time; over-issuance returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`.
36. Day-31 transition (convert / auto-downgrade / decline) MUST execute exactly once per active trial and trigger §34.6 preservation for over-cap entities on auto-downgrade.
37. AI usage during trial MUST meter against the vendor's Wallet, not the buyer's (§34.13.6).
38. The 365-day same-buyer-vendor rate-limit MUST be enforced atomically.
39. Vendor non-redemption MUST NOT refund the buyer's allocation (anti-probing rule §34.13.5).
40. Anti-spam framework (§3.5) MUST gate Pro Trial Seat issuance and redemption.

### 34.14.9 Webhooks, Events, and API Surfaces

41. Webhook events for §34 (wallet thresholds, contest lifecycle, cost-base recalc, committed-spend lifecycle, pricing-table publish, downgrade-bucket lifecycle, seat-snapshot triggers, Pro Trial Seat lifecycle) MUST be added to Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`. Each event MUST follow §31 patterns: HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB.
42. API endpoints for §34 (Billing Ledger, Public Pricing API, Wallet read/configure, Contest file/list, Capability Registry public read, CommittedSpend admin, DowngradeExcessDataBucket read + Ops restore, BillingSeatSnapshot list) MUST follow §32 patterns: authentication, rate-limit headers, cursor pagination (default 50, max 250), error codes from Appendix I per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Endpoint Additions`.
43. Every error code referenced in §34 MUST be added to Appendix I per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 4 Known Gaps` (catalog extension still pending).

### 34.14.10 Glossary and Enum Discipline

44. Every multi-section term introduced or used in §34 MUST have a glossary entry under "Terms Introduced in §34 (v7.0.0 Pricing Rewrite)" in Appendix K (Glossary) — to be added per the Pricing Rewrite Track Phase reconciliation.
45. Every enum value referenced in §34 MUST be registered in Appendix J under a section ending in `(§4.8.x)` or `(§34.x)`; deploy-time validator asserts no inline-undefined enums.
46. The §34.1 `Plan Tiers` enum split (`buyer_*` and `seller_*` per console) MUST be reflected in Appendix J → `Plan Tiers` and is logged as a Breaking Change.

# 35\. User Onboarding Experience {#35.-user-onboarding-experience}

## 35.1 Buyer Onboarding Flow {#35.1-buyer-onboarding-flow}

### Step 1: Sign Up

Email \+ password (or SSO for Enterprise). Auto-creates Organization and first Workspace.

### Step 2: Organization Setup

Organization name, logo (optional). Plan selection (Free or start Business trial).

### Step 3: Team Setup

Invite team members by email (bulk paste or single). Assign workspace roles: Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead, Reviewer. Skip option available.

### Step 4: First Use Case

Prompt: "What are you evaluating?" Pre-configured options: "Custom SaaS Evaluation", "Security-First Evaluation", "Compliance Evaluation" (links to Template Gallery). Or "Start from scratch."

### Step 5: First Requirement

"Create your first requirement" with guided field completion (title, description, response type, weight). Inline help for each field. Or "Import from policy document" (links to Policy Ingestion).

### Step 6: Optional — TCO Setup

If applicable: "Do you want to compare vendor costs?" Links to TCO Use Case creation.

### Step 7: Dashboard Tour

Highlight tour: Sidebar navigation, Command Palette (`Cmd+K`), Keyboard shortcuts, Pulse dashboard. Tour is dismissible and can be replayed from Settings → Help.

## 35.2 Seller Onboarding Flow {#35.2-seller-onboarding-flow}

The Seller Onboarding Flow exploits the single highest-converting moment in Sourcera's GTM: the forced vendor signup triggered by an incoming buyer invite. The vendor arrives at peak pain (incoming RFP, deadline, blank response, no chosen tool) with an immediate business reason to engage. The onboarding is engineered to collapse the new-vendor cold-start wall from ~2 days (status quo: manual triage, KB hunt, draft from scratch) to under 60 minutes end-to-end.

Narrative context and conversion rationale live in `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md §14–§17`. This section is the implementation spec.

### 35.2.1 Seven-Stage Flow

| Stage | Duration | State | Product Surface |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Magic-link arrival | 0–30s | Buyer invite email, magic-link |
| 2 | Signup + synchronous bootstrap | 30s–3m | Progress storytelling screen |
| 3 | Ready-workspace landing | 3–5m | Bid Workspace with drafts staged |
| 4 | Review and submit | 5–60m | Inline drafts + KB-gap detector |
| 5 | Post-submit stake reveal | Day 0 | Stake-reveal screen |
| 6 | Outcome debrief | Day 3–30 | Win/loss debrief surface |
| 7 | Upgrade touch | Day 1–90 | Contextual upgrade CTAs |

### 35.2.2 Step 1 — Magic-Link Arrival

Vendor receives email: *"You've been invited to participate in '{Workspace Name}' evaluation."* Magic-link opens Sourcera. No credit card prompt. No company profile form gate. Domain + invite identity is sufficient.

**Pre-arrival preparation (hidden from vendor):**
- Domain enrichment against public records (company name, industry, HQ region)
- Marketplace Tagger assigns probable category tags based on domain + buyer-side evaluation context
- Bootstrap queue is pre-warmed; crawl URLs resolved and rate-limited against Firecrawl

The bootstrap starts within the SSO redirect latency window — before the vendor sees a workspace.

### 35.2.3 Step 2 — Signup + Synchronous Bootstrap

Three operations run in parallel while the vendor watches a progress storytelling screen:

1. **Domain Bootstrap** (Capability S1, Opus, lifetime-free on Free). Crawls homepage, help center, docs, trust center. 30–90 seconds.
2. **KB Propose.** 40–200 draft KB entries staged with confidence scores and provenance URLs.
3. **First-Pass Draft** (Capability S2, Sonnet). Drafts responses for every requirement in the buyer's evaluation, citing newly bootstrapped KB entries.

**Progress storytelling screen.** Narrates true status lines:
- *"Scanning yourcompany.com..."* (0–15s)
- *"Found your security documentation..."* (15–30s)
- *"Drafting responses for {Buyer Company}'s 82 requirements..."* (30–90s)
- *"Your bid is ready to review."*

Status lines must reflect real operations — never fabricate steps.

**Account linking (for existing users):** If invitee already has a Sourcera account in a different Organization, present choice:
- *"Join the new organization with your existing account"* → Account linked to new org. Console switcher in sidebar shows all memberships.
- *"Create a new account with different email"* → Separate account created.

**Published Seller Profile** is auto-created on first signup (Basic verification tier, domain-verified). Profile appears in the public Marketplace immediately — no publication gate.

### 35.2.4 Step 3 — Ready-Workspace Landing

Vendor lands on the Bid Workspace with this headline:

> *Your bid for {Buyer Company} is ready. **47** of **82** requirements have AI drafts. **31** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~35 min**.*

Three clear next steps surfaced inline (not in a modal):
- Review drafts
- Add or edit KB
- Invite teammates

No pricing page. No demo walkthrough. No "try Pro free for 14 days" modal. The hero moment is the pitch.

### 35.2.5 Step 4 — Review and Submit

**Inline citations.** Every First-Pass draft shows its KB citation in the response row: *"from: yourcompany.com/trust/soc2"* with hover expansion to the exact quoted sentence.

**Accept / Edit / Reject per requirement.** Three buttons. Every click is an outcome signal written to the Outcome Resolver (§34.11) for Capability S2.

**Live budget counter.** Top of workspace shows *"AI budget used: $X.XX of $5.00 · N drafts accepted, M rejected."* — visible to the user, sized so a complete first bid end-to-end fits within the $5 Free budget.

**KB-gap detector.** Rejected-response empty state is not a dead end:
> *"No KB content answered this. Write your answer below and we'll save it as a KB entry."*
> `[inline text field with 1-click save]`

One-click creates a KB entry from the vendor's inline answer. Every rejection grows the KB.

**"AI got this right" confirmation.** Accepting a draft with no edits records the strongest acceptance signal and surfaces a confirmation chip (*"added to your KB as verified response"*).

**NDA Review.** If the evaluation requires an NDA (Marketplace §27, NDA Record §4.5.3), the NDA module is surfaced as a blocking step before final submission. NDA review does not delay the hero moment — drafts are still prepared and reviewable during NDA negotiation.

### 35.2.6 Step 5 — Post-Submit Stake Reveal

On submission, the closing screen reads:

> *You just built a reusable KB of **N** verified entries in **Y** minutes.*
> *Your next bid will reuse them automatically.*
> *Sourcera tracked **$X.XX** of value pricing for the AI work on this bid (covered by your Free plan).*

This is a **stake-reveal screen**, not an upgrade CTA. It reminds the vendor what they have built, what it is worth, and how it compounds. Upgrade conversations come later at natural ceilings (Step 7).

### 35.2.7 Step 6 — Outcome Debrief

Triggered by buyer-side bid close event. Agent generates a debrief surface for the vendor:

**Win debrief:**
> *You won. **N** KB entries cited on winning responses. Those entries are now higher-weighted in your KB — Sourcera learned what answers close deals for you. Keep your KB alive — upgrade to Starter to unlock weekly crawls of your site and auto-staleness checks.*

**Loss debrief (with buyer's published reasoning where available):**
> *You lost this one. Gap analysis identified **N** requirements where your KB had no strong answer. Those gaps are flagged in your KB. Upgrade to Starter to let Sourcera crawl your product docs weekly and fill gaps automatically.*

### 35.2.8 Step 7 — Upgrade Touch

Three planned conversion moments, each with a distinct buying reason:

| # | Trigger | Buying reason | CTA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Second concurrent invited bid | Urgency — "my deal is at risk" | *"Starter unlocks 3 concurrent bids and shares your KB across all of them."* |
| 2 | First proactive EOI attempt | Ambition — "I want to find more deals" | *"Outbound EOIs start at Starter. Your first 10/month are included."* |
| 3 | KB approaches 50-entry cap | Investment — "don't lose what I've built" | *"Your KB is about to hit the Free ceiling. Starter raises it to 1,000 entries."* |

Every upgrade CTA must carry over KB, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, and Firecrawl configs without re-setup (§34.5). CTAs state the carry-over explicitly.

### 35.2.9 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Acceptance

If the invite was issued with a Pro Trial Seat (§34.13), Step 2 provisions Seller Starter entitlements instead of Seller Free. The Billing Admin role on the vendor's Org receives a notification and may reject the grant; rejection is audited. On day 31, the vendor is prompted to convert, explicitly decline, or auto-downgrade to Seller Free (all data preserved per §34.6).

### 35.2.10 Activation Metric

**"Minutes from magic-link click to first submitted requirement response"** — target p50 < 20 minutes, p90 < 60 minutes. This is a top-level product metric and must be surfaced in the founder dashboard and Ops Console.

### 35.2.11 Onboarding Anti-Patterns (Explicitly Banned)

The onboarding surface must not:
- Ask for a credit card at any point before the first upgrade intent click
- Require the vendor to describe their company or industry before bootstrap runs
- Gate any feature behind a "try Pro free for 14 days" modal on first login
- Show a pricing page until the vendor has submitted their first bid
- Use dark patterns on upgrade CTAs (roach motels, hard-to-find downgrade, fake urgency)
- Present upgrade offers during active bid work — only at natural completion points or ceiling events

These bans exist because the supply-side flywheel depends on vendor trust. Any onboarding friction that reads as sales-ey kills that trust.

### 35.2.12 Required Platform Capabilities

Shipped as dependencies for the Seller Onboarding Flow to go live:

1. Magic-link SSO orchestrator that starts bootstrap inside the SSO redirect latency
2. Progress storytelling UI that renders bootstrap and first-pass status honestly
3. Inline-citation UI on every First-Pass draft response row
4. Budget counter persistent at top of Bid Workspace on Free and Starter
5. KB-gap detector in rejected-response empty states with 1-click KB-entry creation
6. Stake-reveal screen on first bid submission
7. Outcome debrief surface triggered by buyer-side bid close
8. Contextual upgrade CTAs that carry over KB, bids, and in-flight state
9. Pro Trial Seat plumbing (pool allocation, 30-day trial state, auto-downgrade on day 31)
10. Free-ceiling-approaching notifications (40/48 KB entries, 80% budget utilization, first EOI attempt)

## 35.3 Skipped Steps Recoverability {#35.3-skipped-steps-recoverability}

A persistent "Setup Checklist" widget appears in the sidebar during onboarding. Steps completed are checked off. Uncompleted steps remain visible.

**Behavior:**

- Checklist remains until all steps completed or explicitly dismissed  
- Dismissed checklist can be re-opened from Settings → Onboarding → Resume Setup  
- Clicking a step in checklist navigates to that onboarding screen  
- Checklist can be dismissed per-step (click X on individual step) or entirely (Dismiss All)

**Dismissal State:**

- Individual step dismissals: per-step flag stored in onboarding state  
- Full dismissal: `setup_checklist_dismissed` flag set on org record, but steps remain recoverable via Settings

## 35.4 Acceptance Criteria {#35.4-acceptance-criteria}

- Buyer onboarding complete in < 10 minutes.
- **Seller onboarding — time from magic-link click to first submitted requirement response p50 < 20 minutes, p90 < 60 minutes.**
- Seller Profile published publicly in the Marketplace by end of Step 2 (signup + bootstrap).
- KB Bootstrap completes within 90 seconds on p90 for domains under 500 pages.
- First-Pass Draft Generator produces drafts for ≥40% of requirements on p50 for invited bids with ≥40 requirements.
- All tooltips dismissible with single click or `Escape`.
- Onboarding never shows a pricing page before first bid submission.
- Onboarding never prompts for credit card before first upgrade intent click.
- Multi-org users can join additional organizations without account conflict.
- Setup Checklist persists until completed or dismissed, and is recoverable from Settings.
- Pro Trial Seat grants provision Seller Starter entitlements at signup; auto-downgrade on day 31 preserves all data for 90 days per §34.6.
- Activation metric (magic-link → first submitted response) surfaced in founder dashboard and Ops Console in real time.

| **Deletion** | Delete workspace (requires Workspace Owner \+ Org Admin approval, 3-day confirmation window). Permanent purge after 30 days. | Workspace Owner \+ Org Admin |

## 36.4 Acceptance Criteria {#36.4-acceptance-criteria}

- Every user setting has clear labels, help text, and example values.  
- Organization settings permission matrix enforced on every mutation.  
- Workspace settings respect phase locks (e.g., cannot change Scoring Mode after Phase 10).  
- Data exports complete within 5 seconds for \<10K requirements.  
- Settings page load time \< 1s.  
- All settings changes logged to audit trail (Section 5.6).

# 37\. Accessibility & Internationalization {#37.-accessibility-&-internationalization}

## 37.1 Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) {#37.1-accessibility-(wcag-2.1-aa)}

- **Color Contrast:** ≥ 4.5:1 (normal text), ≥ 3:1 (large text). Color is not sole information conveyor.  
- **Keyboard Navigation:** All interactive elements reachable via keyboard. Focus indicators ≥ 3:1 contrast, ≥ 3px border. No keyboard traps.  
- **Screen Reader:** ARIA labels and roles on interactive elements. Landmark regions (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>`). Form labels associated via `<label for>`. Status messages announced via `aria-live`.  
- **Motor:** Touch targets ≥ 48x48px. Keyboard alternatives for drag-and-drop (e.g., "Use arrow keys to reorder").

## 37.2 Internationalization (i18n) {#37.2-internationalization-(i18n)}

**v6.0 is English-only at launch.** The codebase is i18n-ready:

- All UI strings externalized via `next-intl` library.  
- No hardcoded strings in components.  
- Locale-aware formatting is supported:  
  - Dates: Per browser locale (en-US: MM/DD/YYYY, en-GB: DD/MM/YYYY, etc.)  
  - Numbers: Thousands separator and decimal per locale.  
  - Currency: Configurable per Organization (default USD).  
  - Timezone: User-configurable (default browser timezone).

**Phase 2 Roadmap:** Spanish, French, German, Japanese UI translations. User-generated content (requirements, responses) remains in original language.

## 37.3 Right-to-Left (RTL) Support {#37.3-right-to-left-(rtl)-support}

**v6.0: Deferred to Phase 2\.**

**CSS Architecture Prepared:** All layouts use CSS Logical Properties (`inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start`, `block-end`) instead of directional properties (`left`, `right`). Flexbox and Grid with logical flow directions. This enables RTL retrofitting without component rewrites.

## 37.4 Testing {#37.4-testing}

- Automated accessibility audits (Axe DevTools) on every UI change (CI/CD gated).  
- Annual third-party WCAG 2.1 AA audit (external firm).  
- Screen reader testing (NVDA, JAWS) on critical workflows.

## 37.5 Acceptance Criteria {#37.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Zero Axe violations on all pages.  
- All interactive elements keyboard-accessible.  
- Focus indicators visible on every interactive element.  
- ARIA labels present on custom components.  
- Logical properties used throughout CSS (no hardcoded `left`/`right`).

---

# 38\. Responsive Design & Platform Support {#38.-responsive-design-&-platform-support}

## 38.1 Breakpoints {#38.1-breakpoints}

| Breakpoint | Width | Layout |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mobile | \< 640px | Single-column. Sidebar collapsed to hamburger menu. Bottom navigation bar. |
| Tablet | 640-1024px | Two-column (sidebar \+ main). Touch targets ≥ 48px. Top navigation. |
| Desktop | \> 1024px | Three-column (sidebar \+ main \+ detail pane). Keyboard shortcuts enabled. Sidebar pinned. |

## 38.2 Browser Support {#38.2-browser-support}

**Desktop:** Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest 2 versions each). Minimum 1024x768px. **Mobile:** iOS Safari, Chrome Android (latest 2 versions). Samsung Internet (latest). Minimum 375x667px. **Unsupported:** Internet Explorer (all versions).

## 38.3 JavaScript Requirement {#38.3-javascript-requirement}

Sourcera requires JavaScript. The platform is built on Convex (real-time reactive subscriptions) which requires the Convex SDK (JavaScript). There is no server-side rendering fallback for JavaScript-disabled browsers. If JavaScript is disabled, the app displays a static banner: "Sourcera requires JavaScript to function. Please enable JavaScript in your browser settings."

## 38.4 Mobile Feature Parity {#38.4-mobile-feature-parity}

Mobile experience is read \+ limited write. Full workflows (scoring, complex editing) require desktop.

**Mobile Read Access:**

- View requirements, responses, scores, comments  
- View workspace status and phase  
- View Pulse health metrics  
- View Intelligence briefings (read-only)

**Mobile Limited Write Access:**

- Comment on requirements (threaded comments)  
- Submit boolean responses (Seller Console)  
- View and acknowledge notifications

**Mobile Not Supported:**

- Collaborative scoring (requires Tablet+ due to multi-pane layout)  
- Policy Ingestion (file upload, complex extraction review)  
- TCO configuration (complex parameterization)  
- Scenario modeling (matrix-intensive)  
- Command Palette (replaced by Search Bar on mobile)  
- Full requirement editing (Markdown editor requires larger viewport)

**Mobile Search Bar:** On mobile, `Cmd+K` is not available. Instead, top navigation includes "Search" icon (magnifying glass) that opens mobile search. Searches: requirements, vendors, use cases, comments.

## 38.5 Acceptance Criteria {#38.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Mobile experience displays correctly on 375px width.  
- Touch targets ≥ 48px on mobile.  
- Read workflows fully functional on mobile.  
- Limited write workflows (comments, boolean responses) fully functional on mobile.  
- Mobile search bar responsive and discoverable.  
- Tablet layout properly reflows when rotated (landscape ↔ portrait).

# 40\. Data Export & Import {#40.-data-export-&-import}

## 40.1 Export Formats {#40.1-export-formats}

| Format | Contents | Availability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CSV** | Requirements, responses, scoring matrix, plan tier breakdown | All plans |
| **PDF** | Selection Report (executive summary \+ full scorecard) | All plans |
| **Excel** | Multi-sheet workbook (Requirements, Vendors, Scores, Comments, Traceability Matrix if applicable). Includes formulas for score aggregation | Business+ |
| **JSON** | Complete workspace snapshot (all entities, relationships, audit metadata) | Business+ (read-only API), Enterprise (full) |

### Additional Export Types

- **Traceability Matrix:** Standalone CSV/Excel of requirement ↔ framework control mappings (Policy Ingestion only).  
- **Scenario Export:** Scenario name, parameters, summary, and optional score snapshot. JSON or Excel.  
- **Intelligence Briefing:** JSON (raw) or PDF (formatted). Via Settings → Data & Privacy or API.  
- **Audit Export:** All audit events for a workspace (CSV/JSON). Enterprise only.

## 40.2 Data Retention & Deletion {#40.2-data-retention-&-deletion}

| Condition | Retention |
| :---- | :---- |
| Deleted workspace (soft delete) | 30 days, then permanent purge |
| User data (responses, comments, audit) | Life of workspace |
| Canceled subscription | 90 days, then purge |
| GDPR deletion request | 30 days to process (Section 33.4) |
| Deprovisioned user (SCIM) | Owned entities reassigned within 24 hours. User record retained but marked `deprovisioned`. |
| Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention | Life of parent entity (Workspace / Use Case / Requirement / Response / Scenario / Selection Report draft). On parent soft-delete, cascade soft-delete + 30-day purge. |
| Presence Record | Ephemeral (Convex session). Evicted 60s after last heartbeat or on explicit disconnect. Never written to cold storage. Not subject to DSAR export. Excluded from round-trip fidelity per §40.4. |
| Unread Marker | Purged 30 days after parent thread hard-delete **or** 30 days after user loses Workspace Membership, whichever fires first. Org-delete cascade per 90-day rule above. |
| Buyer Referral — identity fields (`referee_email`, `referrer_user_id`) | Pseudonymized on DSAR within 30 days. |
| Buyer Referral — financial fields (`credit_value_usd`, `credit_redeemed_usd`, `stripe_credit_note_ids`) | Retained unaltered for Org-life + 7 years per Sarbanes-Oxley-aligned financial record retention and Stripe audit requirements. Not subject to right-to-erasure under §45.1 financial-record exemption. |
| Pro Trial Seat Grant — identity fields (`vendor_email`, `issuer_user_id`) | Pseudonymized on DSAR within 30 days. |
| Pro Trial Seat Grant — financial and outcome fields | Retained for Org-life + 7 years per financial audit. |
| Usage Event — raw rows | 24-month rolling. After 24 months: anonymize (`user_id` pseudonymized, `ip_address_hash` purged, `properties_json` compacted to coarse counts), roll up into monthly aggregates. |
| Usage Event — monthly aggregates | Retained for Org-life. |
| Usage Event — DSAR | `user_id` and `properties_json` values referencing the subject redacted within 30 days per §6.8. `ai_value_dollars` retained in aggregate. |
| Time-Saved Credit — raw rows | 36-month rolling. After 36 months: purge raw rows; retain monthly aggregates. |
| Time-Saved Credit — monthly aggregates | Retained for Org-life. |
| Time-Saved Credit — DSAR | `user_id` redacted within 30 days; monetary aggregates retained. |
| Marketplace Category | Platform-life. `draft` soft-deleted rows purged after 30 days. `deprecated` rows retained indefinitely for FK integrity and URL redirect continuity. Not subject to DSAR (no PII). Residency: taxonomy is global. |
| Vendor Opt-Out Record | Org-life + 7 years per platform-integrity + legal-defensibility policy. Not subject to right-to-erasure under §45.1 platform-integrity exemption. Identity fields (`created_by`, `reason_note`) pseudonymized on DSAR within 30 days. |
| SellerSoftware | Org-life. On Seller Org deletion: soft delete immediately; hard purge 90 days later. KB namespace migrates to orphan namespace per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4. `created_by` / `updated_by` pseudonymized on deprovisioning. Residency: Seller Org's `data_residency_region`. |
| SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage | Published rows: Org-life. On Org delete or SellerSoftware soft-delete, transition to `archived`, 90-day retention, then purge. CDN + Schema.org cache busted within 30 days. Public pages are non-PII by construction; any PII in authored copy subject to DSAR sweep (30 days). |
| CategoryPage / GuidePage / ComparisonPage | Platform-life while referenced Category is `active`. On Category deprecation, archived + 301-redirected for 180 days, then purged. Rejected drafts purged after 90 days. No PII; DSAR not applicable. |
| MarketIntelligenceReport | Platform-life; auto-archive after 8 quarters. Archived rows keep URL with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` and a "Report archived" PDF landing page; purged only on category hard-deprecation. Any authored PII redacted within 30 days on DSAR. |
| HeatMapCell | 24 months of raw cells retained. After 24 months: raw purged; quarterly roll-ups preserved in MarketIntelligenceReport. No PII; DSAR not applicable. |
| GhostBidImport — `raw_text` and `parsed_qa_pairs_json` | 90 days after `import_status=published`, then purged. KB entries produced persist per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 retention. Rejected/failed imports purged 30 days after terminal state. DSAR scans `raw_text` for PII; targeted redaction within 30 days. Residency: Seller Org region. |
| SellerSignal | Raw aggregates retained 180 days, then signal counts rolled into HeatMapCell and raw row purged. DSAR on a contributing buyer triggers recompute within 24 hours; if recompute drops cohort <k, signal suppressed. Residency: per `residency_region_scope`. |

## 40.3 Data Import {#40.3-data-import}

Enterprise customers receive assisted data import from existing procurement tools. Supported source formats: CSV, Excel, JSON.

**Process:**

1. Customer provides source data export.  
2. Import consultant maps source schema to Sourcera schema.  
3. Test import run. Customer reviews mappings and reconciles conflicts.  
4. Production import. Verification run. Audit log generated.

Typically 2-4 weeks. Sourcera does not modify source data; mapping is customer responsibility.

## 40.4 Import Round-Trip Fidelity {#40.4-import-round-trip-fidelity}

**Tested Guarantee:** A workspace exported to JSON and re-imported produces equivalent entities. Equivalence defined as:

- All requirement fields match exactly.  
- All vendor/target account mappings preserved.  
- All response text preserved (formatting may normalize).  
- Audit trail fields retained (timestamps, user IDs).  
- Internal relationships (Use Case ↔ Requirement, Requirement ↔ Response) preserved.

**Lost in Round-Trip:**

- Real-time presence indicators (last login, active sessions).  
- Transient Agent task states (in-progress Pre-Scoring operations).  
- WebSocket subscription state.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Round-trip test suite (sample workspaces exported → re-imported → validated).  
- Passes as part of regular QA for each release.  
- JSON import format documented for Enterprise customers.

## 40.5 Acceptance Criteria {#40.5-acceptance-criteria}

- All export formats complete within 30 seconds for workspaces with ≤ 10,000 requirements.  
- JSON export includes complete audit metadata.  
- Traceability Matrix export includes framework control mapping.  
- Import process preserves all entity relationships and timestamps.  
- Round-trip fidelity tested quarterly.

## 41.3 Email Compliance {#41.3-email-compliance}

- **CAN-SPAM:** Unsubscribe link \+ physical address (sourcera.io footer) in all emails.  
- **GDPR:** Transactional emails not subject to marketing consent. Marketing requires explicit opt-in. Transactional email address (`noreply@sourcera.io`) not used for marketing.  
- **CASL:** Same as GDPR (implied consent for transactional, explicit for marketing).  
- **Bounce Rate Target:** \< 2%.  
- **Complaint Rate Target:** \< 0.5%.  
- **Deliverability Monitoring:** Sent emails \> 100/day. Spam trap monitoring. List hygiene (bounce management, complaint handling).

## 41.4 Opt-Out Classification {#41.4-opt-out-classification}

| Email Type | Opt-Out Classification | Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Vendor Invitation, NDA, Q\&A, Response notifications, Phase advancement, SLA alerts, Comment mentions, Selection Report, Disqualification, EOI received, Workspace invitation, GDPR notifications | **Transactional (No opt-out)** | Sent regardless of preference. Cannot unsubscribe. |
| Trial expiring, plan downgrade warning | **Transactional-Critical** | Sent regardless of preference for account/billing changes. |
| Weekly Digest, feature announcements, webinar invitations | **Marketing/Lifecycle (Opt-in)** | Require explicit opt-in. Unsubscribe link in footer. User preference honored. |

## 41.5 Acceptance Criteria {#41.5-acceptance-criteria}

- All email templates have preview URL for QA review.  
- All transactional emails delivered within 60 seconds of trigger.  
- All marketing emails respect user opt-out preference.  
- Weekly digest emails include unsubscribe link in header and footer.  
- Bounce and complaint rates monitored weekly via Loops.so dashboard.  
- No transactional emails sent from marketing sender address.

| Free | None (best effort) | N/A | N/A |
| Business | 99.5% (22 min downtime/month max) | 24-hour response | SEV-3 only |
| Enterprise | 99.9% (43 sec downtime/month max) | 1-hour response | All severities |

**SLA Measurement:** Uptime measured via synthetic monitoring (Datadog endpoint checks) every 60 seconds from 3+ geographies. Latency measured per-endpoint (p95 \< 500ms, p99 \< 1s).

## 42.2 Monitoring & Alerting {#42.2-monitoring-&-alerting}

**Key Metrics:**

- API latency (p50, p95, p99)  
- Error rate (4xx, 5xx)  
- Database query latency  
- Convex Storage latency  
- Agent API latency and cost  
- Webhook delivery success rate

**Alerting Rules:**

| Condition | Severity | Action | Escalation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Error rate \> 1% | Warning | Alert to \#incident Slack channel | Page on-call if persists 5 min |
| API latency p95 \> 2s | Warning | Alert to \#incident Slack channel | Page on-call if persists 5 min |
| API latency p95 \> 5s | Critical | Page on-call immediately | 5-min response SLA |
| Database unavailable | Critical | Page on-call immediately | 5-min response SLA |
| Webhook delivery \< 95% | Warning | Alert to \#incident Slack channel | Manual escalation if persists 30 min |

## 42.3 Incident Response {#42.3-incident-response}

**Severity Definitions:**

| Severity | Impact | Response Time | Update Frequency |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **SEV-1 (Critical)** | Service completely unavailable or data loss | \< 15 minutes | Every 30 minutes |
| **SEV-2 (Major)** | Service degraded or partial outage | \< 1 hour | Every 60 minutes |
| **SEV-3 (Minor)** | Service fully functional, cosmetic issues | \< 4 hours | Daily |

**Process:**

1. Incident detected (alert or customer report).  
2. On-call paged. Severity assigned.  
3. War room opened (Slack \+ Zoom).  
4. Customer notified (Statuspage.io status update) for SEV-1/2.  
5. Mitigation actions executed.  
6. All-clear declared.  
7. Postmortem scheduled within 24 hours.  
8. RCA completed within 48 hours.

**Postmortem Artifacts:**

- Root cause analysis  
- Contributing factors  
- Preventive actions (code changes, process changes, monitoring improvements)  
- Action items (assign, estimate, track)  
- Published internally to team

## 42.4 Disaster Recovery Targets {#42.4-disaster-recovery-targets}

| Metric | Target |
| :---- | :---- |
| **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)** | 1 hour |
| **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)** | 1 hour |

**Backups:**

- **Database:** Convex-managed snapshots hourly (aligned with 1-hour RPO) and daily (30-day retention).  
- **Object Storage (Files):** Geo-redundant (S3 replication, multi-region).  
- **Test Restore:** Quarterly restore tests. Restore to staging environment. Verify data integrity.

**Failover:** Convex provides transparent multi-region failover. Sourcera application code is stateless. No manual intervention needed. Automatic DNS failover (sub-60 second TTL).

## 42.5 On-Call Rotation {#42.5-on-call-rotation}

- 24/7 on-call coverage (Business & Enterprise).  
- Primary \+ secondary on-call.  
- Rotation weekly.  
- Incident history tracked in Pagerduty (paid plan).  
- Page timeout escalation: 10 minutes → escalate to secondary.

## 42.6 Observability Stack {#42.6-observability-stack}

| Component | Purpose | Tool |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Logging** | Structured logs (JSON) for all API requests, errors, state changes | Pino (application) → Datadog |
| **Metrics** | System and application metrics (latency, throughput, errors) | Datadog Agent |
| **Tracing** | Distributed request tracing (API → DB → Agent) | OpenTelemetry → Datadog |
| **Error Tracking** | Application errors and exceptions | Sentry |
| **Alerting** | Alert routing, escalation, notification | Datadog \+ PagerDuty |
| **Status Communication** | Public incident status | Statuspage.io |
| **Dashboards** | Real-time health visualization | Datadog dashboards |

**On-Call Runbooks:** Stored in Notion. Linked from Datadog alerts. Cover: common SEV-1/2 scenarios, diagnostic steps, mitigation playbooks, rollback procedures.

## 42.7 Acceptance Criteria {#42.7-acceptance-criteria}

- Uptime SLA met per month (tracked via Datadog dashboard).  
- All SEV-1 incidents have RCA posted within 48 hours.  
- Postmortem action items tracked and closed within 30 days.  
- Alert false positive rate \< 5% per month.  
- Restore test passes quarterly (data integrity verified).  
- On-call team trained on all runbooks (quarterly review).
