# 43\. Internal Operations & Admin Tooling {#43.-internal-operations-&-admin-tooling}

## 43.1 Admin Dashboard {#43.1-admin-dashboard}

**Organization Management:**

- View all organizations, users per org, current plan, billing status  
- Search by org name, domain, email  
- Pause/unpause subscriptions (for billing holds or violations)  
- View usage (workspaces, members, API calls, agent tokens)  
- GDPR data export initiation (DSAR response generation)

**Workspace Management:**

- View workspaces per org, current phase, member count, requirement count  
- Search workspaces by name  
- Reset workspace (clear all data, return to Phase 1). Requires confirmation.  
- Archive/delete workspace. Requires confirmation \+ org admin approval.  
- Bulk export (multiple workspaces to JSON).

**User Management:**

- View all users, org memberships, roles, last login  
- Reset password (email reset link to user)  
- View/revoke API tokens (list all tokens, show creation date, expiration date)  
- View user audit log (all actions by this user across all orgs)  
- Suspend/deactivate user (login blocked, but data retained)  
- Trigger SCIM deprovisioning sync

**Billing Management:**

- View subscriptions (plan, status, renewal date, invoice history)  
- View invoices (paid, pending, overdue)  
- Manually apply discounts (percentage or fixed dollar amount)  
- Manually adjust plan (override plan tier for specific org, set expiration date)  
- Trial management (create, extend, convert to paid)  
- Refund management (initiate refund, provide reason)  
- Stripe integration (view disputes, manage payment methods)

**Marketplace Moderation:**

- View all marketplace listings (active, pending review, flagged)  
- Approve/reject listings (provide feedback)  
- View listings flagged for abuse (spam, fraud, harmful content)  
- Hide listings pending review (user notified)  
- View appeal history (user can appeal rejection)  
- Send enforcement message to seller (account warning, listing removal)  
- Ban seller from marketplace (permanent, requires escalation approval)

**Agent Debugging:**

- View Agent call history (organization, date, task type, cost, latency, status)  
- Search by workspace or requirement  
- View Agent prompt and response (full context)  
- Retry Agent task (useful for transient failures)  
- View Agent token usage (per org, per month)

## 43.2 Admin Dashboard Access Control {#43.2-admin-dashboard-access-control}

Only Sourcera internal staff (marked `is_staff: true` on user record) can access admin dashboard. Access requires:

- Sourcera user account  
- `org_id: null` (not member of any customer org)  
- `is_staff: true` flag (set by Sourcera ops team manually)

## 43.3 Support Tools {#43.3-support-tools}

- **Zendesk Integration:** Tickets linked to customer organizations (auto-populated via email domain). Ticket history searchable in admin dashboard.  
- **Customer Impersonation:** "Assume user session" button (Enterprise support only). Assumes the user's session context, can see what user sees. Fully audit logged (timestamp, admin name, duration, actions taken).  
- **Workspace Export:** One-click export for troubleshooting. Downloads complete JSON snapshot.  
- **Datadog Dashboard:** Real-time platform health, error rates, latency distribution. Linked from admin dashboard.  
- **Sentry Dashboard:** Application error tracking. Linked from admin dashboard.  
- **PostHog Events:** User behavior analysis. Linked from admin dashboard.

## 43.4 Audit Logging for Admin Actions {#43.4-audit-logging-for-admin-actions}

All admin actions logged to a dedicated `admin_audit_log` table:

- Action (reset password, apply discount, assume session, etc.)  
- Admin user  
- Target organization / user  
- Timestamp  
- Details (discount amount, plan override tier, etc.)  
- IP address

Admin audit logs retained forever and not subject to plan tier retention limits.

## 43.5 Acceptance Criteria {#43.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Admin dashboard loads in \< 2 seconds.  
- All admin actions require confirmation (double-click pattern).  
- Customer impersonation fully audit logged.  
- Admin actions never affect production customer data (dry-run option available for batch operations).  
- Admin can quickly find orgs/users (search ≤ 500ms).  
- Marketplace abuse report SLA: reviewed within 24 hours, action taken or appeal process initiated.

# 44\. Performance Requirements {#44.-performance-requirements}

## 44.1 Performance Targets {#44.1-performance-targets}

| Metric | Target |
| :---- | :---- |
| First Contentful Paint | \< 1s |
| Time to Interactive (TTI) | \< 2s |
| API Response Latency (p95, excluding Agent) | \< 500ms |
| API Response Latency (p99, excluding Agent) | \< 1s |
| Real-time Subscription Latency (collaborative scoring) | \< 200ms |
| Search Index Latency (Command Palette fuzzy search) | \< 200ms |
| PDF Export (100 requirements) | \< 5s |
| Workspace Load (1,000 requirements, matrix view) | \< 2s |
| **Agent Pre-Score per Requirement** | 10-30s (Sonnet) |
| **Agent Pre-Score per Workspace** | budget \= count × 15s (e.g., 100 requirements ≈ 25 minutes) |
| **Selection Report Generation** | \< 5 minutes (Opus, includes narrative \+ optional appendices) |

## 44.2 Agent Performance Budgets {#44.2-agent-performance-budgets}

**Pre-Score Per-Requirement Latency:**

- Haiku: 5-10s  
- Sonnet: 10-30s  
- Opus: 30-60s (used for reasoning-heavy requirements only)

**Full Workspace Pre-Score:**

- Budget: `requirement_count × 15 seconds` (average case)  
- Example: 100 requirements → max 25 minutes  
- Parallelization: Process up to 10 requirements concurrently → effective duration ≈ 2.5 minutes for 100 reqs

**Cost Estimates (per requirement, list price):**

- Haiku: $0.02-0.05 (input tokens: 500-1000, output tokens: 100-200)  
- Sonnet: $0.05-0.15 (input tokens: 1000-1500, output tokens: 200-400)  
- Opus: $0.15-0.40 (input tokens: 1500-2000, output tokens: 300-500)

**Monthly Agent Token Budget:**

- Free: 50K tokens/month (≈ 500-1000 requirements pre-scored)  
- Business: 500K tokens/month (≈ 5000-10000 requirements pre-scored)  
- Enterprise: 5M tokens/month (unlimited)

## 44.3 Optimization Strategies {#44.3-optimization-strategies}

- **Code Splitting:** Routes lazily loaded. Command Palette and advanced features code-split.  
- **Database Indexing:** Requirements indexed by workspace\_id \+ status. Vendors by organization\_id. Scores by (workspace\_id, vendor\_id, requirement\_id) composite.  
- **Caching:** Workspace metadata (10-min TTL). Vendor profiles (1-hour TTL). Scoring rubrics (permanent, versioned).  
- **Compression:** GZIP for API responses and static assets.  
- **CDN:** Vercel's global edge network for static assets.  
- **Real-time Optimizations:** Convex subscriptions use delta updates (send only changed fields, not full entities).

## 44.4 Load Testing {#44.4-load-testing}

- **Monthly:** 500 concurrent users. Target p95 \< 1s.  
- **Quarterly:** 5× spike tests (2,500 concurrent users). Target p95 \< 3s (degraded but functional).  
- **Quarterly:** 24-hour endurance test (steady 100 concurrent users). Monitor for memory leaks, connection exhaustion.

## 44.5 Acceptance Criteria {#44.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Production p95 latency consistently \< 500ms (excluding Agent calls).  
- Production p99 latency consistently \< 1s (excluding Agent calls).  
- No single API call times out (server-side timeout: 30s).  
- Real-time collaborative features sync \< 200ms (measured via WebSocket delta timing).  
- Agent calls stay within budget (95% within allotted time, 5% timeout with graceful degradation).

# 45\. Privacy & Abuse Prevention {#45.-privacy-&-abuse-prevention}

## 45.1 Data Privacy {#45.1-data-privacy}

- **Data Ownership:** All customer data owned by the Organization. Sourcera is Data Processor.  
- **Model Training:** No customer data used for model training. Claude calls do not train models.  
- **Analytics:** Aggregated anonymized metrics sent to PostHog for product analytics (feature adoption, user behavior). No PII in analytics events.  
- **Error Logs:** May include non-sensitive metadata (user ID, feature name, error code) but never requirement text, response data, or customer-specific scores.  
- **Data Processor Agreement (DPA):** Available for all plans. Sourcera signs DPA for GDPR compliance.  
- **Subprocessor List:** Published at sourcera.io/compliance/subprocessors. Updated quarterly.

## 45.2 Abuse Prevention {#45.2-abuse-prevention}

- **Rate Limiting:** Section 32.4. Per-org, per-API-key, per-user concurrency.  
- **Login Throttling:** Exponential backoff after 5 failed attempts (WorkOS-managed). Account locked for 15 minutes.  
- **API Token Rotation:** Recommended 90 days. Enforced for Enterprise (token expires after 90 days).  
- **Response Validation:** No executable scripts in responses. Sandboxed rendering. Strict Markdown sanitization (no raw HTML, no external images, no script execution).  
- **Marketplace Abuse Reporting:** Buyer can report vendor listing as spam, fraud, or harmful. Report → admin queue → 24-hour SLA → listing hidden pending review → seller notified → appeal process (seller can provide rebuttal within 7 days).

## 45.3 Marketplace Abuse Escalation {#45.3-marketplace-abuse-escalation}

**Abuse Report Workflow:**

1. **Report Filed:** Buyer clicks "Report Listing" on marketplace. Describes issue (spam, fraud, harmful, competitor sabotage, etc.). Listing ID and timestamp recorded.  
     
2. **Admin Queue:** Report added to admin queue in admin dashboard. Queue status: `pending_review`.  
     
3. **24-Hour SLA:** Admin reviews report within 24 hours. Assessment: confirmed or dismissed.  
     
4. **If Confirmed:** Listing status changed to `flagged_for_review`. Listing hidden from marketplace (public browse still works if direct link, but not discoverable). Seller notified by email: "Your listing \[name\] is under review. \[reason\]. You may appeal within 7 days."  
     
5. **Seller Appeal:** Seller can appeal via link in email. Provides rebuttal. Admin re-reviews (additional 24-hour SLA). Decision: upheld or overturned.  
     
6. **If Overturned:** Listing un-hidden. Seller notified: "Your appeal was accepted. Listing restored."  
     
7. **If Upheld:** Listing remains hidden. Seller notified: "Your appeal was denied. Listing remains under review."  
     
8. **Persistent Violations:** Repeated reports on same seller or violations of usage policy → escalation to Sourcera management → potential seller ban from marketplace (permanent, irreversible).

## 45.4 Acceptance Criteria {#45.4-acceptance-criteria}

- All customer data retention policies documented and enforced.  
- DPA available on request (all plans) and signed for Enterprise.  
- Marketplace abuse reports processed within 24 hours.  
- Rate limits enforced per Section 32.4.  
- No customer data included in error logs or analytics.

# 46\. Test Strategy & QA Framework {#46.-test-strategy-&-qa-framework}

## 46.1 Test Pyramid {#46.1-test-pyramid}

| Level | Coverage | Tools |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Unit** | ≥ 80% | Vitest |
| **Integration** | ≥ 60% | Vitest \+ Convex test harness |
| **E2E** | ≥ 40% (critical paths) | Playwright |

## 46.2 Advanced Feature Test Cases {#46.2-advanced-feature-test-cases}

### Collaborative Scoring (Section 12\)

- \[E2E\] Two reviewers score same requirement-vendor pair. Grades sync in real-time (\< 500ms).  
- \[E2E\] "Score Independently" toggle hides teammate grades for unbiased scoring.  
- \[Integration\] Insight Card generated on divergence \> 0.3.  
- \[Unit\] `scored_collaboratively` flag set correctly.  
- \[Unit\] Grade aggregation (average) correct for 3+ reviewers.

### Policy Ingestion (Section 11\)

- \[E2E\] Upload NIST 800-53 PDF → framework detected → controls extracted → review UI → accept/reject → triage queue.  
- \[E2E\] Non-standard document → generic extraction → no control mapping.  
- \[Unit\] Deduplication identifies ≥ 90% true duplicates (semantic match).  
- \[E2E\] Traceability Matrix generated and exportable (CSV/Excel).  
- \[E2E\] Policy requirements tagged with framework source control and version.

### TCO Modeling (Section 14\)

- \[E2E\] Create TCO Use Case → add pricing requirements (6 types) → vendors submit → 3-year TCO calculated.  
- \[Unit\] TCO formula handles all 6 pricing structures correctly (flat, tiered, one-time, percentage, range, discount).  
- \[E2E\] TCO data exported to Excel with formulas (references, calculations).  
- \[E2E\] Scenario modeling affects TCO calculations (weight adjustment does not affect TCO scores).

### Scenario Modeling (Section 13\)

- \[E2E\] Enter Simulation Mode → override weights → save scenario → load scenario → compare baseline.  
- \[Integration\] Score recalculation under scenario parameters is correct (vendor rankings may shift).  
- \[E2E\] Reset clears overrides.  
- \[E2E\] Multiple scenarios compared side-by-side.

### Organizational Intelligence (Section 24\)

- \[E2E\] Navigate to Intelligence → vendor history loads → efficiency metrics display → discrepancies flagged.  
- \[Integration\] Briefing generated (Sonnet, \~500 tokens).  
- \[Unit\] Cross-evaluation performance metrics calculated correctly (average score, completion time, approval rate).

### Capability Declarations (Section 25\)

- \[E2E\] Declare capability → upload evidence → badge appears → indexed in Marketplace.  
- \[E2E\] Buyer searches by capability → matching vendors appear.  
- \[E2E\] Capability filter on marketplace (Business+) works.

### Command Palette (Section 19\)

- \[E2E\] `Cmd+K` → "disagree" → disagreement filter applied.  
- \[E2E\] `Cmd+K` → "simulate" → Simulation Mode enters.  
- \[Unit\] Context-aware filtering (e.g., `go tco` hidden when no TCO Use Case).  
- \[E2E\] Fuzzy search results correct (relevance ranking).

### Real-Time Collaboration (Convex OT)

- \[E2E\] User A edits requirement description. User B sees changes in real-time (\< 200ms).  
- \[E2E\] Concurrent edits (A and B edit same field simultaneously) → conflict resolution correct.  
- \[Integration\] Presence indicators show active users (cursor \+ avatar).

### API

- \[Integration\] All API endpoints functional (CRUD operations).  
- \[Unit\] Rate limits enforced (10,001st request → 429).  
- \[Unit\] Pagination cursor-based, consistent across list endpoints.  
- \[Unit\] Error codes return correct HTTP status (Appendix I).  
- \[E2E\] Webhook delivery and retry (test with mock consumer endpoint).

### Mobile Responsiveness

- \[E2E\] Mobile viewport (375px) displays without horizontal scroll.  
- \[E2E\] Touch targets ≥ 48px on mobile.  
- \[E2E\] Read workflows fully functional on mobile (view requirements, responses, comments).  
- \[E2E\] Limited write workflows (comments, boolean responses) fully functional on mobile.

## 46.3 QA Process {#46.3-qa-process}

**Pre-Release:**

- All tests pass (unit, integration, E2E).  
- Axe DevTools accessibility audit passes (zero violations).  
- Manual regression on critical paths (Phases 1-13 progression, scoring, API).  
- Load test (500 concurrent users, p95 \< 1s).  
- Datadog dashboard green (error rate \< 1%, latency p95 \< 500ms).

**Release:**

- Feature flag rollout to 10% (canary) via PostHog.  
- Monitor 24 hours (error rate, latency, user feedback).  
- If stable, 100% rollout.  
- Post-release monitoring 48 hours.

## 46.4 Feature Flag System {#46.4-feature-flag-system}

Advanced features are individually flaggable via **PostHog Feature Flags**.

| Flag | Feature | Default |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `collaborative_scoring` | Real-time collaborative scoring | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `policy_ingestion` | Policy Ingestion | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `scenario_modeling` | Scenario Modeling | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `tco_modeling` | TCO Modeling | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `organizational_intelligence` | Organizational Intelligence | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `capability_declarations` | Capability Declarations | On (all sellers) |
| `marketplace_capability_filter` | Marketplace capability filtering | Off (enable for Business+) |
| `ai_vendor_research` | AI Vendor Research (Perplexity) | Off (enable for Enterprise) |

Feature flags evaluated in combination with plan tier entitlements. A feature must pass both the flag check and the entitlement check to be accessible.

## 46.5 Acceptance Criteria {#46.5-acceptance-criteria}

- All sections with features have explicit acceptance criteria (already met in Sections 1-30; Sections 31-47 maintain parity).  
- E2E test coverage ≥ 40% of critical user flows.  
- Unit test coverage ≥ 80% of business logic.  
- Pre-release QA sign-off required before deployment.  
- All bugs fixed before 100% rollout.

# 47\. Governance & Future Roadmap {#47.-governance-&-future-roadmap}

## 47.1 Specification Versioning {#47.1-specification-versioning}

This specification is versioned using semantic versioning: Major.Minor.Patch.

- **Major:** Breaking API changes, fundamental architecture shifts.  
- **Minor:** New features, non-breaking schema changes, behavioral enhancements.  
- **Patch:** Bug fixes, clarifications, documentation updates.

Current version: **6.0.0** (released 2026-04-11).

## 47.2 Change Management Process {#47.2-change-management-process}

**Minor/Patch Changes:**

1. Change proposed (feature request, bug report, clarification).  
2. Reviewed by Product and Engineering leads.  
3. Specification section(s) updated. Version incremented (Minor or Patch).  
4. Changelog generated (Section 1.4 will maintain a change log of all versions).  
5. Deployed to staging. QA validates.  
6. Rolled out to production via feature flag (canary → 100%).

**Major Changes:**

1. Change proposed (RFC document).  
2. All-hands review. Feedback collected.  
3. Specification rewritten (new major version).  
4. Deprecated features marked with sunset date (minimum 6 months notice).  
5. Migration guide published.  
6. Old version kept in read-only archive.

## 47.3 Known Limitations & Future Work (Phase 2+) {#47.3-known-limitations-&-future-work-(phase-2+)}

| Item | Current | Phase 2 Target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| RTL Support | CSS-ready; UI deferred | Full RTL (Arabic, Hebrew) |
| i18n Languages | English only | Spanish, French, German, Japanese |
| Customer-Managed Encryption Keys | — | Available for Enterprise |
| Field-Level PII Encryption | — | Automatic for sensitive fields |
| Custom Scoring Rubrics | Fixed rubrics per response type | Custom rubrics per requirement |
| Requirement Hierarchies | Flat (no dependencies) | Dependency trees (with blockers) |
| Custom Pipeline Phases | Fixed 13 phases | Customizable phase structure (Enterprise) |
| Two-Sided Marketplace Ratings | Not supported (by design) | Alternative: objective performance metrics |
| Agent Fine-Tuning | Public Claude models only | Custom fine-tuned models (Enterprise, Phase 3\) |
| Video Demos | Not supported | Native video upload \+ AI summarization |
| Mobile Full Parity | Read \+ limited write | Full write (scoring, editing) |

## 47.4 Data Residency & Compliance Expansion {#47.4-data-residency-&-compliance-expansion}

**Current:**

- Data residency region selectable (data\_residency\_region on Organization).  
- GDPR DPA signed.  
- SOC 2 Type II targeted.

**Phase 2:**

- ISO 27001 certification.  
- HIPAA BAA available.  
- CCPA compliance certified.  
- Data sovereignty for APAC (Singapore data center).

## 47.5 Acceptance Criteria {#47.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Specification version tracked in Git (semantic versioning).  
- All breaking changes communicated 6+ months in advance.  
- Changelog maintained for each version.  
- Feature flags allow incremental rollout of new features.  
- Deprecated features have minimum 6-month sunset period.

## Appendix A: Requirement Status State Machine {#appendix-a:-requirement-status-state-machine}

**State Diagram:**

draft ──→ active ──→ finalized ──→ archived

  ↑                      │

  └──────────────────────┘  (via Revert Rule, Phases 2-5 only)

amendments:

finalized ──→ active (amended) ──→ finalized (re-amended)

(Phases 6-9 only, via Amendment Protocol)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| draft | active | Requirement Owner marks complete | All required fields populated (title, description, weight, response\_type) | Auto-transitions on field completion. Reversible. |
| active | finalized | Phase 1 → Phase 2 advancement | Part of phase gate validation. All requirements must be active or finalized. | Irreversible unless Revert applied. |
| finalized | draft | Revert Rule (Section 9.4) | Phases 2-5 only. Workspace Owner/Admin action. | Triggered when requirement needs editing before vendor release. |
| finalized | active (amended) | Amendment Protocol (Section 9.5) | Phases 6-9 only. Workspace Owner action. | Version increments. Vendor's existing response marked `needs_reverification`. |
| active (amended) | finalized | Re-verification approved | Vendor re-submits updated response. Buyer accepts. | Version increments. New version becomes current. |
| (any) | archived | Workspace reaches Phase 13 | Automatic. All requirements in workspace archived. | Soft delete. Recoverable for 30 days. |
| archived | (none) | Workspace purge after 30 days | Automatic, permanent purge. | No recovery after purge. |

## Appendix D: Response Status State Machine {#appendix-d:-response-status-state-machine}

**State Diagram:**

pending ──→ draft ──→ submitted ──→ locked

                         │              ↑

                         └→ needs\_reverification ──→ submitted (re-verified) ──→ locked

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| pending | draft | Vendor opens response form | Response form accessed; no data required | Initial state when requirement released to vendor. |
| draft | submitted | Vendor clicks "Submit" | All required fields populated per response type | Buyer notified. Response locked from further vendor edits (until amendment). |
| submitted | locked | Phase 9 entry (Submissions Closed) | Automatic on phase advancement | Vendor cannot edit response. |
| submitted | needs\_reverification | Requirement amended (Amendment Protocol, Phases 6-9) | Buyer amends requirement via Amendment Protocol | Vendor notified. Response status changes. Existing submission moved to archive. New empty response created (`pending`). |
| needs\_reverification | draft | Vendor re-opens response to amend | Vendor clicks "Edit" on amended requirement | Vendor must re-verify against amended requirement. |
| draft (amended) | submitted (amended) | Vendor re-submits amended response | All required fields populated per amended response type | New version created. Buyer notified. |
| submitted (amended) | locked | Phase 9 entry | Automatic | Vendor cannot edit. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- All response status transitions logged to audit trail.  
- Vendor cannot submit incomplete responses (validation prevents Submit button click).  
- Amendment-triggered re-verification clearly communicated to vendor (banner in response form).

---

## Appendix E: Workspace & Bid Workspace Status State Machine {#appendix-e:-workspace-&-bid-workspace-status-state-machine}

### Workspace Status (Buyer Console)

**State Diagram:**

active ──→ archived

active ──→ canceled

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| active → archived | Manual archive OR Phase 13 entry | Workspace Owner can archive; automatic at Phase 13 | Soft delete. Recoverable for 30 days. |
| active → canceled | Workspace Owner cancels | Requires confirmation. Cannot undo. | Terminal state. Data purged after 30 days. |
| archived → (none) | N/A | Archived workspace cannot transition. | Recovery available within 30 days (manual un-archive). After 30 days, permanent purge. |

### Bid Workspace Status (Seller Console)

**State Diagram:**

draft ──→ active ──→ submitted ──→ closed

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| draft | NDA accepted by vendor | Vendor accepts NDA in Phase 4 | Bid Workspace auto-created. Initial status `draft`. |
| draft → active | Phase 5 entry (Bid Acceptance) | Buyer marks vendor as accepted | Bid Workspace unlocks. Vendor can view all requirements and begin responding. |
| active → submitted | Phase 9 entry (Submissions Closed) | Automatic phase advancement | Vendor console hard-locked. No further edits. |
| submitted → closed | Phase 13 entry (Closed) | Automatic phase advancement | Bid Workspace archived. Read-only access. Responses available for KB import. |

### Target Account Status (Vendor Curation)

**State Diagram:**

invited ──→ nda\_pending ──→ active ──→ closed

                   │

                   └───────→ withdrawn

                   

active ──────────→ disqualified

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| invited | Phase 3 entry (Vendor Curation) | Target Account created | NDA not yet sent. Vendor not yet invited. |
| invited → nda\_pending | NDA link sent to vendor | Buyer sends NDA | Waiting for vendor signature. |
| nda\_pending → active | Vendor signs NDA, Phase 5 entry | Phase 5 (Bid Acceptance) required for activation | Bid Workspace unlocked. Vendor can respond. |
| nda\_pending → withdrawn | Buyer retracts NDA (before vendor signs) | Buyer withdraws vendor from evaluation | Vendor notified. Bid Workspace not created. |
| active → disqualified | Buyer marks vendor as disqualified | Any phase after Phase 5 | Vendor notified. Bid Workspace marked read-only. Responses archived. |
| active → closed | Phase 13 entry (Closed) | Automatic | Target Account archived. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- All status transitions logged with timestamp and user attribution.  
- Status changes trigger appropriate email notifications.  
- Phase locks prevent invalid transitions (e.g., cannot mark as active before NDA).

## Appendix F: Webhook Retry & Recovery {#appendix-f:-webhook-retry-&-recovery}

**Retry Schedule:** 5 attempts over 24 hours.

| Attempt | Delay from Previous | Cumulative | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Immediate | 0 min | Initial delivery |
| 2 | 1 minute | 1 min | If attempt 1 fails |
| 3 | 15 minutes | 16 min | If attempt 2 fails |
| 4 | 1 hour | 76 min | If attempt 3 fails |
| 5 | 6 hours | 436 min (7.3 hrs) | If attempt 4 fails |

After 5 failures, the webhook is marked `failed`. Org Admin is notified via email. Failed webhooks available for manual retry from Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks (30-day retention).

**Success Criteria:** HTTP 2xx response within 10 seconds. Any other response (3xx, 4xx, 5xx, timeout) triggers next retry.

**Idempotency:** Each delivery includes unique `event_id`. Consumer must deduplicate. Same `event_id` delivered multiple times must produce idempotent result.

**Payload Signing:**

signature \= HMAC-SHA256(webhook\_secret, raw\_request\_body)

Header: X-Sourcera-Signature \= "sha256=" \+ hex(signature)

Consumer must verify signature before processing.

**Dead Letter Queue (DLQ):** Permanently failed deliveries (after 5 retries) stored in DLQ. Org can query DLQ via Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks. DLQ entries retained 30 days, then purged.

**Webhook Consumer Contract:**

- Accept HTTP POST request (JSON body).  
- Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature.  
- Deduplicate by `event_id`.  
- Process idempotently.  
- Return 2xx within 10 seconds.  
- If processing fails (internal error), return 5xx (will trigger retry).  
- If payload invalid (malformed), return 4xx (will NOT retry).

## Appendix H: Stripe Billing Model {#appendix-h:-stripe-billing-model}

### Subscription Products

| Product | Price | Billing | Renewal |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera-free` | $0/month | Tracking only (no payment method) | N/A |
| `sourcera-business` | $499/month (annual) or $599/month (monthly) | Recurring, auto-renew | Monthly or yearly |
| `sourcera-enterprise` | Custom | Annual contract | Annually |

### Metered SKUs

| SKU ID | Trigger | Pricing | Billing Granularity |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera_api_calls` | API call count | Free: $0.01/100 (beyond 1K). Business: $0.005/100 (beyond 10K). Enterprise: unlimited | Daily meter event |
| `sourcera_policy_ingestions` | Policy Ingestion count | Business: $25/ingestion (beyond 3/mo). Enterprise: unlimited | Per ingestion |
| `sourcera_agent_tokens` | Agent token usage | Business: $0.01/1000 tokens (beyond 500K/mo). Enterprise: included in contract | Daily meter event (1000-token units) |
| `sourcera_storage_overage` | Storage beyond plan limit (GB) | All plans: $0.10/GB/month | Daily meter event (1 GB units) |

### Billing Mechanics

- **Monthly Invoices:** Generated on subscription anniversary date.  
- **Line Items:** Subscription amount \+ metered overages \+ prorated changes.  
- **Auto-Charging:** Stripe auto-charges default payment method.  
- **Failed Charges:** 3 retries over 15 days. After final failure, subscription paused (access revoked until payment successful).  
- **Tax:** Stripe Billing handles Sales Tax/VAT/GST automatically (requires tax ID configuration).  
- **Meter Reporting:** Metered charges reported to Stripe daily. Events aggregated by date and SKU.  
- **Invoice Visibility:** Customer views invoices in Settings → Billing → Invoice History.

### Free-to-Paid Upgrade

- Free → Business: Immediate upgrade. Customer enters trial or paid subscription. Billing cycle starts on upgrade date (prorated for remainder of month if mid-cycle).  
- Business renewal: On anniversary date, Stripe charges subscription amount \+ metered overages from previous month.

### Plan Downgrade

- Business → Free: Effective at next renewal date. If current usage exceeds Free limits, customer enters "read-only overage" state and must resolve within 30 days (Section 34.6).  
- Metered charges stop on downgrade date.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Stripe webhooks synced (invoice.paid, customer.subscription.updated, etc.).  
- Metered charges reported daily, appear on next invoice.  
- Billing calculations audit trail (can trace any charge to source).  
- Failed payment retry logic honored (3 attempts over 15 days).

## Appendix J: Controlled Vocabulary Registry {#appendix-j:-controlled-vocabulary-registry}

**All enum values used throughout the specification are canonically defined here. Section 3 schema definitions must reference these values exactly.**

### Response Types

`boolean`, `qualitative`, `evidence`, `informational`, `pricing`

### Rubric Grade Categories

| Grade | Code | Value | Default PM (if PM mode) | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fully Meets | FM | 1.0 | 100% | Vendor response meets requirement fully, out of box |
| Partially Meets | PM | 0.6 (configurable per workspace, default) | Configurable (0.1-0.9) | Vendor response meets requirement partially; requires customization or integration |
| Does Not Meet | DNM | 0.0 | 0% | Vendor response does not meet requirement |
| Exception | EX | Excluded | — | Requirement scored as exception (excluded from vendor comparison, flagged in report) |

### Global Organization Roles

`org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin`, `member`, `guest`

**Notes.**
- `billing_admin` (added v7.0.0; §5.2, §5.2.1, §4.8, §34.12.6) — org-scoped, console-pooled billing & AI-accounting authority; orthogonal to `org_admin` (a user MAY hold both, but neither implies the other). See §5.2.1 for the full operation-level permission list and the Replacement Pattern that lets `org_owner` retain de facto Billing Admin authority when the role pool is empty.
- `org_owner` retains de facto Billing Admin authority by fallback per §5.2.1.2 even when the Org has zero `billing_admin` users — this is enforced at the API layer, not at the enum level.
- `member` and `guest` are NEVER Billing-Admin-eligible by direct grant — granting `billing_admin` to a `guest` is rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_admin_grant_target_ineligible_role` (new; Appendix I) per §5.2.1.2 Assignment.

### Billing Admin Audit Action Types (§5.2.1, §4.8.3, §4.8.5, §4.8.7, §4.8.8, §4.8.9, §4.8.10, §4.8.11, §34.12.6, §34.13)

The `billing_admin_action` namespace registers the qualified action enum used for every Billing Admin Audit View row (§5.2.1.4). Action strings follow the dotted form `org.<billing_subdomain>_<verb>`. The full enum is partitioned by subdomain:

**Wallet & Auto-Topup (§4.8.3):**

`org.wallet_viewed`, `org.wallet_overage_enabled`, `org.wallet_overage_disabled`, `org.wallet_overage_cap_changed`, `org.wallet_autotopup_enabled`, `org.wallet_autotopup_disabled`, `org.wallet_autotopup_config_changed`, `org.wallet_topup_manual_initiated`, `org.wallet_topup_failed`, `org.wallet_topup_succeeded`, `org.wallet_payment_failed_grace_entered`, `org.wallet_suspended`, `org.wallet_reactivated`, `org.wallet_closed`

**Free Allowance (§4.8.7):**

`org.free_allowance_viewed`, `org.free_allowance_quota_overridden_by_ops`

**AIOperation Ledger & Pricing (§4.8.1, §4.8.9):**

`org.billing_ledger_viewed`, `org.billing_ledger_exported`, `org.pricing_table_version_pinned`, `org.pricing_table_version_unpinned`, `org.pricing_history_viewed`

**ContestRecord (§4.8.5):**

`org.contest_filed`, `org.contest_viewed`, `org.contest_withdrawn`, `org.contest_decision_received`, `org.contest_credit_posted`

**CommittedSpendContract (§4.8.8):**

`org.committed_spend_viewed`, `org.committed_spend_renewal_opt_out`, `org.committed_spend_renewal_opt_out_reversed`, `org.committed_spend_signed`, `org.committed_spend_terminated`

**Plan Tier (§34):**

`org.plan_changed`, `org.plan_change_blocked_pending_ops_signoff`, `org.plan_downgrade_warning_acknowledged`

**Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (§34.13):**

`org.pro_trial_seat_allocated`, `org.pro_trial_seat_granted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_accepted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_declined`, `org.pro_trial_seat_acceptance_rejected`, `org.pro_trial_seat_converted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_auto_downgraded`, `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_overridden`, `org.pro_trial_seat_revoked_by_buyer`

**DowngradeExcessDataBucket (§4.8.10):**

`org.downgrade_bucket_viewed`, `org.downgrade_bucket_restored`, `org.downgrade_bucket_archive_pending_acknowledged`

**BillingSeatSnapshot (§4.8.11):**

`org.billing_seat_snapshot_viewed`

**Billing Admin Role Lifecycle (§5.2.1.2):**

`org.billing_admin_role_granted`, `org.billing_admin_role_granted_via_scim`, `org.billing_admin_role_revoked`, `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_enabled`, `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_disabled`

**Billing Admin Audit View Self-Reference (§5.2.1.4):**

`org.billing_audit_viewed`, `org.billing_audit_exported`

**Semantics:**

- Every action above is an Audit Event entity row (§4.6.1) with `action` = the qualified string above (the field's bare-verb enum is extended via this namespace; the bare-verb enum continues to govern non-billing entity audits unchanged).
- `status` ∈ `success`, `failure` per §4.6.1; on failure the action string is preserved and `failure_reason` populated.
- `entity_type` MUST be one of: `ai_wallet`, `contest_record`, `committed_spend_contract`, `pricing_table_version`, `pro_trial_seat_grant`, `organization_plan`, `free_allowance_counter`, `billing_seat_snapshot`, `downgrade_excess_data_bucket`, `billing_admin_role_assignment`, `audit_event_view`. The `entity_type` enum in §4.6.1 is extended accordingly (Authored Extension; logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`).
- `changes` JSON populated for state mutations (per §4.6.1); for read actions (`*_viewed`), `changes` is `{}` and `notes` carries the query-filter snapshot for forensic re-execution.
- Notification dispatches (§5.2.1.1 Operation #22) are NOT audit-logged at the recipient level; the underlying state-change event (e.g., `org.wallet_overage_enabled`) is the audit anchor.
- Retention: standard per §40.2 plan-tier defaults, with `org.contest_*` and `org.committed_spend_*` rows retained for 7 years on every plan (financial-record exception per §40.2 `extended_financial`).
- DSAR / right-to-erasure: per §6.8 the user attribution fields (`user_id`, `created_by`) anonymize on request; the action and `entity_id` survive (financial-record exception). For `billing_admin_role_assignment` audits, the deprovisioned user's `user_id` is replaced with the synthetic `anonymized_former_user_<hash>` token to preserve the role-change trail without exposing the deprovisioned identity.

### Referral Status

`pending`, `signed_up`, `activated`, `credit_issued`, `credit_redeemed`, `credit_expired`, `forfeited`, `flagged_fraud`, `revoked`

**Semantics:**

- `pending` — referral created, no signup yet.
- `signed_up` — referee Org provisioned, activation threshold not yet met.
- `activated` — referee met minimum-activity threshold; eligible for credit issuance on next nightly job.
- `credit_issued` — credit posted to referrer wallet; `credit_issued_at` populated.
- `credit_redeemed` — `credit_redeemed_usd = credit_value_usd` (fully used); Stripe Credit Notes captured.
- `credit_expired` — `credit_expires_at` passed with residual credit; residual forfeit.
- `forfeited` — credit withheld due to fraud or eligibility violation; `credit_forfeited_reason` populated.
- `flagged_fraud` — Signal Integrity Monitor flagged; Ops review pending; credit suspended.
- `revoked` — Ops manual revocation post-issuance (distinct from forfeited, which is pre-issuance block).

### Pro Trial Seat Status

`issued`, `invite_sent`, `provisioned`, `in_trial`, `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `vendor_declined`, `expired_unaccepted`, `buyer_revoked`, `fraud_blocked`

**Semantics:**

- `issued` — grant created; grant_code minted; invite not yet sent.
- `invite_sent` — vendor invite email dispatched via Loops.so.
- `provisioned` — vendor signed up; Seller Starter entitlements active; `trial_starts_at` set.
- `in_trial` — within 30-day trial window.
- `converted` — vendor converted to Seller Starter+ with payment method; `converted_at` + `converted_to_plan` set.
- `auto_downgraded` — day 31 reached with no conversion action; vendor downgraded to Seller Free; 90-day read-only preservation triggered.
- `vendor_declined` — vendor Billing Admin explicitly declined the grant during trial.
- `expired_unaccepted` — invite sent but vendor never signed up before 30-day invite TTL.
- `buyer_revoked` — buyer revoked grant before provisioning.
- `fraud_blocked` — Signal Integrity Monitor blocked; `anti_spam_hold_reason` populated.

### Pro Trial Seat Rejection Reasons

## Appendix K: Glossary {#appendix-k:-glossary}

**Authoring note:** The Sourcera project-level authoring conventions reference "Appendix-B Glossary." Appendix B in this specification is the Keyboard Shortcut Reference (preserved from v6.0.0). Glossary entries are collected here in Appendix K instead. Future integration phases should either (a) renumber appendices to elevate the Glossary, or (b) amend the authoring conventions to point at Appendix K. See RECONCILIATION.md → Known Gaps.

### Terms Introduced in §4.3 (v7.0.0 Integration)

**Internal Comment.** A private buyer-side comment surface attached to a Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Scenario, or Selection Report draft. Never visible to vendors or seller-console users. Materialized as three entities: Internal Comment Thread (container), Internal Comment Post (content), and Internal Comment Mention (normalized @-mention record). See §4.3.11, §4.3.12, §4.3.13.

**Internal Comment Thread.** Container entity for Internal Comment Posts. Polymorphically anchored to a workspace-scoped entity via `attached_to_type` and `attached_to_id`. See §4.3.11.

**Internal Comment Post.** An individual post within an Internal Comment Thread. Editable by the author for 15 minutes after creation; overridable by Workspace Owner with audit. See §4.3.12.

**Internal Comment Mention.** A normalized @-mention record linking an Internal Comment Post to a targeted User. Drives notification fan-out and the `has_unread_mention` flag on Unread Markers. `mention_kind` supports `user`, `team`, and `role` targets, with team/role expansions frozen at mention time. See §4.3.13.

**Presence Record.** A Convex Presence-backed, session-scoped, ephemeral entity that tracks live-cursor and collaboration state for an active user session. Not persisted to cold storage; never subject to DSAR export; excluded from round-trip import/export fidelity. See §4.3.14 and §40.4.

**Unread Marker.** A per-user-per-thread unread-count tracker shared across Internal Comment Threads, Q&A Threads, and Inbox Item Groups. One row per (user, thread_type, thread_id) tuple; `thread_type` resolves polymorphically. Drives in-app badge counts and the Inbox unread experience. See §4.3.15.

**Buyer Referral.** M16 growth-mechanic entity tracking a structured referrer → referee relationship with credit issuance, fraud signals, activity gating, and Stripe Credit Note reconciliation. Cross-referenced by Summary C.74. See §4.3.16.

**Referral Code.** 10-character URL-safe Base32 string, unique per Buyer Referral, used in magic-link redemption.

**Minimum Activity Threshold.** Referee-side activity bar that must be reached before a Buyer Referral transitions to `activated` status and becomes credit-eligible. Default: referee Org has completed ≥1 workspace through Phase 9 with ≥3 paid users. Configurable by Ops via C.97; version-stamped on each Buyer Referral for retroactive-change safety.

**Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant.** M17 entity that records the lifecycle of a single 30-day Seller Starter trial gifted from a buyer (Scale or Enterprise) to an invited vendor. Pool-accounted against the buyer's billing month. Complements §34.13 procedure with the persistent record. See §4.3.17.

**Grant Code.** 16-character URL-safe Base32 string, unique per Pro Trial Seat Grant, used in vendor signup URL.

**Dual-Projection Read.** API pattern applied to Pro Trial Seat Grants: a single endpoint returns different field projections depending on whether the requesting Org is the buyer (issuer) or the vendor (redeemer). Third-party Orgs receive HTTP 404. Authored in §4.3.17.

**Usage Event.** Canonical product-analytics ledger entity mirroring every buyer- and seller-side action. Dual-written to Convex (system of record for billing and DSAR) and PostHog (dashboards and long-tail analytics) via an outbox pattern. Standardized property schema per C.89. See §4.3.18.

**Outbox Pattern (PostHog).** Pattern for dual-writing Usage Events: Convex is the source of truth; PostHog delivery is tracked via `posthog_delivery_status` with idempotent retry keyed on `id`. Skipped when DSAR redaction is mid-process.

**Time-Saved Credit.** C.91 Time-Saved Baseline Model output. One credit per qualifying Usage Event. Version-stamped against the conversion-factor policy at credit time so Ops edits do not retroactively change dashboard totals. Supports reversal entities for retroactive AI-outcome undoes. See §4.3.19.

**Conversion Factor.** Capability-specific minutes-saved-per-event value used by the Time-Saved Baseline Model to convert Usage Events into labor-hours-saved estimates. Managed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager; version-stamped.

**Loaded Hourly Rate.** Labor rate used to monetize Time-Saved minutes into USD. Org-default with optional per-user override (Enterprise only) and Ops calibration override. Stored on each Time-Saved Credit row to preserve audit integrity across rate changes.

**Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM).** C.100 Ops surface that detects anomalous referral velocity, same-domain patterns, payment-method overlap, and suspicious grant issuance. Emits flags onto Buyer Referral `fraud_signal_flags` and Pro Trial Seat Grant `anti_spam_hold_reason`. Can trigger kill-switches on M16 and M17 mechanics.

**Pro Trial Seat Pool.** Buyer's monthly allocation of 5 (Scale) or 15 (Enterprise) Pro Trial Seats per §34.13.2. Replenishes on the buyer's billing anniversary. Unused seats do not carry over. Pool snapshots frozen on each grant via `buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant`.

**Author Role Snapshot.** Enum field on Internal Comment Post that freezes the author's workspace role at post time, preserving context across later role changes.

**Edit Lock Window.** 15-minute window from Post creation during which the author may edit or soft-delete (placeholder) their own post without admin involvement. Enforced server-side via `edit_locked_at`.

### Terms Introduced in §4.4 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 2)

**Marketplace Category.** The Ops-maintained, single-global taxonomy node used as the canonical FK target for SellerSoftware, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, HeatMapCell, and SellerSignal. Supports two-level hierarchy (parent + child) and deprecation-with-successor migrations. See §4.4.7. Maintained per Summary C.60.

**Vendor Opt-Out Record.** The append-only Opt-Out Registry entity per Summary C.123. A seller-authored suppression record that retroactively redacts the seller's name, pages, or product references from all public Sourcera-owned Marketplace content. Supports global, category-, software-, page-type-, and page-level scopes. Auto-honored on write; Ops post-hoc review governs approved/rejected/revoked state. See §4.4.8.

**SellerSoftware.** A distinct software product owned by a Seller Org (one-to-many). Carries its own slug, category, capability declaration refs, KB namespace, claim status, page status, and SEO status. See §4.4.9. Introduced per Summary §6.15.5.

**Claim Status (SellerSoftware).** The lifecycle state tracking whether a Seller Org has verified ownership of a SellerSoftware row. States: `unclaimed`, `claim_pending`, `claim_verified`, `claim_disputed`, `claim_revoked`. Verification methods include DNS TXT, verified email, Ops manual, and SSO domain match. See §4.4.9.

**KB Namespace (Software-Level).** A per-SellerSoftware KB namespace that isolates retrieval by product. Defined in KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4; referenced by SellerSoftware as `kb_namespace_id`. Migrated to the Org namespace on SellerSoftware soft-delete.

**SellerOrgPage.** The public, SEO-indexed page backing `/sellers/:slug` per Summary §6.15.4. Auto-enriched via the Opus-tier `page_enrichment` capability; seller-reviewed before publication. Enrichment billed to Platform Marketing. See §4.4.10.

**SoftwarePage.** The product-level equivalent of SellerOrgPage, backing `/software/:slug`. One-to-one with SellerSoftware. Publication requires `claim_status=claim_verified` on the parent. See §4.4.11.

**CategoryPage (M9).** AI-generated, editorially-reviewed per-category Marketplace landing page, powered by `category_faq_generation`. Sourcera-owned; Platform Marketing cost center; k-anonymity floor k=5. Summary C.67. See §4.4.12.

**GuidePage (M10).** Long-form "How to Evaluate [X]" SEO guide generated by `guide_draft_generation` and refreshed by `guide_refresh_analysis`. Sourcera-owned; Platform Marketing cost center; k-anonymity floor k=5. Summary C.68. See §4.4.13.

**ComparisonPage (M11).** AI-generated, continuously refreshed side-by-side software comparison page. Vendor opt-out honored globally via column suppression. Auto-archives when non-suppressed comparison count drops below 2. Summary C.69. See §4.4.14.

**MarketIntelligenceReport (M12).** Quarterly, k-anonymized (k=20) aggregate market intelligence publication produced by `market_intelligence_report`. Dual-sign-off (Marketing + Finance) required before publication. Summary C.70. See §4.4.15.

**HeatMapCell (M13).** Aggregated demand cell for the Public Marketplace Heat Map: one cell = one (category, region, industry, company_size_band, period). k-anonymity floor k=10. Summary C.71. See §4.4.16.

**GhostBidImport (M15).** A historical RFP ingestion record. Sellers paste or upload historical RFPs to seed their Software- or Org-level KB via `ghost_rfp_ingestion`. First import per Seller Org is free; subsequent imports bill as AI Operations. Summary C.73. See §4.4.17.

**SellerSignal.** Anonymized, aggregated buyer-intent record per Summary §6.17. Buyer opt-in; k-anonymity floor k=5. Delivered via in-app Dashboard, weekly digest, and CRM Sync. De-anonymization only on explicit buyer EOI or direct invite. See §4.4.18.

**Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule.** For every public-facing content entity that references a seller or product, the denormalized `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` field points at the active Vendor Opt-Out Record; `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` stamps the last registry evaluation. Nightly reconciliation enforces drift <1% between the denormalized pointer and the authoritative Registry. Introduced in §4.4.

**Sourcera-Owned Cost Center.** AI Operations performed by `category_faq_generation`, `guide_draft_generation`, `guide_refresh_analysis`, `comparison_page_generation`, `market_intelligence_report`, `page_enrichment`, and `seller_signal_aggregation` are billed to the internal Platform Marketing cost center, not to any customer Org. Summary §6.16.5.

**k-Anonymity Floor.** Minimum cohort size before any aggregate-derived fact is surfaced publicly. Floors per Summary §3.5: k=5 (SellerSignal, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage), k=10 (HeatMapCell), k=20 (MarketIntelligenceReport). Violations suppress or coarsen the rendered content.

**Claim Verification Method.** The mechanism by which a Seller Org proves ownership of a SellerSoftware row. One of: DNS TXT record, verified email at the seller's domain, Ops manual verification, or SSO domain match. See §4.4.9.

**Minor-Update Bypass (GuidePage).** A publish path for GuidePage that skips editorial re-review when `refresh_diff_score < 0.10`, allowing small cadence refreshes to land without reviewer involvement. Authored extension; flagged for human sign-off in RECONCILIATION.md.

**First-Import-Free Rule.** A Seller Org's first successful GhostBidImport transition to `published` does not create an AI Operation billing entry; second and subsequent imports do. Computed atomically at publish via a reconciliation worker that handles race conditions between concurrent imports.

**Distinctiveness Score (SellerSignal).** A secondary check on top of the raw k-anon floor that suppresses a signal when the combination of (region, industry, company_size_band) is narrow enough that identifying a single contributing buyer becomes feasible even at cohort ≥ k. Threshold governed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager.

### Terms Introduced in §4.5 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 3)

**Taxonomy Node.** The single platform-scoped registry behind every controlled-vocabulary dimension the Marketplace depends on beyond Marketplace Category. Multi-kind (one table, one state machine, `kind`-scoped namespacing), Ops-managed, versioned, deprecation-aware with successor-pointer migrations. Two-level hierarchy max (depth 0 or 1). For `kind=marketplace_category`, the paired §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row holds authority over category-specific fields; the Taxonomy Node row exists as a shared-registry projection. See §4.5.4. Summary C.60 and C.95.

**Taxonomy Projection (Marketplace Category).** The 1:1 pairing between a `kind=marketplace_category` Taxonomy Node row and a §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row. Reconciled nightly by `taxonomy_projection_drift` alert; mismatches raise an Ops alert.

**Taxonomy Merge.** The Ops operation that collapses a Taxonomy Node into its `successor_id`. Executes FK rewrites on all referencing entities in idempotent batches of 500 with a 10-minute bounded-lag SLO. Transitions source node to `merged`; irreversible post-completion.

**Taxonomy Redirect Chain.** The 301 redirect path generated by deprecated Taxonomy Nodes with `deprecation_action=redirect_to_successor`. Maximum chain depth is 3 hops; the 4th hop returns 410 with a canonical fallback to the root Marketplace index.

**Controlled-Vocabulary Tag.** The individual, seller-referenceable tag values attached to Capability Declarations, Marketplace Listings, Seller Profile industries and certifications, and SoftwarePage structured data. Finer-grained than Taxonomy Node (a Taxonomy Node represents a dimension; a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag represents an individual published value under a dimension). Sellers MAY propose new tags via the §27.6 proposal workflow; Ops approval gates publication. Append-only once approved; retirement via deprecation-with-successor. See §4.5.5.

**Sellers-Cannot-Create-Freeform-Tags Rule.** The write-layer enforcement that every tag value written to any consumer entity (Capability Declaration, Marketplace Listing filter, Seller Profile industries/certifications, SoftwarePage structured data) MUST exist in `(state=approved AND visibility=public)` at the time of write. Violations return `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (HTTP 422) with a Levenshtein-based "did you mean" suggestion. Summary C.60. See §4.5.5.

**Vocab Tag Review SLA.** 5 business days from `submitted` → `in_review` → terminal decision on a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag proposal. Breach emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` and pages the `ops_marketing_editor` on-call. See §4.5.5.

**Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract.** The uniform precondition pipeline every marketplace-domain render path executes before emitting any row identifying a Seller Org or a SellerSoftware: acquire opt-out snapshot (≤ 60s), resolve scope matches, apply redaction decision, build Schema.org with suppressed-ids omitted, honor partial-opt-out page-type filters. Consolidated in §4.5.6 as a cross-reference to the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record entity.

**Retroactive Sweep (Vendor Opt-Out).** The worker that enumerates every already-published marketplace-domain page referencing a newly opted-out entity and re-renders each with the opt-out applied. Progress tracked in `retro_backfill_status`. SLO: ≤ 15 minutes for ≤ 10,000 pages; ≤ 60 minutes for ≤ 100,000; up to 4 hours for > 100,000 (with explicit Ops progress bar). Batching per `retroactive_sweep` retry-curve class in §31.

**Vendor Opt-Out Redaction Placeholder.** The deterministic, layout-preserving token emitted in place of an identifying row when the opt-out render contract suppresses a candidate (e.g., ComparisonPage emits an "Opted out" column rather than collapsing the column). See §4.5.6.

**Marketplace Abuse Report.** The first-class entity materializing the §45.3 abuse-escalation workflow. Supports buyer, seller, anonymous public, Ops-internal, and automated-signal reporters; polymorphic subject kinds; severity triage; seller appeal within a 7-day window; Ops 24-hour triage SLA; immutable `subject_snapshot_json` so closure survives subject hard-purge. See §4.5.7.

**Abuse Report Triage SLA.** 24 hours from `created_at` to the first transition out of `pending_review`. Breach stamps `sla_breach_at` and emits `abuse_report.sla_breach`.

**Appeal Magic Link.** The authenticated, deadline-gated link emailed to the subject Seller Org Admin when a Marketplace Abuse Report reaches `awaiting_seller_response`. Requires logged-in session match to the `subject_org_id` with `seller_org_admin` role; unauthenticated click routes to sign-in; link expires at `appeal_deadline_at`. See §4.5.7, §4.7.2 (reused for disqualification appeals).

**Subject Snapshot.** The immutable `subject_snapshot_json` captured on Marketplace Abuse Report creation. Preserves the subject content at report time so terminal Ops decision is possible even when the subject is subsequently hard-purged. See §4.5.7.

**EOI Acceptance Record.** The first-class, queryable, auditable record of the buyer-side one-click EOI acceptance decision referenced in Summary C.62 and §27.5. 1:1 with the §4.5.2 EOI Record; materializes a Target Account, emits a Console Bridge Event, dispatches seller and buyer-team notifications, and optionally materializes a Bid Workspace (immediately on `accept_and_skip_nda`, on NDA execution otherwise). Supports bulk acceptance (≤ 25 per batch) and reversal within 72 hours. See §4.5.8.

**One-Click Acceptance Flow.** The atomic, transactional sequence that fires on an EOI Acceptance Record write: Target Account creation, Console Bridge Event emission with firewall-redacted payload, seller notification via Loops.so, buyer-team notification fan-out per §18, EOI Record state transition to `approved`, optional Bid Workspace materialization, and Match Score snapshot stamping. See §4.5.8.

**Bulk Acceptance Batch.** A single API call that accepts up to 25 EOIs, producing one EOI Acceptance Record per EOI with a shared `bulk_accept_batch_id`. Per-record failures do not roll back the batch; successes remain. Rate-limited to 2 batches per 15 minutes per buyer user.

**Acceptance Reversal.** An append-only reversal record that points at the original EOI Acceptance Record (and vice-versa) and executes a reversal cascade: Target Account withdrawal, Bid Workspace cancellation, NDA revocation, Console Bridge Event emission of kind `eoi_acceptance_reversed`. Permitted by Workspace Owner/Admin within 72 hours of original acceptance; post-72h requires Ops. See §4.5.8.

**EOI Acceptance Seller-Visible Projection.** The fixed whitelist of EOI Acceptance Record fields carried across the firewall to the Seller Console: `{id, accepted_at, acceptance_action, acceptance_conditions, referenced_capability_declaration_ids, resulting_bid_workspace_id, nda_required, nda_record_id}`. All other fields (including `accepted_by_user_id`, `source_surface`, `bulk_accept_batch_id`, `match_score_*`, reversal internals) are NEVER returned to the seller. Enforced at the API serializer.

### Terms Introduced in §4.7 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 3)

**Console Bridge Event.** The authoritative per-change cross-console sync unit between a Buyer Workspace and its linked Seller Bid Workspace(s). One row per atomic source change (fan-out events produce N rows, one per Bid Workspace). Carries a firewall-compliant redacted payload, retry state, bounded-lag SLO metadata, conflict resolution disposition, and cross-Workspace correlation. Summary C.116 and C.117. See §4.7.1.

**Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) — Bridge Enforcement.** The two-layer redaction-and-projection enforcement applied by Console Bridge Event: write-time validator ensures `payload_json` conforms to the kind's field-level redaction whitelist and rejects mismatches with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation`; seller serializer applies a defense-in-depth secondary whitelist at read. Firewall violation patterns alert the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100). See §4.7.1.

**Redaction Verification Hash.** The sha256 hash over a canonicalized serialization of `payload_json` with the kind's whitelist applied. Stored on every Console Bridge Event; re-verified at every retry. Mismatch triggers firewall-violation rejection and SIM alert.

**Seller-Visible Projection (Console Bridge Event).** The kind-specific whitelist applied by the seller-side serializer to every Console Bridge Event read. Defense-in-depth over write-time redaction. QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` asserts compliance for each event kind. See §4.7.1.

**Bounded-Lag SLO (Console Bridge).** The 30-second SLO from `created_at` to `synced_at` per Summary C.117. Observable via `slo_bounded_lag_ms` and `slo_breach_flag`. Breach rate > 1% over a rolling 15-minute window pages Ops. Terminal `dlq` and `failed` states are excluded from the SLO accounting (surfaced separately as anomalies).

**Retry-Curve Class `console_bridge_standard`.** The exponential-backoff retry curve applied to Console Bridge Event apply failures: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s — 5 attempts total. Post-5 transitions to `dlq` with Ops alert. Defined in Appendix J; pending full §31 retry-curve taxonomy extension.

**Console Bridge DLQ.** The dead-letter queue state entered after 5 failed Console Bridge Event apply attempts. Visible in the buyer Workspace Bridge Health panel (full detail), the seller Bid Workspace Sync Health panel (redacted detail), and the Ops Console cross-Workspace bridge dashboard. Re-drive requires explicit Ops action (no automated re-drive) to prevent infinite loops on persistent failures. See §4.7.1.

**Idempotency Key (Console Bridge).** The unique `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, event_kind, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` tuple enforced by a unique index on Console Bridge Event rows. Duplicate writes return the existing row's id (HTTP 200) rather than failing. Prevents duplicate apply across restarts and retries.

**Fan-Out Group.** The `fanout_group_id` correlation id that groups Console Bridge Events produced by a single source operation broadcast to N Bid Workspaces (e.g., Amendment broadcast, account-level Vendor Disqualification cascade). One row per target; shared `fanout_group_id` enables batch observability. See §4.7.1.

**Superseded Event.** A Console Bridge Event in the `superseded` state, set when a newer event for the same source entity arrives before the current event is applied. The `superseded_by_event_id` pointer carries the forwarding. Implements `last_write_wins` conflict resolution for rapid successive edits. See §4.7.1.

**Last-Write-Wins (Console Bridge).** The default conflict-resolution rule for concurrent buyer-side edits on the same source entity. Newer event supersedes older pending/retrying events. Alternatives per event kind: `buyer_origin_wins` (bidirectional conflicts), `operation_non_idempotent_dlq` (non-idempotent operations like `requirement_reverted` on amended versions), `merge_op` (Amendments are rebased against current state). See §4.7.1.

**Daily Bridge Reconciliation.** The 2am UTC job per §25.2 that scans for stale Console Bridge Events (`pending` or `retrying` > 24h) across all workspaces, escalates to DLQ or re-drives as appropriate, and emits `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` with per-workspace counts.

**Vendor Disqualification Record.** The first-class entity materializing the §25.3 / Summary C.118 disqualification workflow. Supports three severities: `soft` (workspace-local), `account_level` (buyer Org's Workspaces, forward-looking 12 months), `global_ban` (Ops-imposed across the platform). Binds the buyer-private `rationale_internal` to the vendor-visible `notification_body_to_vendor` with explicit asymmetric-visibility fields; carries cascade status, appeal workflow, and reversal rules. See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Cascade.** The set of downstream effects triggered by a Vendor Disqualification Record write: Target Account transition, Bid Workspace transition, response locking, Q&A orphaning, Scoring-matrix exclusion (where applicable), Console Bridge Event emission, Seller Signal suppression, EOI auto-rejection (account_level), Marketplace Listing hiding and page 410 (global_ban). Completion observable via `cascade_status`. Soft SLA: 10s. Account-level SLA: 60s (fan-out). See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Reversal.** The reverse of the cascade, executed when a disqualification is overturned on appeal, reversed by the Workspace Owner within 72 hours (soft only), or reversed by Ops leadership (global_ban). Preserves historical Selection Reports (no rewrite); post-Phase-12 reversals annotate rather than re-open Scoring. See §4.7.2.

**Rationale Asymmetry.** The deliberate separation between buyer-private `rationale_internal` (NEVER carried across the firewall) and vendor-visible `notification_body_to_vendor` (always carried) on Vendor Disqualification Records. Enforced by the Console Bridge Event redaction validator for kind `disqualification_issued`. See §4.7.2.

**Notification Style (Disqualification).** The `notification_style` enum on Vendor Disqualification Records: `neutral_no_rationale` (default; no rationale shared), `rationale_shared_with_vendor` (buyer explicit opt-in + Ops approval; not permitted for global_ban), `silent_no_vendor_notification` (global_ban Ops-covert investigations). See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Appeal Window.** The deadline for a Seller Org to appeal a Vendor Disqualification Record: `not_offered` for `soft`, 14 days for `account_level`, 30 days for `global_ban`. Global ban overturn requires Ops leadership dual sign-off. See §4.7.2.

**Ops Compliance Admin Role.** The Ops Console role empowered to reverse Vendor Disqualification Records beyond the 72-hour Workspace Owner window and to co-sign `global_ban` severity transitions with an Ops leadership user. Appendix J.

**Ops Content Admin Role.** The Ops Console role empowered to take `seller_banned` closure dispositions on Marketplace Abuse Reports. `org_level_all_consoles` bans require dual sign-off by two `ops_content_admin` users. Appendix J.

**Superseded by Global Ban.** The annotation applied to existing soft Vendor Disqualification Records when a global ban on the same seller takes effect. Existing records remain in place for audit integrity; `superseded_by_global_ban=true` flags them; surfaces reduce to Ops-only. See §4.7.2.

### Terms Introduced in §4.8 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 4)

**AIOperation.** The canonical, immutable, single-row record of one billable AI invocation. Org-scoped, console-tagged, append-only after settlement. Joins the four billing facts: what was billed (capability, model_tier, cost basis), who consumed it (actor + console + workspace), against which wallet, locked at which FX rate. Settlement state machine: `pending → accepted | rejected | auto_accepted → contested → reversed`. Per Summary C.75 the single billing unit across the platform. See §4.8.1.

**CapabilityRegistryEntry.** The Ops-Console-managed authoritative list of every capability that can produce an AIOperation. Supersedes the v6.0.0 hardcoded "21 capabilities" reference. State machine: `alpha → beta → active → deprecated → retired`. Per Summary C.76. See §4.8.2.

**AIWallet.** The Org-scoped, console-pooled value-dollar account that customer-billed AIOperations draw against. One row per Org. Pooled across both buyer and seller consoles per Pricing Strategy §11. State machine includes `active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `payment_failed_grace`, `suspended`, `closed`. See §4.8.3.

**OutcomeContract.** The per-capability versioned, Ops-managed signal contract that drives AIOperation acceptance/rejection resolution. Versioned: contract changes do NOT retroactively reclassify settled operations; pending operations resolve under the contract version active at AIOperation write. Per Pricing Strategy §10. See §4.8.4.

**ContestRecord.** The per-AIOperation, customer-initiated dispute record. Filed by `billing_admin` within the 14-day contest window per Summary C.78. State machine: `open → in_review → approved | rejected | escalated`; `withdrawn` from `open`. Auto-filed by the system when a late outcome signal arrives after auto-accept. See §4.8.5.

**CostBaseRecalculationLog.** The per-run audit record of the nightly job that re-derives `cost_base_cents` from actual Anthropic billing, Convex compute attribution, and external-provider billing. Drift severity drives auto-applied vs Ops-Finance-approval routing per Summary C.77. Margin-floor breach (margin < 88%) requires explicit override. See §4.8.6.

**FreeAllowanceCounter.** The per-Org-per-capability counter implementing Summary C.80: 10 free operations per signup as a PLG lever. Default lifetime quota; per-period reset configurable per capability. Atomic decrement-and-return prevents double-spend. AIOperation rows consumed against this counter set `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`. See §4.8.7.

**CommittedSpendContract.** The Enterprise annual AI value-dollar commit per Summary C.81. Discount bands derived from `commit_value_dollars`: 10% at $25K, 15% at $50K, 20% at $100K, 25% at $250K+. Floor: $12K/yr per Pricing Strategy §6. AIOperations preferentially burn down the commit pool before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`. See §4.8.8.

**PricingTableVersion.** The publish-time snapshot that backs the Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Immutable once published; customers can pin a version for forecasting reproducibility but AIOperation pricing always uses the current published version. `breaking_change_flag=true` requires 30-day-advance customer notification. See §4.8.9.

**DowngradeExcessDataBucket.** The per-Org-per-data-class record of entities preserved in read-only mode for 90 days after a plan downgrade per Summary C.85. State machine: `active_preservation → notice_sent_d60 → notice_sent_d80 → archive_pending → archived`; `restored` reachable from any prior state when customer upgrades back. Hard-archive at preservation_until; cold-storage retention 7 years. See §4.8.10.

**BillingSeatSnapshot.** The periodic point-in-time count of active seats per Org per console for analytics, plan-gate enforcement, and Stripe invoice line-item context per Summary C.86. Sourcera does NOT charge per seat; this snapshot is reporting-only. Guests and API-only identities excluded. Snapshots immutable post-creation. See §4.8.11.

**Value Price.** The customer-facing price of an AIOperation when the Outcome Resolver fires `accepted` or `auto_accepted`. Default formula: `cost_base_cents × value_multiplier` (default `value_multiplier = 10.000`); floor `min_value_price_cents` from CapabilityRegistryEntry. Locked at AIOperation write time.

**Cost Price.** The customer-facing price of an AIOperation when the Outcome Resolver fires `rejected`. Default formula: `cost_base_cents × cost_multiplier` (default `cost_multiplier = 1.050`); floor `min_cost_price_cents`. Bills at near-cost so rejected outputs are never profitable per Pricing Strategy §2.4 / §2.6. Margin-protection mechanism.

**Cost Base.** The per-capability per-model-tier underlying cost in integer USD cents, re-derived nightly by the cost_base recalc job from actual Anthropic billing + Convex compute + external-provider billing. The customer never sees `cost_base` directly; they see `value_price` and `cost_price` denominated in stable value-dollars per Pricing Strategy §11.

**FX-Locking.** The mechanism by which an AIOperation's billing-currency exchange rate is locked at write time to the daily Treasury rate for `(legal_entity, billing_currency)`. Preserved through `contested` and `reversed` so a reversal credit issues at the same FX rate as the original charge. Per Summary C.84.

**Residency-Locked Invoicing.** The mechanism by which the legal entity that issues the customer's invoice is determined deterministically from the Org's `data_residency_region`: `us → sourcera_us_llc`, `eu → sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `apac → sourcera_apac_pte`, `uk → sourcera_uk_ltd`. Locked on AIWallet at first creation; locked on AIOperation at write. Per Summary C.84.

**Settlement Freeze.** The state of an AIOperation in which all writes other than DSAR redaction are rejected with `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` (HTTP 422). Reached when `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, rejected, auto_accepted, reversed}` AND `contest_window_at < now`. Preserves financial-record integrity.

**Contest Window.** The 14-day (default; capability-overridable per OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days`) period after `settlement_at` during which a customer's `billing_admin` may file a ContestRecord against an AIOperation. Per Summary C.78.

**Outcome Resolver.** The system component responsible for transitioning AIOperations from `pending` to `accepted` / `rejected` / `auto_accepted` based on the OutcomeContract for the operation's capability. Operates per AIOperation. Default-on-timeout is `rejected` per Pricing Strategy §6 unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`.

**Auto-Accept Timer.** The `auto_accept_after_seconds` countdown on a `pending` AIOperation; on expiry without an outcome signal, the operation transitions to `auto_accepted` and bills at value price. Distinct from `accepted` for product-quality dashboards (high `auto_accepted` rate is a quality signal).

**Wallet Hold.** The soft reservation of `value_price_cents` from the wallet at AIOperation write time, ensuring the funds are available for the eventual settlement charge. On settlement, the hold is converted to a charge (if accepted/auto_accepted) or partially released (if rejected, with `cost_price_cents` charged).

**Soft Credit.** The temporary wallet credit applied when a ContestRecord is filed against an `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation. Reversed if the contest is rejected; finalized as a permanent credit if approved.

**Drift Severity.** The categorical magnitude of the per-capability cost_base change observed by the nightly recalc job: `normal` (≤5%), `warning_5_10` (5–10%), `alert_10_25` (10–25%), `critical_gt_25` (>25%). Drives auto-apply vs explicit Ops Finance approval routing per Summary C.77.

**Margin Floor Breach.** A flag on a CostBaseRecalculationLog row indicating the proposed new value price would yield gross margin below 88% (per Pricing Strategy §2.6). Never auto-applied; requires explicit Ops Finance override or capability deprecation.

**Free Allowance.** The per-Org-per-capability default-10 free operations granted on signup as the primary PLG lever per Summary C.80 / Pricing Strategy §3 / Seller §14. Exhaustion surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the ROI of the operations already run.

**Committed Spend Pool.** The Enterprise pre-paid commit balance that AIOperations preferentially burn down before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`. Tracked via `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` on AIWallet, reconciled nightly against CommittedSpendContract.

**Discount Band.** The categorical Enterprise commit-volume discount per Summary C.81: `none`, `band_25k_10pct`, `band_50k_15pct`, `band_100k_20pct`, `band_250k_25pct`. Derived deterministically from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; locked.

**Public Pricing API.** The publicly-readable rate-card endpoint at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Backed by PricingTableVersion. Customers can forecast spend programmatically; published payload includes capabilities, value/cost prices, currencies, plan tiers, free allowances, deprecation banners.

**Breaking Pricing Change.** A PricingTableVersion change involving a customer-visible price increase or capability removal. Requires 30-day-advance customer notification per Pricing Strategy §11; publish rejected with HTTP 422 if `customer_notification_sent_at < effective_at - 30 days`.

**Downgrade Excess Preservation.** The 90-day read-only preservation period per Summary C.85 during which entities exceeding the new plan's caps remain accessible (read-only) to the customer. After preservation, hard-archived to cold storage; restorable for up to 90 days post-archive.

**Restoration Partial.** The case in which a customer upgrades back from a downgrade but to a tier insufficient to re-cover all preserved entities. The bucket flags `restoration_partial=true`; the user explicitly selects which entities to restore; remaining entities stay in the bucket.

**Billing Admin Role.** A new Org-scoped role authored in Phase 4 (orthogonal to `org_admin`): permissions are confined to the billing surface — read AIWallet, file ContestRecord, view BillingSeatSnapshot, configure auto-topup, view Billing Ledger across both consoles. No data access to workspaces or marketplace surfaces. Authored as the role gate for the Pricing Strategy §6 / §7 admin actions.

**Ops Finance Admin Role.** The Ops Console role with full read/write across the §4.8 entities for financial review, contest decisions, cost-base approvals, commit-contract management, pricing-table publication, and downgrade restorations.

**Ops Capability Admin Role.** The Ops Console role with CRUD authority on CapabilityRegistryEntry and OutcomeContract — the only role that may add new capabilities to the platform's billable surface.

**Cost Center.** The accounting attribution on every AIOperation: `customer_billed` charges hit the wallet; `sourcera_owned` and `platform_marketing` are recorded for COGS without wallet impact. Drives the Marketplace-content (M9–M13) Sourcera-funded AI operations that produce public pages without customer billing.

**Provenance Hash.** The 64-char sha256 hex over `(capability_id, prompt_template_version, input_content_hash, model_id, cost_base_version_id, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked)` on AIOperation. Used by ContestRecord to assert a specific operation; immutable after AIOperation write.

**Effective Charge.** The final wallet charge for an AIOperation after settlement. Equals `value_price_cents` for `accepted`/`auto_accepted`, `cost_price_cents` for `rejected`, and `0` for `reversed`. Frozen at settlement.

**Auto-Filed Contest.** A ContestRecord automatically generated by the system (not by a user) when a late `rejected` outcome signal arrives after an AIOperation has already auto-accepted. Reason code `auto_filed_late_signal`; routes to Ops Finance for review. Customer-trust + margin-protection mechanism: catches outcome-resolver bugs without requiring the customer to notice.

---

**End of Sourcera Master Specification v6.0.0**
